cards.summary: The attempt plan's core (#148, ADR 0059): what the brewer of an attempt's step asks for, as the plan the claude runner takes (ADR 0047) and the limits the driver gives the attempt. Pure: attempt-plans.ts reads the state, the inputs and the files.
cards.comments: The attempt plan's core (#148, ADR 0059): what the brewer of an attempt's step asks for, as the plan the claude runner takes (ADR 0047) and the limits the driver gives the attempt. Pure: attempt-plans.ts reads the state, the inputs and the files. Where the text of an input is read from: the order's issue, a file inside `root`, or nowhere, since the brewer's loader read it (a lens, ADR 0098). An input of the brewer, where it comes from, and where its text is read. What one attempt's plan is made from. The brewer file's body. The attempt's worktree. The brewer's inputs with their text, in its order. The repository's toolchain rules (`foedrum.jsonc`, ADR 0023). Whether the isolation level relies on Claude Code's sandbox (ADR 0010). Where the driver's environment moves the logins the sandbox hides (ADR 0160). The id of the new session, which the driver chose and recorded (ADR 0047, ADR 0116). Why it resumes that session, if it does: after a failure, or after a human answered its questions. Its prompt is then a short one, since the session holds the instructions and the inputs, with only the answers as an input (ADR 0117, ADR 0118). After a turn overrun: the copy of the out doc the run before left, which the runner puts back in a worktree that lost it (ADR 0175). For a later round of a lens step that reviews a diff, what it is told (ADR 0190). Whether its inputs hold the earlier rounds' findings, which the fixed text explains (ADR 0191). On a step of several lenses together, its lenses in its order, which the fixed text names (ADR 0220). An interactive step's: the recipe's first message to its session (ADR 0222). The limits the runner enforces for an attempt of `brewer` in a worktree that started at `start`: a brewer that produces commits needs one after it for a `done` (ADR 0074). A Taster's out doc is read with its findings and verdict, and on a `blocking` step a `changes` verdict blocks it by findings (ADR 0161). Each finding that names a lens names one of the step's `lenses`, and on a step of several together each finding names one (ADR 0220). A recipe choice's question offers only the step's `choices` (ADR 0232). A Gauger a failed red proof of its step sent back (`sentBack`) may name its tests without a commit (ADR 0258). A pullRequest brewer's out doc is read with its sections (ADR 0167), a Finer's with its changes (ADR 0166), a Gauger's with its tests (ADR 0170), a plan with its sub-orders (ADR 0233), a recipe choice with its one question (ADR 0232); every other out doc against the contract's schema. The model id behind the brewer's alias; throws when models.jsonc has none. Blind tasting swaps the alias of a brewer in models.jsonc (brewers-and-recipes §5). Own entries only: a name such as "constructor" is a property of every object. The model family the brewer runs on, read as its attempt runs it, a blind-tasting swap included; undefined when it cannot be told, also when models.jsonc has no model for its alias (ADR 0215). Its plan fails the attempt with the reason; until then every limit holds it. The git rules `git.commit: true` grants (ADR 0074): fixed subcommands that never push (ADR 0062), in Bash; none for any other brewer. `git diff --no-index` and `git log --output` reach any file: a brewer names them itself. The shell commands `rules` allow, once each, in the order first named: each Bash rule's command without its trailing star (#222); none when one of them allows any program. PowerShell rules are left out: the runner's sessions have no PowerShell tool (ADR 0074). The tool of each rule, once each, in the order first named. The latest attempt of `stepId` in `batch` that succeeded, with the worktree it ran in. A resumed attempt ran in the worktree of the session it continues (ADR 0117). The Brewery's repositories and their bases, and the one an attempt's worktree holds. The text of an input `from: "repositories"` (ADR 0234): one line per repository, its own marked. Where each of `inputs` is read from, leaving out those of a step the batch skipped (ADR 0064); throws when a step it names has no out doc yet. A lens input's text is in `lenses`, the lenses the loader found for the brewer (ADR 0098); a repositories input's in `brewery` (ADR 0234), and the recipes input's in `choices`, the Brewery's recipes but those that choose one (ADR 0232). A step's lenses together are one input that names each (ADR 0220). The loader refuses a brewer whose lens it did not find. Each lens file as it is, a blank line apart. `file:<path>`: a relative path with `/`, checked by the brewer's schema. The answers a human gave to the questions of `stepId`, every round in order, as the in-doc of its next attempt, which starts a new session (ADR 0006); or only the latest round's, for an attempt that resumes the session that holds the rounds before (ADR 0118). None when nobody answered. Where the change a Taster's step that reviews a diff is given starts (ADR 0161): the commit `batch` started at in `repo`; none before any attempt recorded one. The most of a change input a prompt holds, in UTF-8 bytes (ADR 0161). The regression tests a step of the batch named (ADR 0170): model text, untrusted. The change input of a Taster that reviews a diff (ADR 0161): the commits after `since`, the regression tests the batch's steps named (ADR 0170), and the commits' diff, as git printed it, held to its limit. The engine reads them, so the Taster runs no git; the lists come before the diff, which the limit cuts. The latest round of a lens step before attempt `ref` that reviewed (ADR 0190, ADR 0196): the commit its worktree started at, or `unfound` when nothing records one. None for a first round: a retry, or an attempt after an answer, belongs to the round of the attempt it follows, so it reviews what that round reviews. A failed, cancelled or lost attempt reviewed nothing: the one before it may have (ADR 0196). The round before a later one, as `roundBefore` finds it. cards.summary: The attempt plans' shell (#148, ADR 0059): for an attempt the driver started, it finds the brewer of its step in the batch's recipe, reads the brewer's inputs and makes the settings file's folder, then plans the attempt through attempt-plan.ts, which decides, in the session the driver recorded (ADR 0116).
cards.comments: The attempt plans' shell (#148, ADR 0059): for an attempt the driver started, it finds the brewer of its step in the batch's recipe, reads the brewer's inputs and makes the settings file's folder, then plans the attempt through attempt-plan.ts, which decides, in the session the driver recorded (ADR 0116). The folded state: the driver's, which has recorded the attempt's start and worktree. The brewers of the recipes' steps (`loadRecipes`). The red proofs of the recipes' check steps (`loadRecipes`): which step each proves (ADR 0258). The toolchain rules of a repository (`foedrum.jsonc`, ADR 0023). A repository's setup (`foedrum.jsonc`), run before every attempt's brewer (ADR 0163). Whether the isolation level relies on Claude Code's sandbox (ADR 0010). Where the driver's environment moves the logins the sandbox hides (ADR 0160). The clone a repository's attempt worktrees are added to: the user's, or the managed one. The Brewery's repositories and the base each attempt starts from (`origin/<base>`): a plan's paths are checked in each once it is done (ADR 0233). Fetches a repository's clone through its worktree manager, when a plan's check finds no ref of its base there (ADR 0233). The Brewery's work root (ADR 0037). The brewer's minimal base environment and the runner's forced variables (ADR 0028). Default this process's. The text of an order's issue, untrusted. Reads the change a Taster that reviews a diff is given, in its worktree (ADR 0161); a plan that needs it fails without it. The Brewery's house-yeast rule files, read with its files, and where a repository's own rules are kept (`foedrum.jsonc`, ADR 0018): a brewer that asks for house yeast gets those that match its change (ADR 0169). Default the file system's: `readOutDocFile` and a recursive `mkdir`. The plan of an attempt the driver started; rejects when it cannot be made. The limits of an attempt, from the brewer of its step in its batch's recipe. The out doc of the brewer of a step in its batch's recipe; undefined without one (ADR 0081). The tools that run a command: a brewer without one cannot use an install (ADR 0163). The attempt `ref` as the driver recorded its start; undefined before. The worktree the attempt runs in, and the attempt that made it: the one the driver recorded when it started the attempt, or for a resumed attempt with none of its own, the worktree of the session it continues (ADR 0117); none before it started. A resumed attempt runs where the driver recreated that worktree (ADR 0117). What an attempt without a brewer is limited to: the plan then fails it, before it runs. The brewer of a step in the recipe its batch brews; undefined without one. The text of one input, untrusted. A lens's text was read, and held to the limit, when the brewer loaded (ADR 0098). Anyone who can file an issue writes its body: it gets the limit of an input file. git in the clone of `repo`, never by discovery in a worktree, with no hook, external diff or textconv a brewer could have planted there (ADR 0029, ADR 0096, ADR 0137): its stdout, or an error that starts with `why` and names the call. With `keepCut`, the start of an output git was stopped for past its limit. Each repository of the Brewery with the commit a plan's paths in it are checked at (ADR 0233): the attempt's own at the commit its worktree started at, another at its base as its clone has it. A base the clone has no ref of is fetched once, through its worktree manager; one that still cannot be read is carried with why, which blocks only a plan that names its repository. No ref of it yet: an attempt in that repository fetches, and none may have run. The change a Taster that reviews a diff is given (ADR 0161): the commits from `since` to `head`, the commit its worktree started at, and their diff. Read in the repository's clone, never by discovery in the worktree, with no hook, external diff or textconv a brewer could have planted there (ADR 0029, ADR 0096, ADR 0137). A diff past git's output limit keeps its start, which the input cuts anyway. The first parents only: never the commits a merge of the base brought in (ADR 0164). Why commit `ancestor` is not on the line to `head` in the clone of `repo`: `off` when git says it is not, or that git failed; undefined when it is. Exit 1 alone says it is not an ancestor; any other end is git's failure (#506). For a later round of a lens step that reviews a diff (ADR 0190): the change from the commit the round before reviewed to `worktree`'s, read as the change is, and what the round is told. Never a range that is not the round's own: none when that commit is not on the line to HEAD, as after a rewind, or when the base `merged` since would bring what it added (ADR 0164). The change input's text without regression tests, under a name of its own. For a later round of a lens step (ADR 0191): the earlier rounds' findings with their dispositions, a blocked round's read from the out doc in its worktree as the route input reads it (ADR 0128); none for a first round. An out doc that cannot be read is not an error: its round says so. The house-yeast rules for an attempt with `stepLenses` in `repo`, whose change runs from `since` to `head` (ADR 0169): the rules each lens would get apart, each once (ADR 0220): the Brewery's, and the repository's, from the Brewery or with git in the clone at `since`, so the batch's own commits never add or remove one. The files the change touched are read in the clone too; with no `since`, it touched none. Before an attempt recorded where the batch started, nothing changed, and no commit holds the repository's own rules. The rule files of `.foedrum/house-yeast/` at commit `at`, read with `read` (ADR 0169). One byte past the limit, and kept when git is stopped there, so the check below says so. The rules are one input's worth of text, as a file input is (ADR 0059). cards.summary: The attempt settings files go with their batch's worktrees (ADR 0063): `claude` reads its settings once, when it starts, so a batch that ended needs none of its files any more.
cards.comments: The attempt settings files go with their batch's worktrees (ADR 0063): `claude` reads its settings once, when it starts, so a batch that ended needs none of its files any more. The batch folders under `root`; none when no attempt wrote settings yet. Removes the settings folders under `<workRoot>/attempt-settings` that no live batch claims: the one of `scope.batchId` when it has ended, or every ended and unknown batch's at a repair.

cards.summary: Writing an attempt's `claude --settings` file (ADR 0046): always from an AttemptSettings that passed its schema, so the file is never one claude would drop.
cards.comments: Writing an attempt's `claude --settings` file (ADR 0046): always from an AttemptSettings that passed its schema, so the file is never one claude would drop. The brewer's tools.allow with the repository's toolchain commands (ADR 0023). The brewer's tools.deny. Whether the isolation level relies on Claude Code's sandbox (ADR 0010). Where the driver's environment moves the logins the sandbox hides (ADR 0160). The driver's home and PATH, whose toolchain folders sandboxed commands may read (ADR 0162). The variables of `env` among `names` that are set. The variables of the driver's environment the toolchain's folders are found from (ADR 0162). The variables of `env` the toolchain's folders are found from. The variables that move a login out of the paths `sandboxCredentials` names (ADR 0160). The variables of `env` that move a login. The logins the variables move, on the sandboxed level's POSIX paths: gh's directory (gh's `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gh`), git's credential store under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and Claude Code's `.credentials.json` under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. A relative or empty value names no one place and adds nothing. ADR 0087's credentials, with the logins the variables move, each path once. Homebrew's prefix on Linux: under `/home`, a user root the block denies, whoever's home it is. The layouts whose PATH folder under the home links into an install prefix around it: the folder, `*` for any one name, and how many of its names the prefix keeps (ADR 0162). nvm: node, npm and npx, which link into the version's lib/node_modules, and global packages. /bin', 4], // Volta: its shims, and the tools they run from ~/.volta/tools. ['.volta/bin', 1], // asdf: its shims, asdf itself, and the versions under ~/.asdf/installs the shims run. ['.asdf/shims', 1], ['.asdf/bin', 1], ]; /** How many names of a folder under the home the folder to re-open keeps: all but a layout's. `path` as one absolute folder: normalized, no trailing slash; '' for the root or a relative one. Whether `path` is `dir` or lies inside it, in any case: macOS's default file system ignores it. The folders of the driver's toolchain that sandboxed commands may read under the block (ADR 0162): Homebrew's prefix on Linux, and each PATH folder under the home, as a layout's prefix or as it is, never its parent. Not a folder with a glob character, which a sandbox path reads as a wildcard, nor one at, inside or around a hidden login, since the narrower read rule wins. In the PATH folders' form, so a moved login's trailing slash still matches. npm's configuration files anywhere in a re-opened folder: a prefix's global `etc/npmrc` and the npm package's builtin `npmrc` can hold the login ADR 0087 hides as `~/.npmrc` (review of #437). A deny holds inside a wider allow, a wildcard one too. The settings as the schema reads them; throws with every problem when it does not. The settings of an attempt: its rules, each bare file tool scoped to the worktree (ADR 0093), the rules every attempt denies, and the sandbox. `--tools` still decides which tools exist. ADR 0160: sandboxed commands lose the home directory and the other user roots. ADR 0151: no Co-Authored-By trailer, pull request footer or session URL from the tool. ADR 0042: by default a sandbox that cannot start lets commands run unsandboxed. ADR 0087: by default it runs every sandboxed command whatever the allow rules say, and lets it read the machine's credentials, wherever a variable moved them (ADR 0160). ADR 0162: the block's command part takes a toolchain under the home, whose folders `allowRead` re-opens. Writes the settings as JSON once they pass the schema; throws, writing nothing, otherwise.

cards.summary: The `claude` command line of a brewer attempt (ADR 0042, ADR 0046). The prompt is not part of it: it goes on stdin, so the line stays short enough for the Job Object helper (ADR 0039).
cards.comments: The `claude` command line of a brewer attempt (ADR 0042, ADR 0046). The prompt is not part of it: it goes on stdin, so the line stays short enough for the Job Object helper (ADR 0039). A session the attempt starts with the id the runner chose, or one it resumes. The model id behind the brewer's alias (models.jsonc). The attempt's settings file, written by the runner. The built-in tools the brewer may use; no other tool exists in its session. A system prompt file appended to Claude Code's own. Whether `id` is a session id claude takes: a UUID. The values come from validated brewers and the runner itself, so a bad one is a defect; it must never reach cmd.exe for npm's claude.cmd (ADR 0031) or read as an option. An attempt's session as an engineer opens it (ADR 0126): its model and guards, interactive. The attempt's system prompt file (ADR 0183). The arguments of an interactive `claude` that resumes an attempt's session. No print-mode flag and no permission mode: the engineer answers what the settings do not allow. A new interactive session of an interactive step (ADR 0222): resume's guards, a first message. The engine's fixed line that points the session at its prompt file. The arguments of an interactive `claude` that opens an interactive step's new session. One line of the engine's own, never an option: it is the session's first message. First, so no option that takes several values reads it as one of them. The checks every command line's values pass. The engine's fixed rules, appended to claude's own system prompt (ADR 0183). The guards of an attempt's session, however it runs. No user, project or local settings file: only --settings, which is the runner's (ADR 0046). The arguments of `claude` for one attempt.

cards.summary: The first check of an attempt's stream (ADR 0046): claude's init event must show the session the runner asked for before anything else of the stream is read. claude drops a settings file silently, and settings of the user could widen a brewer, so what it set up is checked, not trusted. A mismatch is an environment failure, never retried.
cards.comments: The first check of an attempt's stream (ADR 0046): claude's init event must show the session the runner asked for before anything else of the stream is read. claude drops a settings file silently, and settings of the user could widen a brewer, so what it set up is checked, not trusted. A mismatch is an environment failure, never retried. What the runner asked claude for. The built-in tools passed with --tools. What the runner records of a session that matches. The full model id. What claude loaded may come from an untrusted repository, and the reason ends in a summary a human reads: a few names, each cut short, and how many more. One entry as a short quoted name: a string itself, an object by its name. Whether an init event (the stream's first event, parsed) shows the session that was asked. Fail closed: what cannot be read cannot be shown to match. MCP tools included: the brewer has no MCP server, so an mcp__ tool is one too many.

cards.summary: The real brewer runner (ADR 0003, ADR 0028, ADR 0047): runs an attempt as one `claude` process with the runner's own settings file, its prompt on stdin, inside a Job Object on Windows, and reads its stream line by line. What it saw goes through settleAttempt, as with the fake.
cards.comments: The real brewer runner (ADR 0003, ADR 0028, ADR 0047): runs an attempt as one `claude` process with the runner's own settings file, its prompt on stdin, inside a Job Object on Windows, and reads its stream line by line. What it saw goes through settleAttempt, as with the fake. Everything one attempt needs, prepared by the engine (its worktree, prompt and session). The attempt's worktree; the out doc's path is relative to it. The brewer's environment (buildBrewerEnv, ADR 0028). Only a prompt from assembleBrewerPrompt (ADR 0041); it goes on stdin. Where the runner writes the attempt's settings file. The engine's fixed rules, which the runner writes to their file and passes with `--append-system-prompt-file` (ADR 0183); every plan `planAttempt` makes has them. For a brewer that produces commits: the clone its worktree was added to and the attempt's branch, where its commits are counted, never what its worktree says (ADR 0074). The repository's setup: the runner runs it in the worktree before claude starts, in the checks' environment, killed before the attempt's deadline (ADR 0163). The house-yeast rules the plan gave the brewer, which its end records (ADR 0169). For a brewer whose out doc is a plan: each repository of the Brewery, its clone and the commit the plan's paths in it are checked at once it is done (ADR 0233). For a resumed run after a turn overrun: the copy of the out doc the run before left. The runner keeps the out doc in the worktree, or puts this copy back there (ADR 0175). An interactive step's (ADR 0222): the file the runner writes the prompt to, and claude's first message, which points the session at it. An out doc as the runner found it. The `claude` program to start. The process runner a repository's setup runs through: the check sandbox, network kept (ADR 0158). A plan with a setup and no runner for it is blocked on its environment. Writes the attempt's system prompt file (ADR 0183). Reads the out doc only inside `root`, the worktree. Removes the out doc a run before left, only inside `root`, the worktree, before a run that resumes its session there (ADR 0118); throws when it cannot. Puts the copy of the out doc a run that ran out of turns left back in `root`, the worktree, when it has none (ADR 0175); throws when it cannot. Keeps the copy of the out doc of an attempt that ran out of turns (ADR 0175). Resolves after `ms`, or at once when `signal` aborts. The commits on the attempt's branch in its clone after the limits' `commitsSince` (ADR 0074). Scans a done attempt's commits after the limits' `commitsSince` for secrets, as the push does (ADR 0187). Reads which paths of a done plan exist at a commit in a repository's clone (ADR 0233). One stream line, an event, may hold a whole file the brewer read: well above any file it reads, well below what the engine can hold (ADR 0046). The out doc's text reaches the event log (ADR 0028). The ending settleAttempt gives the facts, for a `done` with commits once the push's scan read them on the attempt's branch in the clone (ADR 0187); any other ending with no git run. stderr is the CLI's, but it may quote what the brewer wrote: a reason quotes one line of it, cut as the stream's are. Writes an attempt's system prompt file (ADR 0183). Removes the out doc `file` a run before left in `root`, the worktree, so a resumed run is read by what it writes itself (ADR 0118); nothing when there is none. Throws when it cannot. A folder is no out doc, and the read after the run says so. A linked folder on its path (a junction needs no privilege on Windows), or `..`, could lead out of the worktree; a link in its place goes itself, never the file it points at. Writes `copy`, the out doc a run that ran out of turns left, to `file` in `root`, the worktree, when the worktree has none: it was recreated (ADR 0175). Nothing when there is no copy. A folder git does not track is not in a recreated worktree: the session resumes without it. As clearOutDocFile: a linked folder on its path, or `..`, could lead out of the worktree. A new file only: `wx` neither follows a link put in its place nor overwrites one. How the process ended, from what the stream process answered. A crash or the OOM killer on macOS and Linux: it ran, so it is retried. Why the session is not what was asked: the stream's reason, or arguments claude refused, which it says on stderr before it writes any event (ADR 0042). Past 255 it is a Windows crash status (NTSTATUS), which claude never exits with: a crash. Resolves after `ms`, or at once when `signal` aborts or had aborted. A stop that came before the wait began costs no wait (review of #136). How long the runner waits before it starts claude once more after a passing failure. What claude says on stderr when it refuses for a cause the next start meets again: its arguments, its session id, its login (ADR 0042, #134). A session id a start that wrote its stream has taken (review of #136, claude 2.1.301). Whether claude failed before its first line for a cause it does not name as lasting. The facts of a process that never ran. The reading of a plan's setup, run in its worktree `cwd` through `through`; read as unstarted when the runner has no process runner for it (ADR 0163). As a setup that could not start: the reason is the runner's, not the repository's. The commits on the attempt's branch in the clone the plan names, after `since`, counted by `count` (ADR 0074); none without a start. Readies the out doc `outDoc` in the plan's worktree for a session that resumes or opens there: a session is read by the out doc it writes, never the one the run before left, such as its needs_input (ADR 0118); after a turn overrun that out doc stays, or its copy comes back, since it is the work the session finishes (ADR 0175). A brewer runner over the given stream process and files; unit tests pass fakes. cards.summary: Reading claude's stream-json (ADR 0042, ADR 0046, ADR 0047): one stdout line at a time, the init check first, then the facts settleAttempt decides on and the progress the stall watchdog reads. Pure: the runner hands it each line with the time it came.
cards.comments: Reading claude's stream-json (ADR 0042, ADR 0046, ADR 0047): one stdout line at a time, the init check first, then the facts settleAttempt decides on and the progress the stall watchdog reads. Pure: the runner hands it each line with the time it came. What the runner asked for, and when it stops the attempt itself. Stops the attempt at the denial that reaches it. Whether claude resumes the session rather than start it (ADR 0117). The attempt's worktree, which a file path shown for display is made relative to (ADR 0174). What the stream showed, for settleAttempt. The session claude set up, once its init matched what was asked. The result's tokens. How many lines came, empty ones included. Reads one stdout line that came at `now`; `stop` when the runner must stop the attempt. What the attempt took so far: complete once the result was read (ADR 0172). For the stall watchdog: when the brewer last wrote a file or committed, and turns since. The stream is untrusted and may be huge: what a reason quotes of it is cut short. The tools that write a file; a shell command counts only when it commits. The most models a receipt names: a run uses one or two. A word of a refused command's prefix: plain, and short. The first one or two words of a shell command, as far as they are plain words, without any that looks like a secret (ADR 0088, ADR 0172); none when its first word is not plain. The command is model output: only its start is read, and nothing else of it is kept. The input key that holds the path a file tool works on. The one word the live line shows of a file tool's path (ADR 0174): the path relative to the worktree with `/` separators, `outside` when it leaves it (a lexical test, no file is read), or `(left out)` when it holds a secret. The latest tool call as the live line shows it: its name and, for some tools, one safe word. Whether a shell command runs `git … commit`: `commit` after `git` within one command between separators. The command is model output, so each test is linear (review of #133). The words of each simple command, split at `;`, `&`, `|` and line ends outside quotes, a quoted word as one word without its quotes (review of #136). One linear pass. git's global options that take the next word as their value (unless given with `=`). Whether one simple command is `git … commit`: after variables, git itself (by any path, with or without `.exe`), then its global options, the first word is `commit` (#134). Errors of a failed call before the first reply that the next attempt would meet again: the environment. A rate limit, an overloaded or failing server, or an unknown error may pass. A run-out usage window, only in the forms Claude Code's error reference gives (ADR 0091): the whole text, one line, such as `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am`. The pattern only matches one of the four limits and a reset. What `read` finds first in an error result's `result` or one of its `errors`. A spend limit, only in the forms the error reference gives (ADR 0129): the whole text, one line, one of the documented limits, then nothing or ` · ` and how to raise it, which varies with the plan. A rest that names a reset is a plan window, which comes back by itself: not this. The pattern only matches one of the documented limits. Why a result reported an error: its terminal reason, then what it said. The text of a message claude made up for a failed call. A reader for one attempt's stream, which started at `startedAt`. Whether the model has replied: an error before that is the environment's (#11, item 4). Turns: the main thread's messages by id while it runs, the result's num_turns at the end. Progress: the calls that write, and when one last came back without an error. The receipt (ADR 0172): each call's tool and a shell's command prefix, the calls denied, and what the result says the run took. For the live line (ADR 0174): the main thread's latest call, and whether a denial came after it. Other system events can come first (ui_invalidate, with an API key; ADR 0046). A run that ends before its session starts: a missing session to resume, no sandbox. A session it resumes may be gone, which a fresh attempt gets past (ADR 0117). A denied call comes back as an error too: it is counted as a denial. A file tool's call that came back without an error is an edit (ADR 0172). One more denial of `tool`'s family, with the prefix its call was refused, each once. Without a result, what was seen: until the last line read. Its API duration and tokens per model are then the session's (ADR 0042). Every other type, including those claude adds later (ADR 0042).

cards.summary: House-yeast rules (ADR 0015, ADR 0018): reads rule files and selects those whose scope matches a change and a lens, within a token budget (ADR 0122). Pure: /brew-review selects through it (scripts/house-yeast.ts), and in src/ a batch can too (#434).
cards.comments: House-yeast rules (ADR 0015, ADR 0018): reads rule files and selects those whose scope matches a change and a lens, within a token budget (ADR 0122). Pure: /brew-review selects through it (scripts/house-yeast.ts), and in src/ a batch can too (#434). Reads rule files given with `/` paths, as the skill writes them; a rule's id is its file name without `.md`. A language no extension has would never match, and the rule would drop out silently. The files of `git diff --name-status` the change adds, alters or renames (new path); not deleted ones. The files of `git diff --name-status -z` the change adds, alters or renames (new path), as git wrote them, never quoted; not deleted ones (ADR 0169). Each entry is its status, then its path, or for a rename or a copy its old and new paths. A rule with neither globs nor a language: it matches every change, so curation is due (ADR 0015). A rule's lens by its name matches that lens in either folder: diff/<name> or plan/<name>. A lens given without its folder, as /brew-review gives its own, is the diff lens of that name (ADR 0169). Lower comes first: a rule for this lens, then globs, a language alone, the whole repository. Not localeCompare: a locale's collation would make the order, and so the cut, differ by machine. A rule as a lens reads it: its heading and body. An estimate, about four characters a token: a budget of this size needs no tokenizer (ADR 0122). The active rules whose scope matches the change and the lens, in order of priority, within the budget: a rule that would pass what is left is cut, and the next one is tried. A rule file of the Brewery that could not be read, with why. A rule file as it was read, or why it could not be. The rule files `git ls-tree -z <commit> -- .foedrum/house-yeast/` lists: the regular `.md` files directly in the folder, by path and blob id; never a link or a folder (ADR 0169). The text of each of `blobs`, from what `git cat-file --batch` printed for their ids, in order, or why it is not a rule's (ADR 0169); throws when the output does not hold them. Each blob is `<id> blob <size>`, a line feed, its bytes and a line feed: sizes count bytes. The runner decoded them as UTF-8, and a byte that is not became U+FFFD, three bytes, so a blob ends where the next one's header starts, and its size only checks it. The Brewery's rule files by layer (ADR 0169): those directly in `house-yeast/` are the Brewery layer, and for a repository whose rules are kept in the Brewery, those in `house-yeast/<owner>/<name>/` are its repository layer. GitHub's names are not case-sensitive, so neither is the folder of one. A folder that could not be listed is named by its own path, in the layer it holds. The rules one attempt gets: its inputs, and what it records (ADR 0169). The rules of `files`, with those that could not be read among the invalid. A byte that is not UTF-8 was read as U+FFFD, from the file system as from git. The rules of both layers whose scope matches `change`, within `budget`: a repository rule over a Brewery rule of its id (ADR 0018), each selected one as an input named `houseYeast`, and the ids selected and cut and the files left out as invalid, which the attempt records (ADR 0169). A step's lenses together get the rules each would get apart, each once, in their order, and a rule one lens cut and another selected counts as selected (ADR 0220).

cards.summary: The brewer runner of `foedrum resume` on a running batch (ADR 0127) and of `foedrum brew` on a terminal (ADR 0222): an interactive step's attempt opens a new session, and with resume an attempt that resumes a session opens it, as the person's interactive `claude` in the foreground, with the attempt's settings, guards and environment; each ends by the out doc the session wrote, through settleAttempt as every run does. Every other attempt runs headless, as its driver would.
cards.comments: The brewer runner of `foedrum resume` on a running batch (ADR 0127) and of `foedrum brew` on a terminal (ADR 0222): an interactive step's attempt opens a new session, and with resume an attempt that resumes a session opens it, as the person's interactive `claude` in the foreground, with the attempt's settings, guards and environment; each ends by the out doc the session wrote, through settleAttempt as every run does. Every other attempt runs headless, as its driver would. The `claude` program to start. Whether an attempt that resumes a session opens it in the foreground: `foedrum resume`'s, by default; `foedrum brew`'s runs it headless and opens only interactive steps (ADR 0222). The process runner a resumed session's setup runs through before claude opens: the check sandbox, network kept (ADR 0158, ADR 0163). The headless runner of an attempt that starts fresh, given its plan. Runs `program` in the foreground with the terminal's stdio; its exit code. The variables a terminal program reads to draw itself, which claude gets besides the brewer's. How the platform reads a variable's name: in any case on Windows. Writes the attempt's system prompt file (ADR 0183). Writes an interactive step's prompt file (ADR 0222). Reads the out doc only inside `root`, the worktree. Removes the out doc a run before left, only inside `root` (ADR 0118). Puts back the copy of the out doc of a session that ran out of turns (ADR 0175). The commits on the attempt's branch in its clone after the limits' `commitsSince`. Scans a done attempt's commits after the limits' `commitsSince` for secrets, as the push does (ADR 0187). Reads which paths of a done plan exist at a commit in a repository's clone (ADR 0233). Writes a line to the terminal, before claude has it. As the headless runner reads it: the out doc's text reaches the event log (ADR 0028). What the runner saw of a session the engineer ran: its exit, its out doc and its commits. The open sessions, and the headless runners of the fresh attempts, by attempt key. A stop before a fresh attempt's run exists reaches it once it does. A stop reaches the setup before a resumed session, which is the attempt's, not the engineer's (ADR 0163). As a headless run that was stopped: the engine stopped the attempt, so no session opens for it, since nothing the person did there would be read (ADR 0222). By the step: an interactive step's session opens; a resumed one only in resume's runner. The whole prompt, inputs in their nonce tags, which the first message points at. A new interactive session too: its worktree may hold the out doc of an attempt before. The repository's setup first: the driver may have added the worktree again, without its install (ADR 0163). The session is open meanwhile, so its lease is renewed. A stop during a setup that passed all the same. The terminal's own variables under the attempt's environment (ADR 0109's forced variables included), by name as the platform reads it, as for a finished attempt (ADR 0126). Counted on the attempt's branch in the clone, as for every run (ADR 0074). Scanned for secrets on the attempt's branch, and a plan's paths read, as for every run (ADR 0187, ADR 0233). The engineer's session is theirs to end: a stop reaches only a headless run (ADR 0127), the setup before a resumed session (ADR 0163), and an attempt whose session has not opened. An open session always progresses: its lease is renewed, and no stall limit judges a human. The headless runner of a fresh attempt on the real machine, which runs the attempt's setup through `setup` (ADR 0163). The runner on the real machine: files, git and the headless runner of a fresh attempt. The process runner every attempt's setup runs through (ADR 0158, ADR 0163).

cards.summary: Brewer prompt assembly (ADR 0041): the one place where input text enters a brewer's prompt. Every input goes between tags with a fresh random nonce, after the brewer's instructions and the rule that says the tagged text is data. A mitigation, not the security boundary.
cards.comments: Brewer prompt assembly (ADR 0041): the one place where input text enters a brewer's prompt. Every input goes between tags with a fresh random nonce, after the brewer's instructions and the rule that says the tagged text is data. A mitigation, not the security boundary. Where an input's text came from; named in the tag's `source` attribute. A house-yeast rule, with the file it was read from (ADR 0169). A lens's text (ADR 0098): `path` is the Brewery's `lenses/diff/<name>.md` or `lenses/plan/<name>.md` (ADR 0143), or the default's. The lenses of a step that reviews through several together, in its order (ADR 0220). Where the change a Taster reviews starts: the commit its batch started at (ADR 0161). The Brewery's recipes a step that chooses the recipe may offer (ADR 0232). A human's answers to the questions a step asked (ADR 0006: the in-doc of a fresh attempt). What sent a step back along a route: the failed checks or the findings of `from` (ADR 0128). Sent back by a failing check on the pull request's merged tree (ADR 0226), or by its conflict with the base `branch` (ADR 0244). The merge of the base `branch` a resumed session continues in its worktree (ADR 0244). Why a retry runs: the secret scan failed the attempt before it, `attempt` (ADR 0187). Why a retry runs: the attempt before it, `attempt`, failed (ADR 0248). The Brewery's repositories and their bases, an input `from: "repositories"` (ADR 0234). The earlier rounds' findings of a lens step, with their dispositions (ADR 0191). The brewer's input name (`inputs[].name`, the `{variable}` in its body), when it has one. A prompt built by `assembleBrewerPrompt`; the brewer runner takes no other. `nonce` is empty when there are no inputs: the prompt is then the instructions alone. An input contains this prompt's nonce: by chance that never happens, so a likely injection. Random bytes from a CSPRNG; injected so tests can fix the nonce. The `source` attribute of an input's tag. An attribute value that cannot end its quotes or the tag, or break the line. Placed with the brewer's own instructions, above every input, never next to one. Builds a brewer's prompt: its own instructions, the rule about tagged input, then every input once, in order, between `<untrusted-input-<nonce> …>` tags with a new nonce for this prompt. In any case: a model may take `</UNTRUSTED-INPUT-…>` for the closing tag too.

cards.summary: The check runner (ADR 0069): runs the attempts of check steps, the gravity readings. For an attempt the driver started, it runs the step's checks one after another in the attempt's worktree through the platform shell and the process runner, which kills the whole tree at the step's deadline or when the engine stops the attempt; the first check that does not pass ends the step. No model. A red proof runs the test check and judges the structured test report against the tests the proven step committed, never the exit code (ADR 0078).
cards.comments: The check runner (ADR 0069): runs the attempts of check steps, the gravity readings. For an attempt the driver started, it runs the step's checks one after another in the attempt's worktree through the platform shell and the process runner, which kills the whole tree at the step's deadline or when the engine stops the attempt; the first check that does not pass ends the step. No model. A red proof runs the test check and judges the structured test report against the tests the proven step committed, never the exit code (ADR 0078). A test report's file in a worktree: cleared before the test check runs, read after it. Clears the report only inside `root`, the worktree. Reads the report only inside `root`, the worktree. The folded state: the driver's, which has recorded the attempt's start and worktree. The checks of the recipes' check steps (`loadRecipes`). The commands of a repository's checks (`foedrum.jsonc`), or undefined when it lists none. The test report a repository's test check writes (`foedrum.jsonc`), for red proofs. A repository's setup, run before a check step's checks, and the process runner it runs through: the checks' sandbox with the network kept (ADR 0158). git, for the commits of the step a red proof proves (ADR 0078). The clone a repository's attempt worktrees are added to, where git reads the proven step's commits: never the attempt's worktree, which git would find by its `.git` file. Default the file system's. The brewers' environment: its minimal base and the runner's forced variables (ADR 0063). Default this process's. A test report file's largest size: a report of a large suite, read once per red proof. The test report files of the real file system: removed, a folder included, through the platform's removal, which retries a file another process holds open; read as an out doc is. Resolved through links first: a linked folder on the path could point the removal anywhere. None of a repository's checks: what a step of literal commands plans against. The checks of a tree in a worktree, the repository's setup first: what a check step's attempt runs, and the run on an open pull request's merged tree (ADR 0203). Where a tree is: its repository and its folder. The check runner, and the checks of a tree it runs a check step's through. The attempts it runs, by key, with when they started: their progress for the heartbeat. What one run of `check` read on this platform (ADR 0076). Runs one check in the worktree through the checks' process runner, its sandbox (ADR 0076). The repository's setup running, or undefined when it has none: then nothing is awaited, so the first check starts at once, before the engine could stop the attempt. Once the step needs nothing else before its checks (ADR 0140). A red proof (ADR 0078): the test check's reading, then the report it wrote, judged against what step `of` committed. In the clone, never by discovery in the worktree (#210). foedrum.jsonc's schema gives every repository with a test report its test check. The repository's setup once nothing else blocks the run, so the run finds what it installed (ADR 0140). A report the tree holds, committed or left over, must not stand for this run's. A folder at the path, or on Windows a file another process holds open. TAP on stdout may be as large as a report file. A check that did not exit read no report: it ends as any check does (ADR 0069). The regression tests the proven step named pass, as they should (ADR 0170). The checks `refs` of the tree in `worktree`, the repository's setup first: a check step's attempt's, and the merged tree of an open pull request (ADR 0203). The repository's setup once nothing else blocks the step and a check will run, so the checks find what it installed (ADR 0140).

cards.summary: Gravity readings, the core (ADR 0021, ADR 0069): which command line each check of a check step runs on this platform, what one run read, and the step's outcome from its readings. Pure; check-runner.ts runs the commands.
cards.comments: Gravity readings, the core (ADR 0021, ADR 0069): which command line each check of a check step runs on this platform, what one run read, and the step's outcome from its readings. Pure; check-runner.ts runs the commands. The command behind each check of a repository, or null where it has none (ADR 0023). A check ready to run: its command line on this platform, or a skip. `check` is absent for a Brewery's literal command and a repository's setup (ADR 0140). What the process runner answered for one command. The signal that ended it when the runner did not send it. The line `command` runs on `platform`: its override there, else `run`. The checks of a step, in order, as `repository` maps the named ones. The end of `output` that a reading keeps (`MAX_TAIL_LENGTH`), never half a character. The second half of a surrogate pair whose first half was cut off. `output` with each line that can reach the tail left out when it looks like a secret, saying what it looked like. A check runs code a brewer may have written, so what it prints is untrusted (ADR 0069). A commit hash counts too: the engine cannot tell one from a 40-character key. Only the lines the tail can keep are read, from the end, and of a long line only its end, so output written to stall the patterns costs no more than a tail's worth. Counted as kept once left out, so the tail never reaches a line that was not read. What one run of `check` read. Secrets out first, so the bound never keeps half of one. Whether a reading lets the step go on: a skip, or an exit with code 0. A check as a reason names it: its name and command, or a literal command alone. The last line of `text` that is not blank. A setup that did not pass: no fact about the tree under check, so never a failure along `onFail`, but the attempt's environment, or a cancel at the engine's stop (ADR 0140). The step's outcome from its readings: the first that did not pass decides (ADR 0069). The same tree would read the same again: no retry, the onFail route or Stuck. A crash of the code under check is a failure of the tree, as an exit code is. Another attempt would write as much again; a human makes the check quieter. A missing shell or program: another attempt would meet the same environment.

cards.summary: The part of a failed GitHub Actions job's log that goes with its batch back to a fix step (ADR 0228): the failing step up to its first error, read for secrets and cut to a tail. A job's log is printed by code the pull request changed, so it is untrusted, as a check's output is.
cards.comments: The part of a failed GitHub Actions job's log that goes with its batch back to a fix step (ADR 0228): the failing step up to its first error, read for secrets and cut to a tail. A job's log is printed by code the pull request changed, so it is untrusted, as a check's output is. The time GitHub puts before each line of a job's log: `2026-10-26T18:49:21.7159496Z `. Terminal escape sequences: CSI (colours), OSC (titles, links), and any other escape with its intermediate bytes (`ESC c`, `ESC ( B`). biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noControlCharactersInRegex: escape sequences are what it removes. Every control character left but the tab, C1 included: an ESC that began no sequence, or one the removal of another put back together, never reaches a reader (ADR 0228). biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noControlCharactersInRegex: control characters are what it removes. The excerpt of `log` a record keeps. No error line: the end before the post-job steps, which are never the failure. The step that holds the error starts at the last `Run` group before it. Secrets out first, so the bound never keeps half of one.

cards.summary: The red proof's verdict, the core (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): whether a test report shows the tests a step committed failing because the behaviour is missing. Pure; check-runner.ts runs the tests and reads the report and the step's diff.
cards.comments: The red proof's verdict, the core (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): whether a test report shows the tests a step committed failing because the behaviour is missing. Pure; check-runner.ts runs the tests and reads the report and the step's diff. `tests`: the names of the proven step's tests, all failing. What a run says when a test did not load, compile, import or get collected, in the languages and runners a Brewery is likely to use. A test that fails with one of these never reached the behaviour it tests, so it does not prove the behaviour is missing, even when the code under test threw it: a Gauger that tests such an error asserts on it instead. A reported name longer than this is no declaration: the names come from code a brewer wrote, and each is matched against every line the step added. Longer quotes of a run are cut to this, for the reason that reaches the event log. The first line of `text` that names a load error, trimmed. The forms of a test's name its declaration may have: the name, without the parameters a runner adds (`(int, int)`, `[1]`), its last part after suite titles (`the calculator > adds`), and that part's last part after a class or module (`AddTest.adds`). A class or module holds no space, so a sentence with a dot (`… with git.commit`) has no last part; a suite title may. Whether a line the step added declares the test `name`, as a declaration writes a test's name (ADR 0176): as the whole of a string literal (`test('adds two numbers'`, `` fun `adds`() ``); as an identifier right before `(` where no call can stand (`void adds(`, ADR 0178); after `def`, `fn` or `func` (`def test_adds`, `fn adds<T>()`); as a GoogleTest macro's test (`TEST(CalcTest, Adds)`); or as the rest of a Gherkin scenario's line (`Scenario: adds two numbers`). A bare word in code (`key: null,`, `f(null)`) is none (#466), nor a method call (`calc.add(`), nor a line that only asserts (`assert.equal(add(1, 2), 3)`). Each form is a literal between fixed parts, so the match stays linear in the line. A line keeps no carriage return of a CRLF file. What ends a line's text before a called name: a pair, a character or a word that opens an expression. The longest word of EXPRESSION_END, plus the character before it and the one before `?`. Whether `name(` stands in `text` where a declaration can (ADR 0178): after no letter, digit, underscore or dot, with something before it on the line that does not end in an expression's opening. Each place the name stands is checked, backwards from there only. A line that is a comment, in the languages a Brewery is likely to use; `#[` is a Rust attribute. The lines of `diff` a regression test may be declared in (ADR 0170): in a file where the step declared a test, whose lines testsUnchanged keeps, and no comment, which declares nothing. "test "a"", or "test "a" (and 2 more)". Whether `report` proves red the tests that `diff`, the proven step's commits, added; of them, `regressionTests` are the names the step gave its regression tests, which pass (ADR 0170). A suite's own result follows its tests'; its tests are judged. Why a recipe that proves its tests red cannot brew in `repo`: it has no test report.

cards.summary: A repository's setup (ADR 0140, ADR 0158) and the command lines of check steps: how one line runs in a worktree through a process runner, killed before the attempt's deadline, in the brewers' environment without claude's login. The check runner runs the setup before a check step's checks, and the brewer runners before claude (ADR 0163).
cards.comments: A repository's setup (ADR 0140, ADR 0158) and the command lines of check steps: how one line runs in a worktree through a process runner, killed before the attempt's deadline, in the brewers' environment without claude's login. The check runner runs the setup before a check step's checks, and the brewer runners before claude (ADR 0163). How long before the attempt's deadline a command line is killed: the process runner's grace between SIGTERM and SIGKILL (2.5 s) and a supervisor tick (5 s, ADR 0027), with room to spare. claude's login and settings, which the brewers' base keeps for claude: a check, which has the network on native Windows (ADR 0076), gets none of them (ADR 0069). The environment of a check or a setup: nothing a brewer does not get, and not claude's login either; by key, so a forced PATH replaces Path on Windows (ADR 0063, ADR 0069). Where and how long one command line runs. The attempt's deadline: the line is killed `KILL_MARGIN_MS` before it. Its own limit, when that is sooner than the deadline's. Runs one command line through the platform shell, on Windows in a Job Object, killed before the attempt's deadline, at `timeoutMs` when that is sooner, or at the stop. The process runner kills the tree before the step's deadline, also when no tick comes: early enough that the kill's grace ends and the reading is recorded before a tick expires the attempt and loses it. A repository's setup as it runs on a platform. Its command line for the platform. Its own timeout. Whether no sandbox holds it: on native Windows (ADR 0158). The setup `found` as it runs on `platform`. What one run of `check` read; when no sandbox held it, it says so: a check or a setup on native Windows (ADR 0076, ADR 0158). The reading of a repository's setup, run in the worktree with the network, in the check sandbox where there is one (ADR 0158).

cards.summary: What a step of a batch committed, read with git (ADR 0078): the red proof finds the proven step's tests in it, and the testsUnchanged guard compares an attempt's changes with it.
cards.comments: What a step of a batch committed, read with git (ADR 0078): the red proof finds the proven step's tests in it, and the testsUnchanged guard compares an attempt's changes with it. The commits of step `stepId`: from where its first attempt started to the branch of its latest attempt that succeeded, or of the worktree that attempt resumed in, so a step a route sent back counts its earlier attempts' commits too; undefined when none succeeded, as for a step the batch skipped. A resumed attempt committed on the branch of the worktree its session ran in (ADR 0117). Built from the attempt, never the recorded branch (ADR 0037). The tests step `stepId` named in the out doc of its latest attempt that succeeded, the one whose commits `stepCommits` ends at (ADR 0170); undefined when it named none. The last line of `text` that is not blank. More than the runner's default 4 MiB: a large but ordinary change (fixtures, a lock file). The files changed from `from` to `to`, read in `cwd`, the repository's clone, whatever the user's diff settings, in `paths` only when given; or why git could not read them. A committed .gitattributes (`-diff`, `binary`) must not turn the tests into binary files. A brewer names the files: a name that starts with ":" is no pathspec magic.

cards.summary: The testsUnchanged guard, the shell (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): around the brewer runner, once an attempt of a guarded step succeeded, it reads from git what the proven step committed and what the attempt changed, and fails the attempt when it changed or removed a test declaration or assertion. tests-unchanged.ts decides.
cards.comments: The testsUnchanged guard, the shell (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): around the brewer runner, once an attempt of a guarded step succeeded, it reads from git what the proven step committed and what the attempt changed, and fails the attempt when it changed or removed a test declaration or assertion. tests-unchanged.ts decides. The folded state: the driver's, which has recorded the attempt's start and worktree. The step whose tests attempt `ref` must keep: its recipe's red proof's, when its brewer has the testsUnchanged guard; else undefined. The clone a repository's attempt worktrees are added to, where git reads the commits: never the attempt's worktree, whose `.git` file its brewer can rewrite. Default the system clock. The attempts whose commits it is reading: it reports their progress, so their leases hold. `end`, or how the guard ends the attempt instead. Its own worktree, or for a resumed attempt the one its session ran in, whose maker's branch carries the changes of every attempt of that session (ADR 0117). Without a worktree the attempt changed nothing the guard could read. A step the batch skipped, or that never succeeded, committed no tests to keep. What the proven step committed, then what this attempt committed on top of where it started, in the clone: never by discovery in the worktree, whose .git file the brewer can rewrite. Up to its branch, which the task tree carries on whatever HEAD is (ADR 0066), and only in the files whose lines the guard keeps. Another attempt starts afresh at the task tree, and may keep the tests.

cards.summary: The testsUnchanged guard, the core (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): which test declarations and assertions that the proven step committed an attempt changed or removed. Pure; tests-guard.ts reads the diffs.
cards.comments: The testsUnchanged guard, the core (ADR 0017, ADR 0078): which test declarations and assertions that the proven step committed an attempt changed or removed. Pure; tests-guard.ts reads the diffs. A line of the proven step's tests that an attempt changed or removed, in the file it was in. A line that declares a test, in the runners a Brewery is likely to use. A line that asserts. A line that only imports, which the attempt may change. Whether `line` declares a test: a file with one is a test file, whose lines the guard keeps. Whether `line` asserts without declaring a test: a call of what it tests, not a declaration. The declarations and assertions in each file of `proven` that declares a test, by path. How often each line occurs, trimmed. The declarations and assertions `proven` added that `changes` removed or changed. A line moved within its file is removed and added again: only the lines lost count.

cards.summary: `foedrum brew` on the real machine (ADR 0123): its owner from `--as`, the Claude Code session or else `terminal` (ADR 0259), the Brewery's files read as serve reads them, and runBrew (brew.ts) on serve's shell (serve-shell.ts) with the real git until the batch stops or a stop signal. On a terminal outside Claude Code, an interactive step's session opens in the foreground (ADR 0222). cli-main.ts loads it.
cards.comments: `foedrum brew` on the real machine (ADR 0123): its owner from `--as`, the Claude Code session or else `terminal` (ADR 0259), the Brewery's files read as serve reads them, and runBrew (brew.ts) on serve's shell (serve-shell.ts) with the real git until the batch stops or a stop signal. On a terminal outside Claude Code, an interactive step's session opens in the foreground (ADR 0222). cli-main.ts loads it. Why brew opens no interactive step's session here (ADR 0222): claude needs the terminal, which a Claude Code session keeps, and stdin must be one. brew's shell: with sessions, a runner that opens an interactive step's session in the foreground and runs every other attempt headless, a resumed one too, as serve's (ADR 0222); without, serve's. What brew is asked to brew, as whom and who asked, and why it opens no session, if it does not. What `--new-window` starts the brew with: the machine's launcher facts, node and program. This node. The `foedrum` program this node runs. The variables that tell a brew it runs inside a Claude Code session (noSessionsOf, brewOwner). The real machine's: this process's node, program and platform, and its PATH. Opens a new terminal window that runs `foedrum brew <issue> --take` with this node and program, for the plugin's session, which cannot hand its terminal to claude (ADR 0222). Where none can open, it says the line to run in a terminal (exit 5). As this brew's owner: a window may start with none of this session's variables (macOS). Without the Claude Code session's variables, so the window's brew opens the session. The launcher returned: the window shows whether it opened. Brews the batch of `input.issue` in the Brewery checkout `cwd`, as the command layer `issued` it. A session in `env` that names no driver, without `--as`, is a mistake of the command line (exit 2); its lines go straight to the terminal. The stop signals are listened for while brew runs, and no longer once it returns. On a terminal every lasting line, the state branch's too, goes over the live line. While claude has the terminal, brew's lines wait, its live line is not drawn, and Ctrl+C is claude's, as for resume (ADR 0127, ADR 0222). A live line only where standard output is a terminal that takes it (ADR 0174).

cards.summary: `foedrum brew`, the interactive driver of one batch (ADR 0123): under an owner of its own (`--as`, or the Claude Code session it runs in, else `terminal`), it takes that owner's lock, opens the driver on the wiring it shares with `foedrum serve` (driver-wiring.ts) with `takes` that batch alone, orders and routes the issue first when it has no batch, and ticks until the batch is on tap, cancelled or Stuck. Its exit code says which, so the plugin's session can ask the engineer and brew again. On a terminal (the shell gives one) it keeps a live line of what the running attempts do (ADR 0174).

A question needs two options (ADR 0006). The line feed and the Unicode line and paragraph separators, which end a line. `text` with each line break shown as a `\uXXXX` escape, as `printable` shows the rest. The live line: `frame`, the batch's time, then the attempts, fitted to the terminal. Brews the batch of `request.target` until it stops; the exit code of ADR 0123. The live line (ADR 0174), drawn only with a terminal: when the batch was ordered (this run's start until the batch says, ADR 0179), the attempts that run, when this driver first saw each run, what the driver reports of one, and whether the line is on screen. A lasting line goes over the live line: it clears it, prints, and draws it again. The issue's repository: a target issue's by its alias, which needs an intake (ADR 0105). A paused order would wait with nothing to do: it is continued first (ADR 0202). A sub-order's batch waits for its order's pause, which is the one to continue. An issue with no batch, or an Ordered one, is routed by its one recipe label (ADR 0068). Checked before anything is ordered or claimed, as the intake leaves it unrouted. --take, once nothing else refuses the brew: the batch is this driver's at once, and the one that held it stops (ADR 0124). A lease that lapsed meanwhile leaves nothing to take over. What opens the session a batch waits for, as this brew can or cannot (ADR 0222). A batch that waits for a session when a brew that opens one starts: the person runs it now, once; within the run the batch never retries by itself (ADR 0222). Until the next tick: plain, one wait; on a terminal, a redraw each second (ADR 0174), counted rather than read off the clock, so a clock set back cannot hold the tick off. After a takeover from this driver that resumes a step, the ends of the runs it stopped there, recorded at the step boundary before brew lets its driver go, within a lease: the new holder waits for their leases before it continues the session (ADR 0127). A closed driver records no end, and its runs' leases would hold the step for a whole lease. A takeover whose owner let the batch go since resumes nothing now (ADR 0127). When the last line was said, and when this driver first saw each attempt run. A pause that came while it brews: once nothing of the batch runs, nothing will until a person continues it (ADR 0202). A step can run for many minutes in silence: say it still runs (#406). cards.comments: `foedrum brewers` (ADR 0159): per brewer, the attempts of its steps, how they ended, the batches it holds Stuck and the tokens it used, from the folded events. The brewers in use and what each recipe's step is now, from the loaded files. Every brewer in use, Brewery's and default, with its file. Step `stepId` of recipe `recipe` as the files have it, with its brewer's name when it is a brewer step (a check or an action step has none), or `undefined` when no recipe of that name has that step. How the started attempts ended: by outcome, and those not finished. Started and not finished: running now, or abandoned when the batch went Stuck. What the attempts of some steps did. The attempts that started. The batches Stuck now at one of these steps, by id, in the order they were ordered. The sum of the finished attempts' usage. Every brewer in use, by name, also those with no attempt. The steps the recipe files no longer have (ADR 0059), by recipe and step. A `Tally` while the report fills it. One scheduled and never started did not run. Adds `usage` to `sum`; an attempt that reported none adds nothing. The recipe each attempt was scheduled under, by its `attemptKey`: a batch's steps keep the attempts of the recipe it brewed before a person chose another (ADR 0159). The report over `state`, each attempt under its recipe in `ran` (`recipesRun` of the events `state` folds) and each step's brewer from `source`. The counts of step `stepId` of `recipe`, or none for a step without a brewer. A batch has steps only once a recipe was chosen. `ran` has every attempt of the events `state` folds; the batch's recipe is the latest. A batch is Stuck at a step of the recipe it brews now. Names in code-unit order, the same on every machine. A count with its digits grouped. The tokens of `usage`, each of the four counts on its own, or that none were reported. The attempts and how they ended, the tokens they used, and the batches Stuck at the steps; a batch can be Stuck at a step whose attempt never started. What `foedrum brewers` prints. What the report needs from the Brewery's loaded files. The brewers in use and each recipe's steps, from the loaded files.

cards.summary: `foedrum`'s commands on the real machine, from the checkout `cwd`: the wiring main.ts runs.
cards.comments: `foedrum`'s commands on the real machine, from the checkout `cwd`: the wiring main.ts runs. Runs one command (`argv`) of the command layer in the Brewery checkout `cwd`. doctor's and serve's facts, gh's login among them, come through `exec` and `resolve`, default the real runner and PATH, so a test gives fakes or a canned answer for gh's login. A failure the command layer throws, such as a store that cannot be read, is one line, as for every other failure. `status --watch` draws on `board`, default standard output and the process's environment. Never creates or changes a store (ADR 0030): a read in the wrong folder says so instead of making an empty one, and an older Cellar's store is not migrated under it. A command that changes state never creates a store either; it opens the Brewery's. Files that do not load refuse the command with doctor's line (ADR 0053). Through the engine's git, in each repository's clone as serve finds it (ADR 0092). gh's own login, never a token (ADR 0073), through the runner a test gives. The intake's reads, as serve makes them, through gh's own login (ADR 0073, ADR 0208). Loaded only for serve: it brings the runner, git and the state branch. Loaded only for brew, as for serve. Loaded only for status --watch: the board and the signals that stop it. The store as status reads it, afresh at each board; none yet is no batch. Loaded only for resume: it brings serve's setup and the worktrees. Loaded only for init: the terminal's questions and the Brewery's files.

cards.summary: The command registry (ADR 0019): one schema and one handler per command. Surfaces turn their input into a command's input and run it; run.ts is the terminal's. doctor, status, stuck, brewers, lenses and replay only read, and init writes only the Brewery's files, so they append nothing (ADR 0030, ADR 0199). The others turn their input into one of the engine's human commands and append its events through the command log, recorded with who issued it and from where (ADR 0025).
cards.comments: The command registry (ADR 0019): one schema and one handler per command. Surfaces turn their input into a command's input and run it; run.ts is the terminal's. doctor, status, stuck, brewers, lenses and replay only read, and init writes only the Brewery's files, so they append nothing (ADR 0030, ADR 0199). The others turn their input into one of the engine's human commands and append its events through the command log, recorded with who issued it and from where (ADR 0025). A command as surfaces see it: its schema and handler behind `run`. Whether it may append events (ADR 0030): such a command opens the store for writing, and its events record who issued it and from where. A read-only one never writes. The positional arguments, in order: each is a field of the command's input. The positional arguments after those that may be left out, in order. The field that takes the positional arguments after those, one or more, as a list. The options it takes, each with a value and a field of its own: the value's name, by option. The options that may be given more than once, their field a list of the values in order. The options it takes without a value, each a field of its own that is true when given. What `--help`'s row shows for its options and flags, which it then lists below the table. Why the plugin does not carry it, when it does not (ADR 0125); the parity test reads it. Validates the input against the command's schema, then runs its handler. The lines of the limits that hold now (ADR 0217), from foedrum.jsonc and the recipes, read only while a limit can hold; one line when they do not load. Reads every event of the Brewery's store and folds them; one line when there is no store (or `none`, for a command that has an answer without one) or the fold refuses the log. Never writes (ADR 0030). The store closes once `show` is done. Who issues a human command about `batchId`, and from where (ADR 0019). Issues the human command `build` makes from the folded state (or the reason it makes none) through the command log, so it is decided against the latest events (ADR 0025), and says where the batch is now. `state` folds the latest events each time, for a build that waits on the code host. Never creates a store. Accepted, so the batch exists. Runs `use` on the command log of the Brewery's store, opened for writing and closed after; one line when there is no store or the fold refuses the log. Never creates a store. What `foedrum order <alias>#<n>` claims in, from foedrum.jsonc, or why it cannot. Without an intake, serve would neither mark nor release the claim, nor route the batch. The claim records the Brewery that holds it (ADR 0043). An order as a person wrote it: `<alias>#<n>` or `#<n>`. The order `target` names: a Brewery issue, or a target repository's by its alias in foedrum.jsonc (ADR 0202). The intake's queue as a pass would read it now, in rank order (ADR 0208): the Brewery's open issues and every intake repository's, through gh's login; or what could not be read. `placed`, the order being ranked, is in it while sub-orders of it are left, ready or not (ADR 0211). How `rank` shows an order's rank, or that it has none. Where `order` stands in `queue`: `place <n> of <all> in the queue`, or undefined. An order's ready sub-orders hold one place (ADR 0211). The questions `batch` asks while Stuck on `needs_input`, in order; none otherwise. The target repository an order claims its issue in, and the Brewery the claim records. The human command that orders `order` again (ADR 0105), or why it cannot: refused while `orderRefusal` says so, then a target issue is claimed first, and the batch takes the issue's next id. `foedrum order` and `foedrum brew` order through it. Before the claim, so a refused order claims nothing; decide checks it again. Why a decision on a Stuck batch is the terminal's (ADR 0125). Each the answer to one question, as typed (ADR 0212). Questions and lines on the terminal, run by it as brew is (ADR 0199). A board on the terminal, run by it as brew's live line is (ADR 0188). The task-tree branches the cleanup keeps (ADR 0084), read only when there are any. The batches an interactive driver holds now, by its owner (ADR 0123). A fresh Brewery: serve and brew make the store when they first start. Files that do not load refuse it with doctor's line, before the store is opened. A fresh Brewery: every brewer, none with an attempt yet. Files that do not load refuse it with doctor's line, before the store is opened. A fresh Brewery: every lens, none with a round yet. Beside its own events, the pauses and continues of its order or of all, which name no batch (ADR 0202): since the last continue before it was ordered, so a pause that held it from its order shows too. And the ranks of its order, which it had in the intake's queue (ADR 0208). And the usage windows, which hold the brewers of every batch, since every one was last open before the batch was ordered (ADR 0206, ADR 0215). Without a scope, as #543 wrote it, every closed window opened. On a running batch it drives the batch, through serve's wiring as brew (ADR 0127). A batch that asks nothing is decide's to refuse, with its reason. A Brewery issue is never claimed, so it needs neither foedrum.jsonc nor GitHub. Called only for a claim, which carries its config. A driver of its own on the machine, run by the terminal (ADR 0123). brew's driver, routed to mash-in first, until the Innkeeper's question (ADR 0232). Reads the queue as a pass would, through gh's login, and records the place it finds. The lease goes to the new owner at once; its driver renews it from its next tick (ADR 0124).

cards.summary: `foedrum doctor`, the shell (ADR 0021): finds each tool through PATH and asks it for its version through the process runner, and asks gh for its login and git for its credential helpers (ADR 0073). doctor.ts decides what the answers mean.
cards.comments: `foedrum doctor`, the shell (ADR 0021): finds each tool through PATH and asks it for its version through the process runner, and asks gh for its login and git for its credential helpers (ADR 0073). doctor.ts decides what the answers mean. How each tool reports its version; socat has no --version. A version command answers at once; one that hangs must not hold doctor up. A container runtime that does not answer at once is usually waiting for its daemon, and then not usable anyway (#99). The file a command name runs, or `undefined` when it is not on PATH. `process.execPath`: the program doctor holds in a Job Object to see that it can. The text of the file at `path`, or undefined when there is none. The Brewery's recipe and brewer files in `cwd` (`readBreweryFiles`, ADR 0053). The local gate's personal denylist (`readDenylist`, ADR 0114); doctor keeps only its path. The environment gh runs in, without the GitHub token variables; default this process's. The GitHub host to ask gh about; default the one `foedrum.jsonc` in `cwd` names. Whether a path exists, for the keep-awake mechanism (ADR 0195); default `existsSync`. On Linux, whether AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces; undefined when unknown. The list's state without its text: doctor never prints a word of it (ADR 0114). Every tool's path and version answer, asked all at once. Why the runner killed it comes first, so the report can say so. Brewers run only in a Job Object on Windows (ADR 0039): node, doing nothing, held in one. A foedrum.jsonc that cannot be read (a folder, no permission) is a problem doctor reports. A command doctor runs besides a version command: its exit code and what it printed, why the runner killed it first. `undefined` when its program is not on PATH. gh auth status prints to stderr when there is no login; git config prints to stdout. As Foedrum's own calls are made: without a token variable, which gh would take instead. Found on PATH, never run: starting it would hold the machine awake (ADR 0195).

cards.summary: `foedrum doctor`, the core (ADR 0021): turns facts gathered from the machine into a report of the tools Foedrum needs, the effective isolation level (ADR 0010, architecture §13) and what is missing. doctor-facts.ts gathers the facts.
cards.comments: `foedrum doctor`, the core (ADR 0021): turns facts gathered from the machine into a report of the tools Foedrum needs, the effective isolation level (ADR 0010, architecture §13) and what is missing. doctor-facts.ts gathers the facts. The tools doctor looks for on PATH. A tool found on PATH, and what its version command answered. The exit code of the version command; `null` when it could not start or was killed. `os.release()`; on Linux it tells WSL 1 and WSL 2 apart. `process.versions.node` Each tool, or `undefined` when it is not on PATH.
