Why foedrum.jsonc could not be read, when it is there and could not be. The Brewery's recipe and brewer files in the working directory (ADR 0053). gh's login and git's credential helpers for the Brewery's GitHub host (ADR 0073). Whether the local gate's personal denylist is set, and where (ADR 0114); never its words. On Linux, whether AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces, which bwrap needs (ADR 0076). How this machine is kept awake while an attempt runs, or why it cannot be (ADR 0195). The denylist's state as doctor reports it: its path, never its words or their count. How a command answered: its exit code (`null` when it could not start or was killed) and output. What doctor asks about the GitHub host Foedrum reaches through gh's own login (ADR 0073). gh's `--hostname`: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise host or `github.localhost`. `gh auth status --hostname <host>`, without the token variables; undefined without gh. What `git config --null --get-regexp ^credential\.` printed; undefined without git. The isolation levels Foedrum can reach without configuration (ADR 0010). One row of the report: a tool, its version and where it is; no path when it was not found. `undefined` when the tool did not report one. A required problem stops Foedrum from running brewers; doctor then exits 1. The prompt a brewer's own files build: its instructions and its lens inputs (ADR 0141). Its file: `brewers/<name>.md` or `defaults/brewers/<name>.md`. In UTF-8. An estimate: the bytes divided by 4, rounded up. How this machine is kept awake while an attempt runs (ADR 0195); never a problem. The container runtime that makes the optional container level possible; one that is on PATH but does not answer its version is not usable, with what it said first. The paths of Foedrum's default files the Brewery's recipes use, when doctor read its files and they load: those it has no file of the same name for (ADR 0098). Each brewer in use's prompt from its own files, when doctor read them and they load (ADR 0141). What doctor noticed about the Brewery's files, when it read them; never a problem (ADR 0141). The local gate's denylist, when doctor looked for it (ADR 0114). No required problem. package.json's engines. `git merge-tree --write-tree`, which the base check of open pull requests runs (ADR 0198), came in 2.38.0 (ADR 0200); GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, which a brewer's forced configuration rests on, in 2.31.0 (ADR 0109). git-scm.com/downloads'; gh keeps its login in the OS keyring by default since 2.26.0 (ADR 0073), and since 2.97.0 prints an answer with terminal escape sequences, a job's log, only when asked to (ADR 0228). cli.github.com, then run gh auth login'; The helper `gh auth setup-git` writes: `!gh auth git-credential`, with gh's path. gh's token line, masked or not, and anything that looks like a token: never quoted in a report. What each level keeps from gh's login (ADR 0082, #229). Claude Code's sandbox docs settle the user folders (ADR 0160), the hosts file and the token variables (ADR 0087), not the OS keyring, so the sandbox never "closes" it; on WSL2 the user folders include /mnt, with the Windows user's home. The container mounts only the worktree (ADR 0010). Check steps run in an OS sandbox of Foedrum's own with no network, outside one only on native Windows (ADR 0076). Where check steps run (ADR 0076): bwrap or sandbox-exec, and outside one on native Windows. Ubuntu 24.04 and later keep bwrap from making the user namespaces its sandbox needs, unless an AppArmor profile lets it: Claude Code's sandbox docs, "Ubuntu 24.04 and later: allow bubblewrap to create user namespaces" (ADR 0076). Seen on CI's ubuntu leg (#357). code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing, "Ubuntu 24.04 and later: allow bubblewrap to create user namespaces"), then run sudo systemctl reload apparmor.'; The first dotted number a version command printed; `undefined` when it failed. What a tool, or the runner that could not start it, said first. The user-mode network stack a Linux setup's namespace gets the network from (ADR 0218): slirp4netns, else pasta, else slirp4netns as missing. pasta prints its version as its first line's second word (`pasta 2024_09_06.6b38f07`), not a dotted number; Ubuntu 24.04's says `pasta unknown version`. A setup does not start on Linux without a stack; a Brewery without one needs neither. Whether the dotted version `version` comes before `least`. The host gh reaches the Brewery's GitHub on: the one foedrum.jsonc's `githubApi` names, else `github.com` (ADR 0073), also when the file is missing or not valid. Whether a credential URL from git's configuration covers every https URL of `host`: the same scheme and host, no user, port or path that would narrow it. The credential helpers git asks for `https://<host>`, in order, from what `git config --null --get-regexp ^credential\.` printed: `credential.helper` and `credential.<url>.helper` of a URL that covers the host, where an empty value clears the list before it, as git does. gh, its login and git's credential helper (ADR 0073): Foedrum reaches GitHub only through gh's own login, for the API and, as git's credential helper, for pushes. What gh said after the host's own line, unless it only says what the problem says already. git exits 1

cards.comments: The wiring a driver on the real machine runs on (ADR 0063, ADR 0123), shared by `foedrum serve` and `foedrum brew`: under a lock the caller took, it opens the event store and the state branch, each repository's attempt worktrees, GitHub through gh, the status comments (ADR 0072) and the claim effects, the attempt plans, the check runner and the guards, and the driver with the real runner. Each caller says which batches its driver takes. One tick of the driver, as every command that runs one ticks it: a tick that fails is reported and the next one runs anyway, but a stop of the engine, such as another engine's push of the state branch, is thrown (ADR 0027, ADR 0250). The runner that tells `awake` of each attempt it starts and when that attempt ends (ADR 0195). Before the runner starts it: a check step's process starts inside `start`. What the wiring has opened so far, for the caller to close however far it got. What a driver runs on once it is open. One cache of conditional reads for every GitHub read (ADR 0052). The GitHub client under them, for GraphQL (ADR 0073). The claim refs on GitHub (ADR 0043). Each repository's base and pushes, as the openPullRequest action has them (ADR 0071). The checks of a tree as the check runner reads a check step's (ADR 0203). Whether the driver takes a free batch (ADR 0044). Which batches its owner held at its start it drives on; every one by default (ADR 0123). Whether an attempt's retry or answer resumes its session: by default when its brewer's `retryMode` is `resume` (ADR 0118); `foedrum resume` of a running batch, always (ADR 0127). Whether the driver goes on with a batch it may hold; every one by default (ADR 0127). Whether it opens an interactive step's session: `foedrum brew` on a terminal (ADR 0222). Prints one line of the driver's own, a notice or a report. Reports a driver's notice. Opens the store, the state branch and the driver under `opened.lock`, noting each in `opened` as it goes: on a throw, the caller closes what is there with `closeOpened`. Rebuilds or catches up the store from the branch (ADR 0011, ADR 0024). Each repository's fetch, by its worktree manager: a plan's base it has no ref of (ADR 0233). The pull request goes into the branch the attempts start from (ADR 0071). The last check before the pull request merges that branch as the push fetches it (ADR 0164). GitHub's rate-limit pause runs on the driver's clock, which also decides when to poll. One cache of conditional reads for the intake, the marks and the orders' text (ADR 0052). gh's login: the status comments and the claim marks count only its own (ADR 0072, ADR 0073). Each order's plan, one comment on its issue edited in place (ADR 0233). Each Brewery issue's lane label, through the ledger as its status comment (ADR 0154). The recipe an answer to the Innkeeper chose, as a label on the issue, once (ADR 0232). A claimed batch the store has keeps its marks and release due, intake or not (ADR 0050). A conflict with a base that moved, posted on its pull request (ADR 0198), and a failing check on its merged tree, which says when the recipe sends the batch back to fix it (ADR 0226). A ready pull request's merge brief, on it, its title read as an issue's (ADR 0225). The login was read at the start, for the status comments (ADR 0072). The clone a repository's worktrees are added to: where git reads an attempt's commits, never its worktree (ADR 0074, ADR 0078). A Gauger its red proof sent back may name its tests without a commit (ADR 0258). Every attempt of a brewer with a shell gets its repository's dependencies first (ADR 0163). Where a commit-producing attempt's commits are counted (ADR 0074). A plan's paths are checked in each repository once it is done (ADR 0233). A base its clone has no ref of yet is fetched once, by its worktree manager (ADR 0233). A Taster's change is read by the engine, so the Taster runs no git (ADR 0161). A brewer that asks for house yeast gets the rules that match its change (ADR 0169). A check step's commands run in the brewers' environment, without a token variable (ADR 0069); as the same OS user they can still start gh, which answers from its login (ADR 0073, #204). A repository's setup installs before the checks, with the network (ADR 0140). The brewer of a step with the testsUnchanged guard keeps the red proof's tests (ADR 0078). A batch whose red proof would run needs its repository's test report from the start, so no brewer spends tokens on a batch that cannot prove its tests red (ADR 0017). The driver fails the attempt with the reason when it makes its worktree. Each out doc read is kept for the state branch before its step.finished (ADR 0103). A check step runs no claude, so it has no session (ADR 0116). The family of the model the brewer runs on, a blind-tasting swap included, says which closed usage window holds it (ADR 0215). A retry or an answer continues the session of a brewer that resumes (ADR 0117, ADR 0118), but an interactive step's: its session opens anew, with the whole prompt (ADR 0222). Closes what `opened` holds: the driver, which stops its runs and lets the lock go, or the lock.

cards.summary: `foedrum resume` on a running batch (ADR 0127): the interactive driver of that batch, on the wiring `foedrum serve` and `foedrum brew` share, under an owner of its own. It takes the batch over for the step whose session it continues (ADR 0124's takeover, naming the step, so the driver that held it stops its run there), drives the batch until the attempt that continues the session has ended (the shell's runner runs it in the foreground, resume-main.ts), and lets the batch go, so the driver that takes it next goes on from the next step.
cards.comments: `foedrum resume` on a running batch (ADR 0127): the interactive driver of that batch, on the wiring `foedrum serve` and `foedrum brew` share, under an owner of its own. It takes the batch over for the step whose session it continues (ADR 0124's takeover, naming the step, so the driver that held it stops its run there), drives the batch until the attempt that continues the session has ended (the shell's runner runs it in the foreground, resume-main.ts), and lets the batch go, so the driver that takes it next goes on from the next step. The step of a running batch whose session `foedrum resume` continues, as whom, and who asked. The driver's owner: its lock's and its leases' (ADR 0037). How an attempt ended, in a few words. The attempt of `stepId` that continues the session: the one waiting, or the one after the run. The step's latest attempt when the step's run is over for resume (ADR 0127): the attempt that continues the session has ended, or the run before it ended by itself, not by the stop, so no attempt will continue its session. Undefined while it waits or runs. Its end may have scheduled a retry, the next driver's to start. The stop's own end schedules the retry that continues the session, or leaves the batch Stuck. Takes the batch over, drives it until the resumed attempt ended, and lets it go; 0 when it did. Notices may carry text a model wrote: one line each, as brew's (ADR 0123). The attempt that continues the session, once the log is read, and the state as it is now. The batch's retries and answers continue their sessions, whatever the brewer's retryMode: the engineer took it over to continue one. Nothing more once the step's run is over: in the pass that records its end, the next attempt is the batch's next driver's to start (ADR 0127). The driver that holds the batch stops its run of the step at its next tick (ADR 0127). A lease that lapsed meanwhile leaves nothing to take over: the driver holds it at its tick. Held from the takeover on, also before the driver claims it for an attempt or an effect. At once for the driver that takes it next, rather than when its lease expires.

cards.summary: `foedrum resume <batch> [<step>[#<n>]]` (ADR 0126): opens a finished brewer attempt's own Claude Code session in its worktree, with its settings file written again and the brewer's environment, while the attempt's lease claims it. resume-main.ts gives it the real machine; unit tests give fakes.
cards.comments: `foedrum resume <batch> [<step>[#<n>]]` (ADR 0126): opens a finished brewer attempt's own Claude Code session in its worktree, with its settings file written again and the brewer's environment, while the attempt's lease claims it. resume-main.ts gives it the real machine; unit tests give fakes. What resume needs of serve's setup: where the attempts ran and how their brewers are set up. What resume needs from the machine. The Brewery's root: the event store is `.foedrum/index.db` in it. Opens the event store for writing its leases, or `undefined` when there is none. Serve's setup of the Brewery, or serve's problems. The attempt worktrees of a repository under the work root. Whether Claude Code keeps the session `id` on this machine. Writes an attempt's settings file, making its folder. Writes an attempt's system prompt file beside its settings file (ADR 0183). Whether this runs inside a Claude Code session (`CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1`), which cannot hand its terminal over, and whether stdin is a terminal. This process's environment: only the terminal's own variables reach claude from it. Runs `program` in the foreground in `cwd` with the terminal's stdio and the environment `env`; its exit code. Calls `beat` every `everyMs` until the returned function is called. Writes a line to the terminal while claude runs (stderr). This process's id, which names the lease's owner. Takes a running batch over and continues the session of step `stepId` in it, as the batch's driver until that attempt ended (ADR 0127); serve's setup and wiring, so the real machine's. Claude Code's config directory (ADR 0116): `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, by any case on Windows, else `.claude` in the home folder. Whether a transcript `<id>.jsonl` is in any project folder of `projects/` under `config`. What a terminal program reads to draw itself: the only variables of this process claude gets. Windows Terminal's. The attempt resume opens: its session and the worktree it ran in. The attempt `ref` when it finished with a session and a worktree, or why not. The step of a running batch whose session resume continues as the batch's driver (ADR 0127). The attempt whose session it continues: the one that runs, or the one before a retry. An interactive step's attempt whose session is open in a person's terminal (ADR 0231). The batch's issue, which `foedrum brew` reopens the session by. When its session opened (`interactiveSince`). Whether a driver brews `batchId` now: resume then takes it over (ADR 0127). The step of the running `batch` whose session resume continues (ADR 0127): of `stepId`, or the first step of the batch that has one, whose latest attempt runs a brewer's session, or waits to resume the session of the attempt before it (a retry or an answer, `resumeOf`). An interactive step whose session is open, of `stepId` or of any step, is refused instead (ADR 0231). A person's session cannot be stopped from outside, so it is never taken over (ADR 0231), also when no step is named and a headless step before it runs. The attempt `foedrum resume` opens (ADR 0126): the one `step` names as `<step>#<n>`, else the latest that started with a session and finished, in the order of the log, of the step or of the batch. On a running batch, the step whose session it continues as its driver (ADR 0127). Why an open interactive session is refused (ADR 0231): it must close so it reports, and brew opens it again when it closed without its out doc. Open for sure only while its attempt's lease lives, which brew renews while it waits on claude; the batch's may be another driver's. Runs `foedrum resume`: claude's exit code, or one line on why it opened nothing. From the log, so checked before it names a file or reaches claude's command line. A Claude Code session cannot hand its terminal to claude: the engineer runs it in one. A running batch's step alone: its latest attempt changes as the batch goes on. The attempt's lease alone: the cleanup keeps its worktree, also of an ended batch (worktreeClaims), a driver starts no other attempt of its step meanwhile (ADR 0055), and a second resume of the session is refused. The batch stays free for its driver. Takes or renews the lease, unless another owner's is alive: then that lease. The first claim also refuses a batch that a driver took up since the log was read (serve's setup takes seconds), in the transaction, so no attempt of the step starts in between. A renewal never ends the session: what goes wrong is said on the terminal. The attempt's environment (ADR 0109's forced variables included) with the terminal's own. Never another owner's lease.

cards.summary: The terminal surface of the command layer (ADR 0019): turns `foedrum <command> [args]` into a command from the registry, runs its handler and answers with the exit code and the output. main.ts gives it the real machine; unit tests give it fakes.
cards.comments: The terminal surface of the command layer (ADR 0019): turns `foedrum <command> [args]` into a command from the registry, runs its handler and answers with the exit code and the output. main.ts gives it the real machine; unit tests give it fakes. What `rank` reads of GitHub to know the intake's queue (ADR 0208). The login gh uses: an issue assigned to it is the Brewery's own. What the commands need from the machine. The Brewery's root: the event store is `.foedrum/index.db` in it. Opens the event store at `path` for reading only, or `undefined` when there is none. Opens the event store at `path` for a command that changes state, or `undefined` when there is none: a command never creates one. Loads the Brewery's recipes, which decide where a batch goes next. Only a command that changes state calls it. The brewers in use and each recipe's steps, from the Brewery's files, for `foedrum brewers` (ADR 0159); throws doctor's line when the files do not load. The lenses in use and each recipe's lens steps, from the Brewery's files, for `foedrum lenses` (ADR 0221); throws doctor's line when the files do not load. Who issues the command: the name its events record (ADR 0019). Where the command comes from: the surface its events record. The IANA time zone of the machine, which `pause --by` reads a local time in (ADR 0202). What git says of the task-tree branches the cleanup keeps (`Claims.unpushed`, ADR 0084), for `foedrum status` (ADR 0092). Called only when there are any. The Brewery's `foedrum.jsonc`, checked against its schema; throws with one line when it is missing or does not pass. Only `order` of a target issue reads it (ADR 0105). The claim refs on the GitHub host `config` names, through gh's own login (ADR 0073). Only `order` of a target issue calls it. The reads of the intake's queue on the GitHub host `config` names, through gh's own login (ADR 0073): the open issues and the login. Only `rank` calls it (ADR 0208). Runs the Cellar until Ctrl+C (ADR 0063); its notices go straight to the terminal. Brews one issue's batch until it stops (ADR 0123), as `as` or the Claude Code session's owner, recording who issued it and from where on an order it makes; its lines go straight to the terminal. `foedrum brew`, or `foedrum mash`, which brews the same way to its question (ADR 0232). Draws a board of the live batches until Ctrl+C (ADR 0188), for `foedrum status --watch`; it draws straight on the terminal, and refuses where there is none. The environment, for the Claude Code session that names a driver (ADR 0123, ADR 0124). Opens a finished attempt's session in its worktree (ADR 0126), or takes a running batch over and continues the session of its step (ADR 0127), recording who issued it and from where; claude has the terminal. Asks for and writes a Brewery's files, creating and cloning its repository outside a clone, offers the intake labels, commits and pushes, then runs doctor (ADR 0199, ADR 0207); its questions and lines go straight to the terminal, the answers its options give not asked (ADR 0212). 0 done, 1 the command failed, 2 the command line is wrong. Every control character but the line feed, DEL and the C1 controls: model-written text in the event log (a Stuck summary, a failure reason) must not move the cursor, rewrite earlier lines or set the clipboard (OSC 52) when it is printed. biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noControlCharactersInRegex: finding control characters is its job The text with each control character but the line feed shown as a `\uXXXX` escape. The surfaces `--via` may name (ADR 0125): the terminal's own and the plugin's, which runs the terminal. It changes only what the events record, never what a command may do (ADR 0019). `foedrum serve`, the Cellar (ADR 0063): a program that runs until Ctrl+C, not a command of the command layer that a comment or the plugin could issue, so it is not in the registry. A command whose options are too many for its row lists them below the table. The first problem the schema found, named as on the command line: with the argument it is about, or without one when it is about the whole list. Runs `foedrum <argv>`: exit 2 with one line on stderr when the command line is wrong. The options the command takes, each with a value or, a flag, without: a field of its input. Not strict, so an unknown option is a token this can name instead of parseArgs' message. The optional ones that were given, in order. A store that cannot be read, for example: one line, escaped like every other output.

Its toolchain rules (ADR 0023). The command behind each of its checks, or null where it has none (ADR 0023, ADR 0069). Where its test check writes the structured report red proofs read (ADR 0078). What runs before a brewer attempt and a check step's checks, with the network (ADR 0163). Where its own house-yeast rules are kept (ADR 0018); default in the repository. The path globs a batch's pull request names when its change touches them (ADR 0201). What the intake in serve's loop orders, and how often it polls (ADR 0068). The allow-listed GitHub logins: only an issue one of them opened is ordered. How many batches may be Ordered or Brewing at once: `concurrency`. How many orders may be open at once: `openOrders` (ADR 0217). The target repositories with an intake filter, in the order foedrum.jsonc names them. Whether check steps run without an OS sandbox: on native Windows only (ADR 0076). The brewers' base environment and the runner's forced variables (ADR 0028). Whether the machine is kept awake while an attempt runs (ADR 0195). The Brewery's event store: `.foedrum/index.db` in its root. api.github.com'; One batch at a time (ADR 0068). ADR 0052's interval. A reason's lines joined with spaces, as doctor prints it; brew's `oneLine` escapes them. `text` read against `schema`, or undefined with the problem added; also when it is missing. The models a brewer can resolve (ADR 0153): Foedrum's default `models` with the Brewery's over them, by alias, and the `brewers` of the Brewery's file only. Every `brewers` alias must have a model among the merged ones. Undefined, with the problems added, when a file does not pass. A default that does not load is Foedrum's defect, named by its defaults/ path (ADR 0098). What a command that needs the Brewery's name says when foedrum.jsonc has none. The host gh reaches GitHub on, with its own login, for `config`'s `githubApi` (ADR 0073). foedrum.jsonc's text read against its schema, for a command of the checkout `root`; throws with one line when the file is missing or does not pass. The user's clone of `repo` that .foedrum/local.jsonc names. The clone `repo`'s attempt worktrees are added to, from the text of foedrum.jsonc and .foedrum/local.jsonc: the user's for `source: local`, the managed one in the work root otherwise. Undefined when the files do not name it or do not read. Everything serve sets up, or one line per problem, all of them at once. Without the file, every default applies. Every brewer's alias has a model, so no attempt finds out only when it starts. Elsewhere a check runs in bwrap or sandbox-exec, or not at all (ADR 0076). This machine's word before the Brewery's (ADR 0195).

cards.comments: `foedrum serve` on the real machine (ADR 0063): reads the Brewery's files in the working directory, asks doctor for claude and the isolation level, and runs the Cellar (serve.ts) on the real machine (serve-shell.ts) with the real git until a stop signal. main.ts runs it; the tests call it with a fake or canned runner and PATH lookup, and the opt-in end-to-end test of test/integration/serve.test.ts runs it as the real program. How serve and brew find their starting facts: default the real runner and PATH. Serve's setup of the Brewery checkout `cwd` (ADR 0063, ADR 0123), or its problems. What `foedrum <command>` sets up from the Brewery checkout `cwd`, as serve does, or its refusal with one line per problem. This machine's way to stay awake while an attempt runs, found through `resolve`, and this process for the helper to watch (ADR 0195). Runs the Cellar in the Brewery checkout `cwd` until Ctrl+C. Its starting facts, gh's login among them, come through `exec` and `resolve`, default the real runner and PATH; a test gives fakes. The stop signals are listened for while serve runs, and no longer once it returns.

cards.summary: `foedrum serve`'s shell on the real machine (ADR 0063): the lock, the store, the state branch, each repository's attempt worktrees (a local clone, or a managed clone made from GitHub), the claude runner, and the signals that stop it. git comes in, so its use is tested with a fake.
cards.comments: `foedrum serve`'s shell on the real machine (ADR 0063): the lock, the store, the state branch, each repository's attempt worktrees (a local clone, or a managed clone made from GitHub), the claude runner, and the signals that stop it. git comes in, so its use is tested with a fake. The Brewery's checkout: the state branch's clone. Listens for a signal that stops serve; default `process.once`. The command whose lines the state branch's own start with; default `serve`. How this machine is kept awake while an attempt runs, and the process the helper watches (ADR 0195); absent, nothing holds it. The helper starts through `exec`, default `execProcess`. Where a process listens for signals: `process` itself. Listens for the stop signals while serve runs, until `stop`. `on`, not `once`: a second Ctrl+C or a closed terminal while serve shuts down would otherwise end the process before the driver stopped its runs. The repository on GitHub, where its pull request goes: every fetch, push and ls-remote reaches it by this URL, never through the clone's configuration, with Foedrum's own git directories for it under `workRoot` (ADR 0090, ADR 0096). github.com/${repo}.git`, A check reads the clone's objects only through a worktree of Foedrum's own git directories, which Foedrum alone writes (ADR 0203). A repository's setup installs, so its sandbox keeps the network (ADR 0158). Ctrl+C, a kill, a closed terminal, Ctrl+Break: each stops the runs through the driver, whose brewers lead process groups of their own that a terminal's signal does not reach. From the objects of the clone the worktrees are added to. In a git directory of its own with the clone's objects, as the base fetch (ADR 0198). A worktree of the merged tree from such a directory, for the checks on it (ADR 0203). In the worktree of the check attempt, git as the engine's calls in the clone (ADR 0137). A brewer attempt's setup runs before claude, in the setup's sandbox (ADR 0163). A check's command line runs in the OS sandbox (ADR 0076). The helper watches Foedrum's process, so a killed Foedrum lets the hold go (ADR 0195).

cards.summary: `foedrum serve`, the Cellar (ADR 0063): takes the driver lock `cellar`, opens the driver on the wiring it shares with `foedrum brew` (driver-wiring.ts), ticks it until Ctrl+C with the intake polling beside the ticks (ADR 0068), and closes it all again. The machine comes in through `ServeShell`; serve-main.ts gives it the real one.
cards.comments: `foedrum serve`, the Cellar (ADR 0063): takes the driver lock `cellar`, opens the driver on the wiring it shares with `foedrum brew` (driver-wiring.ts), ticks it until Ctrl+C with the intake polling beside the ticks (ADR 0068), and closes it all again. The machine comes in through `ServeShell`; serve-main.ts gives it the real one. The terminal `foedrum brew` keeps a live line on (ADR 0174). The terminal's width in characters, when it is known. Calls `handler` when the terminal is resized; the returned function stops it. Clears the current line and leaves the cursor at its start. Clears the current line and writes `text` on it, without a line feed. What serve needs from the machine. Prints one line. Aborts on Ctrl+C: serve stops after the tick underway. Waits `ms`, or less once `signal` aborts. Opens the event store at `path`, making it when missing. The attempt worktrees of a repository, making its managed clone first; `recreate` gives a resumed attempt the worktree its session ran in back (ADR 0117). The pushes of the openPullRequest action (ADR 0071), from the clone the repository's worktrees are added to: the user's, or the managed one. The merge of the base into the worktree of a batch's last check (ADR 0164), in the clone the repository's worktrees are added to. The merge-tree of an open pull request's head and its base's tip (ADR 0198), in the clone the repository's worktrees are added to; absent, no open pull request is checked. A worktree of an open pull request's merged tree, for the checks on it (ADR 0203), in a git directory of Foedrum's own with the clone's objects; absent, no checks run on one. The brewer runner: `claudeBrewerRunner` with `claude` and the plans. The process runner the check steps' commands run through (ADR 0069). The process runner a repository's setup runs through: the check sandbox, network kept (ADR 0158). The process runner gh runs through, for GitHub (ADR 0073). git, for the commits red proofs and the testsUnchanged guard read (ADR 0078). How long an intake pass may take; default half the batch lease (ADR 0050). How long between ticks; default 5 s, the supervisor's interval (ADR 0027). Holds the machine awake while an attempt runs (ADR 0195); absent, nothing does. Present only where `brew` keeps a live line (ADR 0174); `serve` never reads it. The supervisor's interval (ADR 0027). A command as a notice names it: its kind, and its batch when it has one. A driver's notice as one line. An intake's notice as one line (ADR 0068). The repositories whose open pull requests each intake pass checks against their base (ADR 0198): every one when the shell can merge-tree, which every git Foedrum runs on can (ADR 0200); else none. The checks on the merged tree, of a batch whose recipe has them (ADR 0203). Runs the Cellar until `shell.signal` aborts; the exit code: 0 stopped, 1 failed. Notices may carry text a model wrote: never a control character on the terminal. The lock first: a second Cellar is refused before it touches the store or the state branch. The Cellar takes every free batch (ADR 0044). A second writer on the store, as a terminal command is (ADR 0044). One run at a time in the Cellar, beside the ticks and the pass (ADR 0203), stopped on every way out of serve. GitHub's rate limit holds requests until then: no pass starts before it (ADR 0052). The pass underway, never awaited by a tick: a slow GitHub holds off no heartbeat (ADR 0068). Elsewhere a check runs in an OS sandbox of its own (ADR 0076). A setup runs before brewer attempts too, so also where no recipe has a check step (ADR 0163). Its deadline bounds the wait. A call the stop itself ended, such as gh reading the login at the start, is a stop. The run on a merged tree is stopped first; it and the pass underway write to the store until they settle. Closing the driver stops its runs and lets the lock go; without one, the lock goes here.

cards.summary: `foedrum status --watch` (ADR 0188): a board of the live batches, redrawn in place about once a second on a terminal, read from the Brewery's store as `foedrum status` reads it.
cards.comments: `foedrum status --watch` (ADR 0188): a board of the live batches, redrawn in place about once a second on a terminal, read from the Brewery's store as `foedrum status` reads it. What the board needs from the machine. The terminal the board is drawn on; none where `status --watch` is refused (ADR 0188). The Brewery's store, read and folded afresh: no lease, no git, no kept branches. Aborts on Ctrl+C or a stop. Waits `ms`, or less once `signal` aborts. How often the board is redrawn. Draws the board until `shell.signal` aborts, exit code 0; refuses, exit code 1, off a terminal. When this board first saw each running attempt run, as `brew` counts `seenAt`. The lines of the board of the store as `folded` holds it now, before they are fitted. A batch's row, led by its time, and a line under it for each attempt that runs. The header and the rows leave the last line of the terminal free; the attempts' lines go before any row does, and a row that does not fit is told as a count. On a terminal of two rows, only the first line fits. The last board of a store that read, which stays on screen while a read fails. A read that fails, such as a store busy while a driver writes, ends no watch: the last board stays, cut where it must be so that it and the line that says so fit in the height less one, and the next board reads again (ADR 0189). From a resize it would be uncaught. The last board stays on screen, and the prompt comes back on a line of its own.

cards.summary: `foedrum status`: every batch with its issue and lane (architecture §4.3), and what it is doing or waiting for, and what its attempts took. The lane's words are shared with replay.
cards.comments: `foedrum status`: every batch with its issue and lane (architecture §4.3), and what it is doing or waiting for, and what its attempts took. The lane's words are shared with replay. The latest attempt of each step that is still under way; an abandoned one never will be. A batch's lane, and what it is doing or waiting for there ('' when nothing). Who paused a batch, with the surface when `via`, and why, and when what still runs is stopped (ADR 0202). The issue a batch brews: `#<n>` in the Brewery, `<owner>/<name>#<n>` in a target repository. A batch's cells in `foedrum status`: its id, order, lane, and what it does, with the owner of an `interactive` driver that holds it (ADR 0123) and what its attempts took. What its attempts took, summed (ADR 0172), in ASCII: a pipe on Windows decodes the output with its code page. What `foedrum status` prints: one line per batch, in the order they were ordered, with the owner of an `interactive` driver that holds it (ADR 0123), then the `kept` lines of the task-tree branches the cleanup keeps (ADR 0092); above the board, the `held` lines of the limits that hold (ADR 0217). Above the board: each holds every batch's brewers, or those of its family (ADR 0206, ADR 0215), then each limit that holds what the intake starts (ADR 0217).

cards.summary: `foedrum stuck`: every Stuck batch with why, what it offers, and the questions it asks, numbered in the order `foedrum answer` takes their answers.
cards.comments: `foedrum stuck`: every Stuck batch with why, what it offers, and the questions it asks, numbered in the order `foedrum answer` takes their answers. The open findings a findings route that ran out of rounds left, one line each with secrets left out, and the recommendation to step back (ADR 0192); nothing for any other reason. What `foedrum stuck` prints: each Stuck batch, in the order they were ordered.

cards.summary: The guard before append: refuses events the fold would throw on, and the lifecycle and bottling rules the fold leaves out (architecture §4.1, §4.3, ADR 0013, ADR 0025). Pure: no clock or I/O.
cards.comments: The guard before append: refuses events the fold would throw on, and the lifecycle and bottling rules the fold leaves out (architecture §4.1, §4.3, ADR 0013, ADR 0025). Pure: no clock or I/O. What the command layer appends, or why it appends nothing. Accepts `events` when each one, folded onto `state` and the events before it, is valid and allowed in its batch's lane; otherwise refuses all of them, naming the first refused event. Checks one event against `state`: the state it leads to, or why it is refused. The lifecycle rules first: "batch b1 is ordered" says more than "step plan was never scheduled". Why `what` is refused in `batch`'s lane, or `undefined` when that lane is one of `allowed`. Says that `what` needs `batch` in one of the `allowed` lanes. Whether the fold holds `version` of `repo`, in any case (ADR 0223). Why `event` is not allowed in `state`, beyond what the fold checks; `undefined` when it is. Once per version, so two writers record a release once (ADR 0223). From on tap only back along the route of its open pull request (ADR 0219). Stuck on routing only before a recipe, and on a step only after one (ADR 0032). Stuck from on tap only on the checks of its pull request (ADR 0219). The fold refuses a continue of what is not paused; a pause holds any order (ADR 0202). decide refuses a rank of an order that left the queue (ADR 0208). The fold refuses an open of a window that is not closed (ADR 0206). A lane refusal for an event of a batch; a batch the log never ordered is the fold's to refuse. Whether a Stuck batch is stuck on routing as `routing` says; other lanes pass. A retry of a batch Stuck on routing sends it back to Ordered, so it needs a new routing deadline; every other resume goes on brewing and has none (ADR 0032). Only an attempt that no later attempt replaced, and that Stuck did not abandon, may start or finish. A rewind names the commit of each repository it resets; the batch of a sub-order or of a claimed target issue only its own. Whether `event` schedules a step of a batch on tap back along the route of its open pull request (ADR 0219). A batch records the end of a pull request it opened (on tap), waits for (Conditioning), or brews a fix of, Stuck or not (ADR 0219). A batch records how an open pull request it opened merges with its base (ADR 0198), and the checks on its head (ADR 0213). A record of the checks on a pull request's head says something new (ADR 0213): a pending record after anything but a pending one, a finished record whose checks differ from the latest. A pair of heads is recorded once on each batch (ADR 0230). A sub-order keeps its repository once it has batches: they, and their branches, live there. A bottle bundles finished sub-orders of its own repository (ADR 0013).

cards.summary: The canonical text of an attempt: the `attemptKey` of its lease (ADR 0027), so the supervisor can tell which attempt a lease holds.
cards.comments: The canonical text of an attempt: the `attemptKey` of its lease (ADR 0027), so the supervisor can tell which attempt a lease holds. One attempt of a step of a batch. Only the three parts: an attempt taken from a larger object may carry other fields. One attempt, one text: a lease under another spelling holds no attempt the engine knows. The JSON array `[batchId, stepId, attempt]`; throws when a part is invalid. The attempt of a canonical text, or `undefined` for any other text.

cards.summary: The check of the Brewery's open pull requests when their base moves (ADR 0198): each intake pass reads each base's tip as the push's own fetch reads it (ADR 0090), merge-trees the pull request's head against a tip that moved since its last check of that head (ADR 0226), and records what it found. A conflict is posted on the pull request through the ledger when it first appears or its files change, and a check that fails on the merged tree when it first fails (ADR 0209), which sends the batch back to its fix step when its recipe has the route (ADR 0226).
cards.comments: The check of the Brewery's open pull requests when their base moves (ADR 0198): each intake pass reads each base's tip as the push's own fetch reads it (ADR 0090), merge-trees the pull request's head against a tip that moved since its last check of that head (ADR 0226), and records what it found. A conflict is posted on the pull request through the ledger when it first appears or its files change, and a check that fails on the merged tree when it first fails (ADR 0209), which sends the batch back to its fix step when its recipe has the route (ADR 0226). What a merge-tree of a pull request's head and its base's tip came to. A repository whose open pull requests are checked against its base. The branch the pull requests go into, as the remote names it (`main`). The commit the remote's `base` points at now (`BranchPush.baseTip`, ADR 0090). How `head` and `tip`, both full shas the clone has, merge. The commit the remote's bottle branch `branch` points at now (`BranchPush.remoteTip`), or `undefined` when it has no such branch. The run of the checks on the merged tree (ADR 0203): whether `batch` has checks to run, and the hand-off of a clean merge, which the pass then does not record. What it could not do: a tip it could not read, a merge-tree that failed, a refused record. The tip the pull request `url` of `batch` was last checked against on `head`, the latest push's: its latest check of that head, else the base the batch's latest merge read (ADR 0164, ADR 0226); `undefined` when neither is recorded. One pass: checks every open pull request whose base moved, and records each check. Each base's tip once per pass; `undefined` when it could not be read. Each batch as the log has it now: other writers append beside the pass (ADR 0044). A repository without a base check: nothing to check it with. A bottle branch someone else pushed to holds what Foedrum never read: recorded once, and checked no more (ADR 0198). Gone: the pull request is closing, and its end is recorded next pass. A pass given up at its deadline records nothing more. A clean merge with checks to run is the merged-check run's to record (ADR 0203). The checks of `batch` that post a comment, each with its number from 1 (ADR 0198): a conflict of a pull request whose check before it was clean, or none, or conflicted in other files. The files of each pull request's check before, as one text; '' when it was clean. A check of a pull request whose run on the merged tree failed (ADR 0203). The checks of `batch` whose run on the merged tree posts a comment, each with its number from 1 (ADR 0209): a failure of a pull request whose check before it was clean, conflicted, unchecked, failed another check, or none. A check is the one the status line names (`checkOf`). The check each pull request's check before failed; '' when it failed none. A post's comment without its marker: the batch's heading, `body`, and what the batch does: it stays On tap, or with `rounds` Foedrum sends it back to `fix` it (ADR 0226, ADR 0244). The comment a conflict posts, without its marker. `text` in a fenced code block whose fence is longer than any run of backticks in it, each `<!--` opened as `<!- -`: a marker a check printed would let a later post be found as posted (ADR 0033). The comment a failure on the merged tree posts, without its marker. Its tail is the one recorded, already cut and with the lines that look like a secret left out (`readingOf`, ADR 0209). The Brewery's recipes: a batch whose recipe has the route back is fixed (ADR 0226). How long one effect may take; the driver's default when left out (`DriverEffects`). The rounds the recipe of `batch` gives a pull request that failed, when it has the route back (ADR 0219); `undefined` when it stays On tap. A step its when skipped runs no round: the batch goes Stuck instead (ADR 0219). The comment on the pull request each post calls for, a conflict's (ADR 0198) or a failure's on the merged tree (ADR 0209), for the driver: due while the batch is on tap, or brews or is Stuck after its pull request sent it back (ADR 0226), and the pull request has no recorded end, found by its marker on the Brewery's own comment (ADR 0033). The comment behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key. On tap, or brewing or Stuck after a failure sent it back from the pull request: a tick that sent it back before the post loses no post (ADR 0226). Stuck on its pull request from on tap too, when no round ran (ADR 0219).

cards.summary: The merge of the base before a batch's last check (ADR 0164): the base as the remote has it now, fetched as the push fetches it (ADR 0090), merged into the check attempt's worktree as a commit of its own, through the ledger, so the checks read the code the pull request will hold and a kill on either side of the merge never merges twice (I4).
cards.comments: The merge of the base before a batch's last check (ADR 0164): the base as the remote has it now, fetched as the push fetches it (ADR 0090), merged into the check attempt's worktree as a commit of its own, through the ledger, so the checks read the code the pull request will hold and a kill on either side of the merge never merges twice (I4). What a merge in a worktree came to: its commit, or the files it conflicts in, aborted, or kept in progress with the files it left unmerged (ADR 0244). A merge in progress in a worktree: the commit it merges, and the files still unmerged. git in an attempt's worktree. Every call stops when `signal` aborts. The commit the worktree's HEAD is at. The parents of `commit`, full shas, in order. Aborts a merge a killed run left in progress; nothing when none is. The merge in progress in the worktree, with the files still unmerged; none when none is. Merges `commit` into HEAD as a commit of its own with `message`; on a conflict, the files it conflicts in, with the merge aborted, or with `keep` the merge left in progress with the files it left unmerged (ADR 0244). How a repository's check attempts merge its base. The branch the pull request goes into, as the remote names it (`main`). The push's fetch of the base and its ancestor check (ADR 0090). The ledger's effect name of the merge before a check attempt (ADR 0164). The files a kept merge left unmerged, as the ledger names them: at most `MAX_CONFLICTS`. The merge into the worktree at `path`, which the attempt of `stepId` started at `start`: found when HEAD is a merge of `start` and a commit of the base, which a run killed before it recorded the merge made; a merge such a run left in progress is aborted, and found as nothing. With `keep`, at the start of a routed fix (ADR 0244), a conflict is left in progress for the brewer, and a merge in progress is kept and found with the files still unmerged, never aborted; a HEAD that moved past `start` otherwise, as a resumed worktree's may, is merged into again from HEAD. A merge in progress has not moved HEAD. Every commit of the base is in the attempt's start, or in a resumed worktree's HEAD, already: nothing to merge. The route that makes attempt `ref` of `batch` merge the base at its start: a `pull_request` route with a cause, a failing check on the pull request's merged tree (ADR 0226) or its conflict with the base (ADR 0244), of it or of the attempt it retries or answers. A retry, or an answer that starts fresh, starts as the attempt before it did (ADR 0117, ADR 0118). Whether attempt `ref` of `batch` merges the base at its start, keeping a conflict (ADR 0244). What the ledger recorded of the merge at the start of attempt `ref`, when it is one it records. Why a `done` of an attempt whose start merge kept a conflict (`result`) fails (ADR 0244): the merge is still in progress in the worktree at `path`, or its HEAD does not hold the tip, the merge aborted; `undefined` once the brewer concluded it, or when the merge kept none. Named as the ledger names them: at most MAX_CONFLICTS, and how many more. How the attempt ends when its merge's `result` stops it: blocked on a divergence when it conflicts, since another round would hit the same conflict; `undefined` when the attempt runs. Whether a success in the worktree attempt `number` of `step` ran in concluded what it did there: of that attempt, or of any that resumed its session in that worktree (ADR 0244, ADR 0117). A worktree is named by the attempt that made it, which every resume of its session runs in. The base the latest merge of `batchId` brought in, when one made a commit: where the batch's own change starts once its task tree holds that merge, so a review of the change never reads what the base added while the batch brewed (ADR 0164). `undefined` when nothing was merged. A kept merge counts once a success in its worktree concluded it (ADR 0244). The merges the ledger recorded before the attempts of `batchId`, in the order it recorded them, each with its attempt; a result that is no merge is passed over.

cards.summary: Ids of the batches the engine orders. They become folder names on the state branch, so they must pass PathSafeId (ADR 0024): `<issue>-<n>` is digits and one hyphen, at most 33 characters, and `<alias>-<issue>[-<n>]` of a target-repository issue starts with a letter, at most 54 (ADR 0050).
cards.comments: Ids of the batches the engine orders. They become folder names on the state branch, so they must pass PathSafeId (ADR 0024): `<issue>-<n>` is digits and one hyphen, at most 33 characters, and `<alias>-<issue>[-<n>]` of a target-repository issue starts with a letter, at most 54 (ADR 0050). The id of the next batch of `issue`: `<issue>-<n>`, with the first `n` no batch uses yet. The id of the next batch of `issue` in the target repository named `alias`: `<alias>-<issue>`, or `<alias>-<issue>-<n>` from 2 when a batch of the issue has that already. The alias a claimed issue's batch id starts with, as `targetBatchId` makes it, or undefined for any other id: the alias has no hyphen, so it ends at the first one (ADR 0050).

cards.summary: One driver per batch at a time (ADR 0019): the driver that drives a batch holds its lease and renews it as its heartbeat. Another driver skips a batch whose lease is alive; an expired lease frees it. The driver renews it, never the brewer runner, so a lease stops when its driver does, even while an orphaned brewer process runs on.
cards.comments: One driver per batch at a time (ADR 0019): the driver that drives a batch holds its lease and renews it as its heartbeat. Another driver skips a batch whose lease is alive; an expired lease frees it. The driver renews it, never the brewer runner, so a lease stops when its driver does, even while an orphaned brewer process runs on. Whether the driver holds the batch now, or which other driver does. The driver's owner (its lock's). How long the lease lasts from `now`. Takes the lease of a batch for `owner`, or renews it, until `now + leaseMs`, unless another owner's lease is alive at `now`. In a transaction, so two drivers cannot both take it. Lets the lease of `batchId` go when `owner` holds it; another owner's lease stays. How long a batch's or an attempt's lease lasts between renewals by default: 5 minutes. A person's handover of a batch to the driver `owner` (ADR 0124). The driver it hands the batch to. How long the new owner's lease lasts from `now`. The step whose session the new owner resumes: the old one stops its run (ADR 0127). Hands `batchId` from the driver whose live lease holds it to `owner`, and records the handover (ADR 0124): the lease is read, and given, in the transaction that appends.

cards.summary: The environment of a brewer's process (#81, brewers-and-recipes §1.1): a minimal base, the brewer's own `env` on top, and the runner's forced variables last, so a brewer cannot undo them.
cards.comments: The environment of a brewer's process (#81, brewers-and-recipes §1.1): a minimal base, the brewer's own `env` on top, and the runner's forced variables last, so a brewer cannot undo them. The minimal base, never the engine's own `process.env`. The brewer's frontmatter `env`. The runner's variables (`PATH`, `npm_config_ignore_scripts`, the per-attempt settings). Windows does not tell names apart by case; the other platforms do. What a process needs to start on each platform, and where claude keeps its login. Where claude finds Git Bash on Windows when it is not where claude looks by default. The minimal base of `serve`'s brewers, from its own environment: what a process needs to start and what claude needs to find its login, never a GitHub token (ADR 0063). By key, as buildBrewerEnv merges: on Windows `Path` is `PATH`. What git reads after every configuration file (ADR 0109): no credential helper and no askpass program, wherever the user's or the clone's configuration set them (an empty helper clears the list), no cookie file, no empty login for Negotiate, and every transport refused but local paths, as git allows them by default, git, http and https, so neither ssh nor a remote helper can reach a key or a login. git reads these variables since 2.31; doctor requires 2.38 (ADR 0200). The runner's forced variables (brewers-and-recipes §1.1): npm runs no lifecycle script, and git holds no credential that lets a push succeed and never prompts for one (ADR 0109), and claude neither updates itself nor sends telemetry, error reports or feature-flag requests (ADR 0177). The layers merged in order; a later layer replaces a name of an earlier one. By key, so on Windows a later `PATH` replaces an earlier `Path`, spelling included.

cards.summary: The brewer runner (ADR 0003): starts an attempt, reports its progress to the supervisor, and ends it with a typed outcome (ADR 0005). The real runner drives the `claude` CLI; tests use a fake. Both turn what the process did into the outcome through settleAttempt, so the rules are shared.
cards.comments: The brewer runner (ADR 0003): starts an attempt, reports its progress to the supervisor, and ends it with a typed outcome (ADR 0005). The real runner drives the `claude` CLI; tests use a fake. Both turn what the process did into the outcome through settleAttempt, so the rules are shared. What the runner enforces for one attempt and where the brewer reports its outcome. The out doc the brewer must write (`output.doc`), and the schema of its frontmatter. Turns the brewer may take; the runner stops it on the first turn past them: its budget is exceeded. Permission denials before the runner stops the brewer: it is blocked by its environment. For a brewer that produces commits: the commit its worktree started at. A `done` out doc then needs a commit after it (ADR 0074). For a Gauger a failed red proof of its step sent back, in that round: a `done` that names its tests needs no commit, since the tests it committed before may only have lacked their names (ADR 0258). For a Taster's blocking step: a `done` with the verdict `changes` is blocked by findings (ADR 0161). The driver can resume the attempt's session: a claude step with a worktree manager that recreates worktrees. A run past `maxTurns` after claude's init then fails retryably (ADR 0175). How an attempt ended, with the tokens it used when the stream reported them. What the attempt took, when the runner read its stream (ADR 0172). What a check step read, one per check (ADR 0069); a brewer's attempt, its repository's setup's when it has one (ADR 0163). The house-yeast rules the attempt's plan gave it (ADR 0169). The session claude set up, when its init matched what was asked (ADR 0046, ADR 0047). The out doc's text as the runner read it, valid or not; model output, which the state branch keeps and nothing follows (ADR 0103). Settles once with how the attempt ended. Stops the brewer's process tree (deadline, stall, cancel, or an attempt abandoned when its batch got Stuck); `ended` then settles as cancelled. Does nothing once the attempt ended. Runs brewer attempts; `progress` reports each running one to the supervisor (ADR 0027). How the brewer's process ended. Ended by a signal the runner did not send. The runner stopped it: a limit was reached, or the engine stopped the attempt. The process could not be started at all (the CLI is missing, the settings could not be written). The runner stopped it because its output passed a limit: a stream line, or stderr. What git said of the commits an attempt made after its worktree's start (ADR 0074). The start commit is no ancestor of HEAD: the brewer rewrote it. git could not answer. What the push's secret scan found in an attempt's commits after its start (ADR 0187): no finding when they may go on. git could not answer. A usage window of claude's subscription that ran out, as claude named it (ADR 0091): which limit, and its reset as claude wrote it (`3:45pm`, `Mon 12:00am`). A spend limit or a credit balance that refuses every request until a human acts (ADR 0129): which spend limit claude named, or a credit balance that is too low. What the runner saw of one attempt. Why claude did not set up the session the runner asked for: its init event (tools, permission mode, MCP servers, skills; the runner stops the attempt when it sees it), a result before init, a lasting error before the first model reply, or refused arguments (ADR 0046, ADR 0047). Why claude could not resume the session the runner asked it to: a result before init when it resumes one, as when the transcript is gone. The next attempt starts fresh (ADR 0117). The out doc's text, or `undefined` when the brewer did not write it. Why the result event reported an error (`is_error`, ADR 0042), when it did. The usage window the error result said ran out, in one of the documented messages. The spend limit or credit balance the error result said refused it, as documented. Why the runner did not read the out doc it found (larger than its limit, not a file). The first line of the event stream that was not a stream-json event. Permission denials in the event stream, every one counted. The tools denied, each once, in the order they were first denied (ADR 0006: named). Turns the brewer took. Whether claude's init report came, so the session it set up can be resumed (ADR 0175). The commits since the limits' `commitsSince`, when they name one. The permission denials of an attempt so far. The denials after one more of `tool`: counted always, its name kept once. Each name once, so a storm of the same denial cannot grow the list. How much of a garbage line a reason quotes: the stream is untrusted and may be huge. A `done` of a brewer that produces commits, by what git said of its commits after `since` (ADR 0074): without one its work never reached the task tree, so a human sees why, unless a Finer says there was nothing to simplify (ADR 0166), or a Gauger its red proof sent back (`namesOnly`) names its tests (ADR 0258). The tests it committed before may only have lacked their names, which the next red proof reads. Not retried: a brewer that found nothing to change would find it again. Why no request goes through, and what a human does before a retry. The outcome of an attempt from what the runner saw, the first rule that applies winning: a limit the runner enforced, then how the process ended, then the stream, then the out doc (ADR 0005: a missing or invalid out doc is a failure, never success). Another attempt would meet the same environment; a human must fix it (ADR 0046). claude refuses every request until the window resets: another attempt now would be refused too, so the engine holds the brewers until the reset claude named (ADR 0091, ADR 0206). Nothing resets by itself: no request goes through until a human acts (ADR 0129). The session it resumes is gone: the next attempt starts a fresh one. After the limits, which a fresh attempt would meet too (ADR 0117). Another attempt would hit the same wall (brewers-and-recipes §1.1). The human needs to know what

The Brewery's recipes; throws doctor's message when its files are not valid. The Brewery's house-yeast rule files (ADR 0169): the `.md` files directly in `house-yeast/`, and those in `house-yeast/<owner>/<name>/` for the repositories whose rules the Brewery keeps (ADR 0018), by their path from the Brewery's root. The folders directly in `folder` of `root`, by name; none when it cannot be listed. readFolder names a house-yeast/ it cannot list; a missing folder has no rules.

cards.summary: The claim marks and the release of a claimed target-repository issue as the driver's effects (ADR 0043, #103). What is due comes from the recorded events alone: the batch's lane, and the end of each of its pull requests that the intake recorded (`pull_request.ended`). Nothing here asks the code host whether a pull request merged. Each effect is found by its key before it is applied (ADR 0033), and the driver holds it to its deadline (#130). The Brewery issue that is the claimed issue's order is opened, and closed with a merge, the same way (ADR 0144).
cards.comments: The claim marks and the release of a claimed target-repository issue as the driver's effects (ADR 0043, #103). What is due comes from the recorded events alone: the batch's lane, and the end of each of its pull requests that the intake recorded (`pull_request.ended`). Nothing here asks the code host whether a pull request merged. Each effect is found by its key before it is applied (ADR 0033), and the driver holds it to its deadline (#130). The Brewery issue that is the claimed issue's order is opened, and closed with a merge, the same way (ADR 0144). The code host side of an issue's marks, as the Brewery's own identity sees and makes them. Every call stops when `signal` aborts. The logins the issue is assigned to. The names of the issue's labels. The id of a comment on the issue that carries `marker` and that the Brewery's own identity made, or undefined: a comment by anyone else never counts, since keys are predictable. Comments on the issue; the new comment's id. The issue's title. Whether the issue is open or closed, or gone: a person deleted it (ADR 0144). An issue that cannot be read for any other reason fails. Closes or reopens the issue. The number of an issue of `repo` that carries `marker` and that the Brewery's own identity opened, or undefined (ADR 0144). Opens an issue in `repo`; its number. The hidden marker that carries an effect's key in a comment, so `findComment` finds it. How long one effect may take; the driver's default when left out (`DriverEffects`). The id the code host answered for a comment or an issue, which the ledger keeps for good. The id the code host answered for a comment, checked: a positive integer, or it throws. Where `effect` lands: found by being there, by its key in our own comment, or by a gone ref. Gone: released by a run before, or by hand; nothing is left to release. Found by its key in an issue of the Brewery its own identity opened. Only the title is copied: the target issue's text stays where it is (ADR 0144). Gone: a person deleted the Brewery issue; nothing is left to close or reopen, and a failing effect would hold off the rest of the release (ADR 0144). The claim effects of every batch of a claimed target issue, for the driver: the marks while the batch is live or a pull request of it has no recorded end, the release once it is cancelled or every pull request it opened has a recorded end (`claimEffectsDue`). The effect behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key.

cards.summary: The Brewery issue that is the order of a claimed target-repository issue (ADR 0144). The driver opens it as an effect of the batch, so its number is what the ledger recorded for that effect; a batch that orders the issue again has the Brewery issue an earlier batch of it opened. Pure: everything here is read from the folded state.
cards.comments: The Brewery issue that is the order of a claimed target-repository issue (ADR 0144). The driver opens it as an effect of the batch, so its number is what the ledger recorded for that effect; a batch that orders the issue again has the Brewery issue an earlier batch of it opened. Pure: everything here is read from the folded state. The Brewery issue the batch opened, as the ledger recorded it; a result that is no issue number never names one. A person deleted the Brewery issue, as the batch's reopen or close found it. The batch's own Brewery issue, given the one the batches before it left (`earlier`). The Brewery issue the batch leaves for the next batch of its issue. The Brewery issue of the claimed batch `batchId`; none for a batch of a Brewery issue. The batches of the issue before this one, in the order they were ordered. The latest claimed batch whose order is the Brewery issue `issue`, or undefined. The Brewery issue each claimed issue has so far, by `<repo in lower case>#<issue>`: one pass. The Brewery issue that routes a batch and shows its status comment and lane label: a Brewery issue's batch's own, and a claimed batch's order once the ledger records it, never the target issue's number (ADR 0155, ADR 0156). Whether `batch` is the latest batch of the Brewery issue `issue`, the one that labels it. A claimed batch's target issue as `<alias>#<n>`, or `owner/name#<n>` when its id has no alias. How `status` and `stuck` name a batch's issue: `#<n>` for a Brewery issue, `#<order> (<alias>#<n>)` for a claimed one, and `<alias>#<n>` until its Brewery issue is opened.

cards.summary: The one way the command layer appends (ADR 0019, ADR 0025): a command is decided against every event committed so far, inside the write transaction that appends its events, so a second writer on the same store (another driver, a terminal command) can never make it decide on a stale state.
cards.comments: The one way the command layer appends (ADR 0019, ADR 0025): a command is decided against every event committed so far, inside the write transaction that appends its events, so a second writer on the same store (another driver, a terminal command) can never make it decide on a stale state. Time between Conditioning and Stuck reminders: 2 days (architecture §4.3). How long an Ordered batch may wait to be routed: 1 hour (ADR 0032). Default `defaultReminderMs`. Default `defaultRoutingMs`. A command, or what makes one from the reads of the transaction that appends it, such as a batch lease (ADR 0124): the command, or why there is none. The folded state of every event committed so far. Decides `command` at `now` against every event committed so far and appends its events with `also`'s writes, in one transaction. A refused command appends nothing and `also` does not run. The folded state, caught up with whatever was committed since it was last read. The write transaction holds the store's write lock from its start, so what it reads first is every committed event, and nothing else is appended before its own events.

How long the text of a comment may be: below GitHub's 65,536 characters for a comment, with room for its marker, and for a merge brief's title. Escaping can make each text a brewer wrote five times as long, so the caps on those texts alone do not keep it there. `text` cut to whole lines below `longestComment`, so no escape or entity is cut in half. The latest revision of `batchId` recorded, if any, and the number of the next. The target that applies the revisions `due` registers, on `brewery`'s issues: an edit of the comment the previous revision made, or a new comment before the first or once that one is gone; `done` hears of each revision it applied or found. The revision behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key. Checked: the id comes from the code host, and the ledger keeps it. The comment that already shows the revision of `key`, by the text before its marker. Still there: a run before would have edited it, not made another. The first revision, or the comment was deleted by hand: it is made again.

cards.summary: The batch state machine: the core of the command layer (architecture §4.3, ADR 0019, ADR 0025). It takes the folded state and one command, and returns the events to append or a refusal. Pure: the caller passes the time, and the recipes through a small interface.
cards.comments: The batch state machine: the core of the command layer (architecture §4.3, ADR 0019, ADR 0025). It takes the folded state and one command, and returns the events to append or a refusal. Pure: the caller passes the time, and the recipes through a small interface. Who issued a human command, and from where (ADR 0019). The commands a human issues, mostly to get a Stuck batch moving again. `shas`: the commit of each repository at `toStepId`, by `owner/name`. A new batch of an issue a person orders by hand (`foedrum order`, ADR 0105): refused while the issue has a live batch, while its last claim is held or being released, or when it is a sub-order (`orderRefusal`). Hands the batch from the driver `from`, whose live lease runs `until`, to the driver `to` (ADR 0124); the caller reads that lease in the transaction that appends. How an attempt ended: a step outcome, or a brewer's `blocked` out doc with its blocker kind, and for a blocking Taster's `changes` its findings (ADR 0192). The usage window claude said ran out, on an end blocked on the environment (ADR 0206). Events the engine records as they happen; they decide nothing about a batch's lane. The commands the engine issues itself: the drivers and the supervisor. A new batch of an order or sub-order, Ordered until it is routed by its deadline (ADR 0032). A check step's gravity readings (ADR 0069), or a brewer's setup's (ADR 0163). What claude reported in its init event, when it came (ADR 0116). What a brewer's attempt took, once its stream was read (ADR 0172). The house-yeast rules the attempt's plan gave it (ADR 0169). The driver stopped it when its batch's pause reached its stopAt (ADR 0202). When the usage window its `usageLimit` names reopens, as the driver read the reset, and whether it could (ADR 0206). The supervisor found the attempt past its deadline (invariant I5). The supervisor found the lease of a running attempt expired: its process is lost (ADR 0027). The runner reported no progress for the recipe's stall limit (ADR 0027). The supervisor found an Ordered batch past its routing deadline (ADR 0032). The supervisor found a Conditioning or Stuck reminder due. A driver that opens no session met the scheduled attempt of an interactive step: the batch waits for a person to run it (ADR 0222). The supervisor found the closed usage window's reopen due (ADR 0206). The supervisor found the batch's open pull request failed on `head`, the commit of its latest push: the batch goes back along its recipe's onPullRequestFail route, or Stuck (ADR 0219). What is wrong with an open pull request that sends its batch back: failed checks on its head (ADR 0219), a failing check on its merged tree with the base at `tip` (ADR 0226), or a conflict with the base at `tip` (ADR 0244). A person's pause of an order, or with no `order` of the whole Brewery and its intake, and its lifting (ADR 0202). `stopAt`: when what still runs is stopped, and the zone it was given in. A person's stop of an order (ADR 0205): each of its brewing batches goes Stuck at once. A person's rank of an order of the intake's queue (ADR 0208); later the Innkeeper's (#227). `place`: marked "finish first", or a position kept as the arrival of the order that was there. How long a Conditioning or Stuck batch waits before the next reminder, in milliseconds. How long an Ordered batch may wait to be routed, in milliseconds (ADR 0032). The options a Stuck batch offers for `reason`. No step yet to skip, answer or rewind to: route it again, choose a recipe, or cancel it. The events `command` appends to `state`, or why it is refused. Why a command is refused; `decide` returns it as a refusal. The events decided so far, each checked against the state the ones before it lead to. `ms` from now, as the events write times. The intake's claim of a target issue waits on the code host between its read and this order, so `foedrum order` may have ordered the issue in between (ADR 0105). pause --all holds the intake: nothing is ordered or claimed (ADR 0202). Back to Ordered, for the intake to route again by a new deadline (ADR 0032). Back along the route once more: a person's round past its rounds (ADR 0219). A skip of a child skips the rest of its group (ADR 0168). Why a person may not order `order` again now (ADR 0105), or undefined: the issue is a sub-order, which its decomposition orders, or `busy` says why. Its batches are the claimed issue's, which a new claim orders again (ADR 0144). Why the issue of `order` may not get a new batch now, or undefined: one of its batches is live, or the claim of a target issue's batch is still held or being released. A new claim made before that release would lose its ref to it. Refuses `order` for `why`, unless `batchId` was ordered before: the fold says so instead. Records how the attempt ended, and moves the batch on as its recipe routes the ending. A blocked out doc is a final failure of its attempt; the blocker kind routes it below. A blocking Taster's findings, which no other event keeps unless its rounds run out (ADR 0221). The window is the subscription's, whatever becomes of this step. An end refused because its batch left brewing closes nothing: the next brewer meets the limit and closes it (ADR 0206). A pause is a person's choice and a usage limit the subscription's wait, no failure: the step runs again whatever attempts it has left, after the reopen for a usage limit. The next round, until the route's rounds are used up (brewers-and-recipes §2). A child's verdict waits for its group's other children (ADR 0168). Another round would hit the same wall, or the plan does not match reality. Makes the batch Stuck when `stepId` is no longer in its recipe: the file was changed under the batch (a step renamed or removed), so the recipe cannot say where it goes next. Another attempt at `stepId` while it has some left, then (when `routed`) the `onFail` route back, then Stuck. An attempt a pause stopped counts against no retry (ADR 0202). cards.summary: One Brewery per work root, and one process per driver (ADR 0037). The work root records the Brewery it belongs to, and every driver of that Brewery (the Cellar, each interactive session) holds a lock of its own there, which the operating system releases when its process dies. On macOS and Linux the lock is an fcntl lock, which belongs to the process, not to the file handle: closing any handle to the file drops every lock the process holds on it. So nothing in Foedrum may open drivers/*.lock except lockDriver; another open and close in the same process, even a read, would free the lock while the driver still runs.
cards.comments: One Brewery per work root, and one process per driver (ADR 0037). The work root records the Brewery it belongs to, and every driver of that Brewery (the Cellar, each interactive session) holds a lock of its own there, which the operating system releases when its process dies.
