A driver's held lock; `held` turns false once it is released. The driver keeps this object for its whole run: the lock lives in the SQLite database it holds, and garbage collection of that database would close it and free the lock. The driver's owner: the name its leases carry, the same across its restarts. The lock file. Releases the lock; does nothing once released. `owner/name` of the Brewery repository. A path segment: `cellar`, or a session's id that the session keeps when it is resumed. This process; recorded with the lock for the refusal message only. Default `process.pid`. Default the system clock. How long to wait for a lock that another process holds before refusing; default 2 s, since Windows may free the lock of a process that died a little late. The work root belongs to another Brewery. Another process runs this driver: its lock is taken. Windows may free the lock of a process that died a little after the process is gone. Claims the work root for the Brewery, or checks that it is the Brewery's. The marker is made whole next to its place and linked in, so it appears complete and only once, whoever is first. A BOM or CRLF from an editor is fine; anything but exactly a Brewery is not. GitHub names are case-insensitive. Only for a refusal's message: a holder file that is missing or broken names no one. Takes the lock of driver `owner` of `brewery` on the work root, creating the work root when missing. Throws `OtherBreweryError` when the work root is another Brewery's, and `DriverRunningError` when a live process holds the driver's lock. A lock whose process died is free: its file lock died with it, so it is taken over without any cleanup. A SQLite database in exclusive locking mode (takeFileLock): no stale lock to detect, and no pid that a new process may reuse. A held lock is waited for `waitMs`. Written under the lock, for the message a refused driver shows; nothing decides by it. When it cannot be written, the lock goes too: no handle would be left to release it. The lock first: a holder file a scanner keeps busy must not keep the lock taken. A process that takes the lock in between may lose its holder file here; that only leaves its name out of a refusal's message. The next holder overwrites it.

cards.summary: What a driver does when it starts on a store, before it takes new work (ADR 0033, ADR 0037).
cards.comments: What a driver does when it starts on a store, before it takes new work (ADR 0033, ADR 0037). The driver's lock (`lockDriver`), held for as long as the driver runs; it names the owner. The attempt keys of the leases its earlier run left, now expired. What the crash repair of the attempt worktrees did. Expires the leases of the driver's earlier run, then repairs the attempt worktrees with the claims that are left. Throws, changing nothing, when the lock is not held. Only the holder of the driver's lock may expire its owner's leases: a second process with the same owner would otherwise expire the live leases of the first (ADR 0037). First the leases: the attempts of the earlier run died with it, so they claim no worktree.

cards.summary: A driver (ADR 0019): the Cellar or an interactive session. It takes its lock and starts on the store before any work (ADR 0037), holds the lease of every batch it drives and renews it on every tick (the driver, never the brewer runner), starts the scheduled attempts of those batches on a brewer runner, finishes them as they end, runs the supervisor over its own batches and the free ones, and applies a batch's effects only while it holds the batch's lease (ADR 0033).
cards.comments: A driver (ADR 0019): the Cellar or an interactive session. It takes its lock and starts on the store before any work (ADR 0037), holds the lease of every batch it drives and renews it on every tick (the driver, never the brewer runner), starts the scheduled attempts of those batches on a brewer runner, finishes them as they end, runs the supervisor over its own batches and the free ones, and applies a batch's effects only while it holds the batch's lease (ADR 0033). The effects the driver applies, and where they land. The effects that the recorded events of `batchId` call for (ADR 0033). How long one effect may take before the driver gives it up and aborts it: whole milliseconds below `leaseMs`, half of it by default. The lease is renewed before each effect, not during one, so a slower effect could let a second driver start it too (ADR 0044, #130). The actions the engine runs itself, never a brewer (ADR 0071): an attempt of an action step is started by the driver, applies its effects through the ledger, and ends once none is left. The effects the started action attempt `ref` calls for, in the order they apply. How `ref` ends, once every effect it called for is in the ledger. The attempt worktrees of a repository the attempts write in, and the base a batch starts at until its task tree moves (ADR 0066). A manager without `recreate` resumes no session: its retries start fresh (ADR 0117). How an attempt of a step that merges the base merges it before it runs (ADR 0164); without it, nothing is merged. What the driver reports instead of failing: it keeps driving. Another driver holds a batch this driver held; it starts nothing more there. Applying an effect failed; the batch's other effects wait for the next pass. The runner's end of an attempt rejected: the attempt is blocked on its environment, and the other runs go on (ADR 0099). `ref` is scheduled but waits until `waitsFor`, another attempt of its step, lets go of its live lease, which expires at `expiresAt` unless renewed (ADR 0055); said once per attempt (#155). What a cleanup of an ended batch's worktrees did. Takes the driver's lock: `lockDriver` on the Brewery's work root (ADR 0037). Whether the driver takes a batch that no other driver holds: every one for the Cellar, the batch it brews for an interactive session. The limits of an attempt: its brewer's, from the recipe its batch brews. The out doc of a step's brewer, which the worktree cleanup lets go (ADR 0081). The attempt worktrees of each repository the attempts write in, and their base. Whether an attempt runs a brewer, in a Claude Code session the driver chooses and records with its worktree (ADR 0116): every attempt with a worktree by default; `serve` leaves out its check steps. Whether the brewer of an attempt resumes the session of the attempt before it on a retry or an answer (`retryMode: resume`, ADR 0117, ADR 0118); never by default. `foedrum serve` and `foedrum brew` ask the brewer of the attempt's step. The model family a brewer attempt runs on, to know which closed usage window holds it (ADR 0215); undefined, which every closed window holds, by default. The IANA time zone claude's usage-limit reset is read in (ADR 0206); default the machine's. The id of a new session; default `randomUUID`. Which of the batches its owner held at its start it drives on (ADR 0044): every one by default. An interactive driver keeps none, so a batch it left earlier lapses within a lease instead of being driven beside the one it brews (ADR 0123); it holds that one through `takes`. Whether it goes on with a batch it may hold: claims it, starts its attempts and applies its effects. Every batch by default; `foedrum resume` of a running batch lets its batch be once the attempt that continues the session has ended, for the driver that takes it next (ADR 0127). Whether it opens an interactive step's session (ADR 0222): `foedrum brew` on a terminal. A driver that opens none, by default, parks such a step's attempt Stuck, waiting for a session. What else goes with an ended batch's worktrees: its attempt settings (ADR 0063). The actions it runs itself (ADR 0071). Without them, an attempt of an action step is blocked on its environment at its start. How long a batch's or an attempt's lease lasts between renewals; default 5 minutes. Default 2 days. Default 1 hour. The driver's owner, its lock's: the name its leases carry. What its start did: the leases of its earlier run that expired, and the worktree repair. The batches it holds, by id. Starts the scheduled attempts of the batches it holds or takes, and finishes the ended ones. Renews its leases, runs a supervisor tick, stops the attempts that Stuck abandoned or whose batch ended, drives on, applies the effects due, and lets go of the batches that are done. Applies the effects due of the batches it holds or takes; one pass at a time. The folded state of every committed event. What the runner reports of the running attempt `ref`, for display (ADR 0174). Stops the runs it still has and lets its lock go; its batch leases expire on their own. The repository an attempt of `batchId` writes in (ADR 0063): a claimed issue's, a sub-order's, or the only one of the Brewery for a Brewery order. Throws with the reason when there is none. A Brewery issue that is a sub-order writes in its repository, with a parent batch or not. How much of a rejected run's message its summary keeps: the runner may quote what it read. The summary of a run whose end rejected with `error` (ADR 0099): the first line of its message, at most `summaryLength` characters, or a fixed text when that has nothing to show or cannot be read, since the event store refuses an empty summary. The command that records how `ref` ended. The session id stays on its step.started; what claude reported in its init goes on its step.finished, when the event can hold it: a blank version or model is left out rather than refusing the ending with it (ADR 0116). cards.summary: The canonical text of an effect key: the `key` of an `effect.applied` event and of the effects index. Validated by the schemas in src/schemas/store.ts.
cards.comments: The canonical text of an effect key: the `key` of an `effect.applied` event and of the effects index. Validated by the schemas in src/schemas/store.ts. Only the key's own parts: a key built by spreading a larger object may carry other fields. A key with either of a step and an attempt is an attempt's, so one without the other fails. The canonical text of `key`; throws when a part is invalid. The key of a canonical text; throws for any other text, so one key has exactly one text. What the ledger recorded for the numbered effects of a batch, `keyOf(1)`, `keyOf(2)` and on, as far as they go: each is due only after the one before, so the first not recorded ends them. Throws for a recorded result that `schema` does not take, naming it `what`.

cards.summary: Applying an external side effect through the idempotency ledger (invariant I4, ADR 0033).
cards.comments: Applying an external side effect through the idempotency ledger (invariant I4, ADR 0033). Where an effect lands (a pull request, a comment, a label on the code host). Its results are checked against the effect's schema before it returns them: they come from outside the process, and the ledger keeps them for good. Both calls stop what they do on the code host when `signal` aborts: the driver aborts an effect at its deadline, below the batch lease (ADR 0044, #130). The result of the effect with this key when the target already has it, found by its key. Only what Foedrum's own identity made counts (its comments and pull requests, branches in its own repositories, never a fork's): keys are predictable, and anyone who can comment could plant one. Applies the effect, carrying its key so that `find` sees it; returns its result. The idempotency ledger: the `effect.applied` events of the store. Appends the `effect.applied` event of `key`. How an effect's result was had: from the ledger, found on the target, or applied now. Applies the effect of `key` at most once: the ledger's result when it is recorded, else the target's when a run before applied it and was killed before recording it, else the result of applying it now. Whatever the target answered is recorded; nothing is recorded when it fails. Calls for one key must not overlap: both would find nothing and apply it. `signal` goes to the target; once it aborts, nothing more is asked or recorded (#130). Given up at its deadline: whether it landed is for the next pass's `find` to say. The effects of every source together (ADR 0072): the keys each gives, and each key applied by the source that gave it. The shortest deadline of theirs holds for all, the driver's when none sets one. The source behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key.

cards.summary: The event store: the append-only event log, leases and the idempotency ledger (ADR 0002, architecture §4.1). Callers depend on this interface only, so the storage behind it can change (ADR 0002: `better-sqlite3` is the fallback for `node:sqlite`).
cards.comments: The event store: the append-only event log, leases and the idempotency ledger (ADR 0002, architecture §4.1). Callers depend on this interface only, so the storage behind it can change (ADR 0002: `better-sqlite3` is the fallback for `node:sqlite`). An event as stored: `id` grows with every append and is never reused. An event as read from the state branch, with the id it had in the store that wrote it. A batch whose pending deadline (a step's `deadlineAt` or a Conditioning `remindAt`) is due. The writes of one transaction; usable only inside the `withTransaction` callback. Validates and appends an event; returns its id. Creates or renews the lease of `lease.attemptKey`. The lease of `batchId`, alive or expired, as the transaction sees it: no other writer changes it before the transaction ends. Creates or replaces the lease of `lease.batchId`. Records an applied side effect; throws `DuplicateEffectError` when the key is already recorded. Records that the state branch has every event up to `marker.eventId`, in `marker.commit` (ADR 0024). Throws when the marker would move back or past the last event. Keeps the text of an attempt's out doc until a flush puts it on the state branch (ADR 0103), replacing one kept for the same attempt. Lets go of the kept out docs of these attempts, once a push put them on the state branch. Runs `fn` in one write transaction: everything it writes is committed together, or rolled back when it throws. `fn` must be synchronous, and transactions cannot be nested. Committed events with an id greater than `afterId`, oldest first, at most `limit`. Batches whose pending deadline is at or before `now`, earliest first. Leases still alive at `now`. Leases that expired at or before `now` and were not released, earliest first. Batch leases still alive at `now`, by batch id. Rebuilds an empty store from a log (ADR 0011: the state branch is the durable record), in one transaction. Throws `ReplayError` naming the first event that cannot be appended. The id of the last committed event; 0 when there is none. How far the state branch has the log, or `undefined` when nothing was ever pushed. The out docs kept for the state branch and not yet pushed (ADR 0103), by attempt. Appends events read from the state branch, keeping their ids, and marks everything up to the last one pushed in `commit` (ADR 0024), in one transaction. The ids must grow and come after every stored event, and every stored event must be pushed already. Throws `ReplayError` naming the first event that cannot be appended. The recorded result of a side effect, or `undefined` when it was never applied. A log that cannot be replayed; `index` is the position of the offending event in the log.

cards.summary: The fold: current state from the event log (architecture §4.1, invariant I3). Pure: no clock, randomness or I/O, and neither the events nor the state passed in are changed.
cards.comments: The fold: current state from the event log (architecture §4.1, invariant I3). Pure: no clock, randomness or I/O, and neither the events nor the state passed in are changed. Where a batch is: the board lanes (architecture §4.3), plus cancelled. `routeBy`: the routing deadline (ADR 0032). An attempt that had not finished when its batch got Stuck is `abandoned` (ADR 0025): whatever the batch does next, it schedules new attempts, and the abandoned one never starts or finishes. Scheduled because the attempt before it failed (ADR 0117). Scheduled because a human answered the questions of the attempt before it (ADR 0118). Scheduled because the attempt before it failed (ADR 0117). Scheduled because a human answered the questions of the attempt before it (ADR 0118). An interactive step's: when its session opened, a person's wait (ADR 0222). Scheduled because the attempt before it failed (ADR 0117). Scheduled because a human answered the questions of the attempt before it (ADR 0118). A check step's gravity readings (ADR 0069), or a brewer's setup's (ADR 0163). What claude reported in its init event, when it came (ADR 0116). What a brewer's attempt took, once its stream was read (ADR 0172). Stopped when its batch's pause reached its stopAt: it counts against no retry (ADR 0202). Ended as claude hit a usage limit: it counts against no retry (ADR 0206). A blocking Taster's findings, when it asked for changes (ADR 0221). By attempt number. The attempt of `step` with the highest number, if it has one: the step's latest (I2). The latest attempt of `step` when it runs: neither finished nor abandoned by Stuck (I2, ADR 0025, ADR 0055). The attempt of `step` with the highest number below `n`, if any: the one attempt `n` follows. The route that scheduled the round attempt `n` of `step` is in: its own, or for a retry, or an answer, that of the attempt it retries or answers, which it starts as (ADR 0117, ADR 0118). A person's handover of a batch from the driver `from` to `to` (ADR 0124). When `from`'s lease would have expired: no effect of the batch is applied before it. The step whose session `to` resumes, whose run `from` stops (ADR 0127). Where a batch's task tree is (ADR 0066): the branch of its latest attempt that succeeded with a worktree, or the commits of its latest rewind, whichever was recorded last. The commit a batch started from in a repository (ADR 0084): the worktree's commit of its first attempt there that succeeded, in the order the finishes came, or of its first attempt there while none has (`succeeded` false). The issue this batch brews: an order or a sub-order. The target repository of a claimed issue (ADR 0043); absent for a Brewery issue. When it was ordered (ADR 0179); absent for an order that did not record it. What chose the recipe; a human's choice also records who issued it and from where. The steps whose latest record is a skip (ADR 0064); absent while none is. Its latest handover from one driver to another (ADR 0124); absent while it had none. Its task tree; absent while it is the repository's base (ADR 0066). Where it started, by repository in lower case (GitHub names are case-insensitive); absent while no attempt of it recorded a worktree. Kept in the order of the events, which the steps do not follow: a recipe change or a route back runs an earlier step again later. How each of its pull requests ended that has ended, by URL; absent while none has. Its attempts in the order they started, across its steps; absent while none has. How its open pull requests merged with their base, each check in the order it was recorded (ADR 0198); absent while none was. The latest record of the checks on each open pull request's head, by URL (ADR 0213); absent while none was. A record names its head: it says nothing of another. The latest merge-tree of its open pull request's head with each other open pull request's head of the Brewery's in its repository, by the other's URL (ADR 0230); absent while none was. The failed head of a pull request that a person's skip of a batch Stuck on its checks left as it is (ADR 0219): nothing sends the batch back for it again. Absent while no skip did. The checks of a finished record as one text, the same in whatever order they were read. Whether two finished records of a head's checks say the same, in whatever order (ADR 0213). One merge-tree of an open pull request's head with another open pull request's (ADR 0230). The batch's own pull request, and the head of it that was merged. The other pull request's head that was merged. The files they conflict in; absent when they merge cleanly. The checks on a pull request's head (ADR 0213): still running since a pass saw it, or finished. Once each: a listing whose pages shift while it is read can return an issue twice. Checked once here, so that no poll rejects for it. A report that throws must not stop the intake. This module decides; the GitHub layer implements `ClaimHost` and turns each due effect into an `EffectTarget` (ADR 0033).
cards.comments: Claiming a target-repository issue across Breweries before brewing it (ADR 0043): which issues the intake picks, the claim ref that exactly one Brewery creates, the marks people see, and the release when the batch ends. This module decides; the GitHub layer implements `ClaimHost` and turns each due effect into an `EffectTarget` (ADR 0033). Which issues of a repository a Brewery brews: all of `labels`, and `milestone` when set. The label a claimed issue carries until its claim is released. The ref that claims `issue` in its repository: `refs/foedrum/claims/issues/<issue>`. What the intake reads of a target-repository issue. GitHub lists pull requests among the issues. GitHub logins. The GitHub login that opened the issue. When it was created on GitHub: its arrival in the intake's queue (ADR 0208). The Brewery that claims: its repository (`owner/name`) and its token's GitHub login. The issues of this repository that have a batch in this Brewery, in any lane. The Brewery's allow-listed users: only an issue one of them opened can become an order. GitHub compares logins, label names and repository names ignoring case. Whether `issue` has all of the filter's labels, and its milestone when it names one. Whether the intake may claim `issue`: open, filtered in, unassigned or ours, never brewed. An issue assigned to a person is that person's; this Brewery's own user is its person. A target repository may be open to anyone; only allow-listed users order work. The code host side of a claim: the claim ref of an issue in a target repository. Creates the claim ref of `issue`, pointing at a commit whose message is `message`; `exists` when the ref is there already. Atomic: of two calls, at most one creates it. The commit the claim ref points at and that commit's message, or undefined when there is no ref. Deletes the claim ref only while it still points at `sha`, in one step on the code host; false when it points elsewhere or is gone. How a claim went: created now, created by this Brewery before, or held by another. `by` is the Brewery the record names, or undefined when the record cannot be read. The Brewery a claim ref's message names for `issue`, or undefined when it names none. The ref was made by someone with push access, but its message is still read as untrusted text. Claims `issue` in `repo` for the claimant's Brewery. Gone between creating and reading it: released in between; the next poll tries again. Releases the claim when its record still names `brewery`; `gone` or `not_ours` otherwise. Only the commit that was read: a claim made since then is someone else's. How a pull request of a batch stands. The effects of a claimed batch's Brewery issue, by the name its key carries (ADR 0144). The Brewery issue that is the order of a claimed batch (ADR 0144): the one the earlier batches of the same issue left, and the batch's own once it is known. `gone`: the batch's reopen found that a person deleted it, so the batch opens its own. A batch of a claimed target-repository issue. Its Brewery issue; absent as for a batch whose Brewery issue nothing opened yet. What an effect of a claim does on the code host. Opens the Brewery issue of the claimed `repo#issue` in `brewery`, with its title (ADR 0144). Closes or reopens the issue `repo#issue`: the Brewery issue of a claimed batch. Why the claim ends now, or undefined while the batch is live or a pull request of it is open. `every` holds for no pull requests at all, which merged nothing. Where the claim of a batch stands: `held` while the batch is live or a pull request of it has no recorded end, `releasing` once its release is due and until `applied` has every effect of it, then `released` (ADR 0105). Only the keys count, and no key names the claimant: its Brewery and login are in the text. The assignee keeps every Brewery off an issue that is not done, until a person decides. The effects of the batch's claim that are due, in the order to apply them: the marks while the batch is live or its pull requests are open, the release once it is cancelled or every pull request it opened is merged or closed. The ledger skips those already applied. The Brewery issue comes after the marks, which keep other Breweries off the issue. A batch ordered again keeps the one an earlier batch opened, reopened however it was closed (found done while it is open), and opens its own when a person deleted it. A merge closes the target issue, and its Brewery issue with it; otherwise both stay open. The assignee stays: removing it would hand the issue to the next Brewery that polls. The ref goes last, so the issue is never claimable while the marks are still on it.

cards.summary: Keeps the out doc text an attempt's runner read in the store as the attempt ends, before the driver records its step.finished, so the next flush puts both on the state branch (ADR 0103).
cards.comments: Keeps the out doc text an attempt's runner read in the store as the attempt ends, before the driver records its step.finished, so the next flush puts both on the state branch (ADR 0103). Told when an out doc could not be kept; the attempt's end goes on without it. `runner`, whose attempts' out docs are kept in their own transaction before their ends settle: the driver records the step.finished after it, so a flush that has the event has the doc too. The end goes on without the text, which no notice or command should carry. A doc the store cannot take must not cost the attempt its outcome.

The labels of the lanes, in the order a batch moves through them. The labels of an issue on the code host, as the Brewery's own identity sets them. Makes the label in the repository; nothing when it is there already. The label of `lane`; none for a cancelled batch. A revision of a lane label that is due: the issue, and the label it leaves, or none. The Brewery's repository, `owner/name`, where its issues are. The lane label of every batch of a Brewery issue, for the driver: a revision whenever its lane's label changes.
