The revision behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key. GitHub's label names are case-insensitive. The lane labels on the issue that are not `label`: the ones to take off. An issue ordered again shows its latest batch: an older one never touches its labels. Nothing to show, or shown already; a batch cancelled before its first label has none.

cards.summary: What a driver does with the leases its earlier run left when it starts again (ADR 0033).
cards.comments: What a driver does with the leases its earlier run left when it starts again (ADR 0033). Sets the live leases of `owner` to expire at `now`: the processes of that owner's earlier run died with it (architecture §5: no "maybe alive"), so the supervisor's next tick loses their attempts. Leases of other owners stay as they are. Returns the attempt keys it expired. A driver calls it through `startDriver`, which refuses unless the driver's lock is held (ADR 0037).

cards.summary: The rounds of a lens step (ADR 0191): each attempt of it that reviewed, in the order the batch ran them, with the dispositions the brewer its findings route brought back wrote. The attempt plan gives a later round the earlier ones from it.
cards.comments: The rounds of a lens step (ADR 0191): each attempt of it that reviewed, in the order the batch ran them, with the dispositions the brewer its findings route brought back wrote. The attempt plan gives a later round the earlier ones from it. An outcome of a review (ADR 0196): a success with a Taster's verdict, or blocked by findings (`onFindings`). One round of a lens step: its attempt, and the dispositions of what its findings brought back. The rounds of `stepId` in `batch`, in the order they started, up to attempt `before` when given: each attempt of it that reviewed (`reviewed`), with the dispositions of the attempt its findings route brought back, or of a retry or an answered attempt that continued that one; a route of another step is never its own. The round each other step's latest attempt answers, while a retry or an answer continues it.

cards.summary: The limits on what the intake starts (ADR 0217), beside the Brewery's `concurrency` (ADR 0068): a recipe's `concurrency`, and the Brewery's open-order limit. Pure: a function of the folded state, the pass's listing of the Brewery's issues and the limits, so a restart holds the same.
cards.comments: The limits on what the intake starts (ADR 0217), beside the Brewery's `concurrency` (ADR 0068): a recipe's `concurrency`, and the Brewery's open-order limit. Pure: a function of the folded state, the pass's listing of the Brewery's issues and the limits, so a restart holds the same. Three orders in progress at once, by default (decided by the maintainer, 2026-10-26). What holds what the intake starts, besides the Brewery's free capacity. How many orders may be open at once: `openOrders` in foedrum.jsonc. The `concurrency` of the recipe called `name`, or undefined when it has none. Why the intake does not start an entry of its queue now, or route a batch. The limits of `openOrders` and the recipes' own `concurrency`. Whether a limit can hold now: some order is open, which every batch Ordered, Brewing, Conditioning or Stuck makes its own. The open orders (ADR 0217), by `orderKey` in the order their batches were ordered, each with its name as `foedrum status` gives it: a batch of it, its own or a sub-order's, is Ordered, Brewing, Conditioning or Stuck, or a sub-order of its latest breakdown has no batch yet while its latest batch is not cancelled. A sub-order's batch is named by its order, a claimed batch as status names it. The one recipe an issue's labels name, or undefined for none or more than one. What a walk of the queue started so far, and what holds its next entry. The limit that holds `entry` now, or undefined when it may start. Counts `entry` as started. Each recipe's batches Brewing, by name, in the order they were ordered. A tally of what is open and brewing now; `listed`: the Brewery's issues read in this pass. A recipe counts its batches Brewing and the Ordered ones the pass will route to it, by their Brewery issue's one label as listed, as the Brewery's `concurrency` counts both (ADR 0068). A target issue's recipe is its Brewery issue's, which exists only once it is claimed (ADR 0156). Only a new order: a sub-order is of an order already open, which it helps finish. What holds the route of an Ordered batch to `recipe`: its batches Brewing at its limit. Why a hold holds, in one line. The lines `foedrum status` prints above the board: each limit that holds now, from the store alone. A recipe counts only its batches Brewing, since its Ordered ones' labels are on GitHub.

cards.summary: The merge brief on a ready pull request (ADR 0225): one comment through the ledger per ready record, `[batch, "brief.<n>"]`, titled `Merge? <title> @ <short sha>`, with the verdict, what changed since it opened, the evidence on its head and the last Taster's risk left, every fact from the ledger and every model text filtered under its own heading. And each brief outdated by a moved head or a later brief, hidden as outdated, `[batch, "brief.<n>.hidden"]` (ADR 0229).
cards.comments: The merge brief on a ready pull request (ADR 0225): one comment through the ledger per ready record, `[batch, "brief.<n>"]`, titled `Merge? <title> @ <short sha>`, with the verdict, what changed since it opened, the evidence on its head and the last Taster's risk left, every fact from the ledger and every model text filtered under its own heading. And each brief outdated by a moved head or a later brief, hidden as outdated, `[batch, "brief.<n>.hidden"]` (ADR 0229). The pull request's comments and title on the code host, as the Brewery's own identity has them. The Brewery's own comment on the pull request whose body ends with `end`: its id and body. Comments on the pull request; the new comment's id. The pull request's title. Whether the Brewery's own comment is hidden; `gone` when it is not there or not its own. Hides the Brewery's own comment as outdated; `gone` when it is not there or not its own. The red proof step of the recipe `recipe`, when it has one (ADR 0078). How much of a model's text is read for secrets: what `plain` shows, and room past it. How many findings of one step, and dispositions in all, the brief lists. A text a brewer wrote at `stepId` as one inert line (ADR 0088, ADR 0184). The output of the latest attempt of `stepId` when it finished and succeeded. Where `{stepId, attempt}` is on the batch's path; -1 when it never started. The attempts a pull request's failure sent back, in the order they started (ADR 0219). What changed since the pull request opened: each fix round, its failed head and its push. A merged-tree failure names its base check, which names its branch (ADR 0226). Each check of the ready record, as the Stuck reason writes them, and how many more passed. A check's name and link are whoever runs CI's words (ADR 0213). How the pull request merges with its base, by its latest base check of `head` (ADR 0198, ADR 0203, ADR 0226). A check an older log wrote names no head: it may be of a head before a fix round. How the head merges with the other open pull requests of its repository (ADR 0230): each it conflicts with, else that it merges cleanly with all once every one was checked; else nothing. A file's name comes from whoever committed it. The readings of a check step's latest success, its repository's setup left out (ADR 0163). The facts of one batch's steps the brief reads, in its recipe's order. The `when` that was false for `stepId`, or its group's, when the batch skipped it (ADR 0064). The red proof's row: its readings, not run and why, or that the recipe has none. Each other check step's latest success: the checks it read, and the ones it skipped. How an attempt that did not succeed ended, in words. Each step that did not run, with the `when` that was false, and each whose latest attempt did not succeed that a person's skip went past; a step blocked by findings is the Findings section's. The Taster's steps of the batch, in its recipe's order: a verdict, or blocked by findings. The last tasting step in the recipe's order, or each child of its parallel group (ADR 0214): the steps whose risk left the brief shows. Where the last Taster tasted, and the fix rounds since, from the log alone. The findings each round of a Taster's step left: a success's from its out doc, a blocked round's as `step.finished` recorded them (ADR 0221). What the step each findings route went back to did with each finding (ADR 0191), round by round in the order they ran, each after the lens of the finding at its place, the first not already taken, as a later round's input pairs them (ADR 0220). The findings of each Taster's step whose latest attempt succeeded: advisory, left open. Each blocking Taster's step blocked by its findings that a person's skip went past, and each finding its round recorded (ADR 0221), which the skip accepted. The last Taster's risk left, each item after its step (ADR 0214). The brief after its title line, for `ready`, the record that makes `batch` ready. Only what can be shown is read, on one line: then no secret, no keyword or mention, no markup. Below the length a comment may be with room for the title (`plain` keeps it to 200 characters, five times as long escaped), which is left out, so a brief found by its marker can be told by the rest. The brief's title line: the pull request's title, which anyone who can edit it wrote. The hidden line before a brief's marker that names the record it was posted for: what tells a brief a killed driver posted from another record's under the same key. No model text can write it, since `plain` writes each `<` as `<`. What a brief of `ready` under `key` ends with: its record's line, then its marker. A brief that is due: where it goes, what follows its title, and the record it is for. A brief's ledger result, checked: the id comes from the code host, and the ledger keeps it. The repository and number of the pull request at `url`, when it is one. A brief to hide that is due: where its comment is. The merge brief of each ready pull request, for the driver (ADR 0225): due when `readyOf` gives a record the latest brief was not posted for, or whose brief was hidden, found among the Brewery's own comments by its record's line and its marker, else posted. And each outdated brief, hidden as outdated before the next brief is posted (ADR 0229): found when its comment is hidden or gone. The brief, or the brief to hide, behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key. By the record alone: another record's brief a killed driver posted under this key stays, and a base that moved since changes the text, not the record. The outdated briefs first, so the pull request never shows two at once.

cards.summary: When a brewed pull request is ready to merge (ADR 0225): the latest record of the checks on the head the batch pushed finished with none failed, its latest base check of that head (ADR 0226) found no conflict and no failing check on the merged tree, and the batch is On tap. And the merge briefs the ledger recorded, one per ready record, and those outdated, to be hidden (ADR 0229). Pure: the brief's effects and the status comment read it.
cards.comments: When a brewed pull request is ready to merge (ADR 0225): the latest record of the checks on the head the batch pushed finished with none failed, its latest base check of that head (ADR 0226) found no conflict and no failing check on the merged tree, and the batch is On tap. And the merge briefs the ledger recorded, one per ready record, and those outdated, to be hidden (ADR 0229). Pure: the brief's effects and the status comment read it. The record of a pull request's checks that makes it ready to merge. The first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its checks, as `sameHeadChecks` compares them. The record that makes the open pull request of `batch` ready to merge, or `undefined` while it is not. On tap, opened by its ledger, not ended, and its branch still the batch's push. The latest record only, and only of the head the batch pushed (ADR 0213). A record keeps the failed checks first, so the ones it left out passed too. A conflict or a failing check on the merged tree of this head is open; a merged tree not checked is not, nor an older head's (ADR 0226). The effect that posts the `n`th merge brief of `batchId`. The effect that hides the `n`th merge brief of `batchId` as outdated (ADR 0229). The merge briefs the ledger recorded for `batchId`, the `n`th at `n - 1`. The latest merge brief the ledger recorded for `batchId`, if any, and the number of the next. Whether the ledger recorded the hide of the `n`th merge brief of `batchId`. Whether `brief` was posted for `record`: the same pull request, head and checks. The latest merge brief of `batchId` while it is of `ready` and not hidden (ADR 0229). The latest merge brief of `batch` while it is of the record that makes it ready now. What the status comment says of the open pull request of `batch` (ADR 0229): its current brief, else that it has none; nothing once no pull request of it is open. The latest push of `batchId` that left its branch somewhere: at the commit it pushed, at someone else's (`moved`), or gone. A push that pushed nothing (`empty`, `refused`) left it where the one before did. Whether `pushed` left the pull request's head at another commit than `head`, or at none. The merge briefs of `batch` to hide as outdated (ADR 0229), by their number: recorded, not hidden yet, of a pull request with no recorded end, and either of a head the pull request is no longer at (the batch's latest push, or a base check that found someone else's push) or followed by a later brief. A record that goes pending or fails on the same head outdates nothing.

cards.summary: The checks of an open pull request's merged tree (ADR 0203): the intake pass hands a clean merge-tree of a moved base on, and this run reads the batch's checks on the merged tree, one run at a time in the Cellar, beside the ticks and the pass. Nothing is recorded until a run ends, so a kill loses no run: the next pass finds the tip moved and hands it on again.
cards.comments: The checks of an open pull request's merged tree (ADR 0203): the intake pass hands a clean merge-tree of a moved base on, and this run reads the batch's checks on the merged tree, one run at a time in the Cellar, beside the ticks and the pass. Nothing is recorded until a run ends, so a kill loses no run: the next pass finds the tip moved and hands it on again. A pull request whose base moved to `tip` and merges cleanly with it, due for its checks. The base branch, as the remote names it. The commit Foedrum pushed. How many checks of the pull request the log held when it was handed on. How a run on the merged tree ended. The checks did not run: the merged tree could not be made, or the checks not found. The engine's stop ended it: nothing is recorded. The checks a batch's merged tree is read with: its recipe's step that merges the base. The most a run may take, so ADR 0130's floor of an hour holds for what it leaves (ADR 0203). The check step of `batch`'s recipe whose checks the merged tree is read with, the one that merges the base before it runs (ADR 0164); `undefined` when it has none. Reads the checks on the merged tree of `due`; ends `stopped` once `signal` aborts. What it could not do: a run that threw, a refused record. Queues `due`, at its newest tip once per pull request. Starts the next run when none is underway; never waits for it. Ends when no run is underway. Whether `due` is still to run, or to record: its pull request open on tap, and no check recorded since it was handed on, so a newer tip's check or a moved branch stands (review of #528). A reason as the log keeps it: its first line, at most MAX_UNCHECKED_LENGTH characters. The due runs by pull request, in the order they came; each at its newest tip. Another writer checked the pull request while it ran. The run underway reads this tip already.

cards.summary: Out doc text on its way to the pull request body and the status comment (ADR 0088): a text that looks like a secret is left out, with a fixed line naming its step. Pure.
cards.comments: Out doc text on its way to the pull request body and the status comment (ADR 0088): a text that looks like a secret is left out, with a fixed line naming its step. Pure. `text`, or a fixed line naming `stepId` when it looks like a secret: never the matched text, nor `findSecrets`' excerpt of it. The text is read as written and as shown, on one line, since joining its lines can make a match (`password` and `= x` on two lines).

cards.summary: Pauses (ADR 0202): which batches a person's pause holds, and when what runs of them is stopped.
cards.comments: Pauses (ADR 0202): which batches a person's pause holds, and when what runs of them is stopped. The order `batch` brews for: its own issue, or for a sub-order's batch its order's. The pause that holds `batch`, if any: `--all`, else its order's (a sub-order's batch is held by its order's), with the earlier stopAt of the two. A batch that ended is held by none. Under --all an order's own --by still stops it, when it comes first. Whether the pause holding `batch` has reached its stopAt at `now`: what runs of it is stopped. When what runs is stopped, in UTC with the time and day in the zone it was given in: `16:30 UTC (17:30 Europe/Brussels, 18 October)` (ADR 0202). The zone was recorded on the machine that paused: the one folding the log may not know it.

cards.summary: The plan comment of an order (ADR 0233): the latest succeeded plan of its batch as a table and a graph on the order's issue, its edits as revisions in the ledger, `[batchId, "plan.<n>"]`, each found by its marker on the Brewery's own comment before it is applied (ADR 0033).
cards.comments: The plan comment of an order (ADR 0233): the latest succeeded plan of its batch as a table and a graph on the order's issue, its edits as revisions in the ledger, `[batchId, "plan.<n>"]`, each found by its marker on the Brewery's own comment before it is applied (ADR 0033). A text the brewer of `stepId` wrote, on one line, or a fixed line when it looks like a secret. The graph of the sub-orders' order (ADR 0180): each id replaced by a node id of the engine's, every label quoted, and a backtick written as Mermaid's entity, so no label ends the block. The plan comment's text for the plan `stepId` of `batchId` wrote, without its marker: every text the brewer wrote one escaped line, left out when it looks like a secret. Filled by the plan lenses (#587) and the gate (#588). The graph goes first, so a cut never leaves its block open. The plan of the latest attempt of `batch` that succeeded with one, and its step. The latest revision of the order's comment before `batch`'s first: of another batch of the same Brewery issue, the last in the order the batches were ordered, so an order shows one plan. The revision of the plan comment of `batchId` that the recorded events call for: the next one when its latest plan's text is not the one the comment shows, else none. The Brewery's repository, `owner/name`, where its issues are. The plan comment of every order whose batch has a succeeded plan, for the driver: a revision whenever its text changed, edited in place, a later batch of the order editing the same comment. No limit a minute: a plan changes only when a plan step succeeds (ADR 0233).

cards.summary: The `touches` check of a plan (ADR 0233): after a plan's `done`, every path a sub-order touches that it does not mark new must exist in its repository at the commit the plan was written against. Git runs only through the injected `ReadPaths`, so no model and no fold is involved.
cards.comments: The `touches` check of a plan (ADR 0233): after a plan's `done`, every path a sub-order touches that it does not mark new must exist in its repository at the commit the plan was written against. Git runs only through the injected `ReadPaths`, so no model and no fold is involved. A repository of the Brewery, its clone, and the commit a plan's paths in it are checked at, or why that commit could not be read: its base could not be fetched (ADR 0233). The paths git found at a commit, or why it could not read them. Which of `paths` exist at `commit` in `clone`; never throws, git's failure is `unread`. The places a failed check names; it counts the rest, as the secret scan does (ADR 0187). A commit as a failed check names it, as the secret scan does (ADR 0187). `ending`, once the paths of a succeeded plan were read in `repositories` (ADR 0233): a repository the Brewery does not list, or a path not marked new that does not exist, fails it retryably; a read that fails blocks it on its environment. Any other ending as it is. The paths to read in each repository, in the order the plan names them, each once.

cards.summary: The checks GitHub runs on an open pull request's head (ADR 0213): each intake pass reads the head of every open pull request of a batch on tap that its ledger opened, and every check on it, and records when it began to wait for them and, once they have all finished, how each one finished. There is no deadline: the engine waits as long as they run, and the status comment says so. A record with failed checks keeps the end of each failed Actions job's log (ADR 0228).
cards.comments: The checks GitHub runs on an open pull request's head (ADR 0213): each intake pass reads the head of every open pull request of a batch on tap that its ledger opened, and every check on it, and records when it began to wait for them and, once they have all finished, how each one finished. There is no deadline: the engine waits as long as they run, and the status comment says so. A record with failed checks keeps the end of each failed Actions job's log (ADR 0228). A check on a pull request's head as the code host has it now; no `conclusion` while it runs; `job`: the id of the GitHub Actions job it is, whose log the reader can read (ADR 0228). What the pass reads of an open pull request's checks; GitHub's is `githubCheckReader`. The full sha of the commit the pull request at `url` heads now. Every check on `head` in the repository of the pull request at `url`, page after page. The log of the Actions job `job` in the repository of the pull request at `url` (ADR 0228): its excerpt, or why it could not be read; it throws only for a read to try on a later pass. What it could not do: a head or checks it could not read, a refused record. Whether a check that finished with `conclusion` passed (ADR 0213). The checks a record keeps: the failed first, then the rest, each in the order read. A finished check as read, with the job whose log a record may keep. How long the log reads of one pass may take, all its records together: well inside its deadline, so a record with slow logs is written all the same and the next pass skips it as unchanged (ADR 0228). Why a failed job's log was not read once the pass's time for logs was up. `checks` as a record keeps them, each of the first `MOST_FAILED_CHECKS` failed Actions jobs with its log (ADR 0228), read one at a time until the pass's minute ends at `until`. Undefined for no record on this pass: given up, a read the reader says to try again, which it reports, or a record whose first read would start after `until`, which the next pass reads. One pass: reads the checks on the head of every open pull request, and records what changed. Each batch as the log has it now: other writers append beside the pass (ADR 0044). Every pass reads them again: a re-run, or a check that registered late, changes them. A pass given up at its deadline records nothing more. The latest record, when it is of this head: a record of another never counts for it. No check at all is finished only on a pass after one that recorded this head: the repository's workflows may not have registered theirs yet. Only a record about to be written reads a log, so an unchanged one never reads it again.

cards.summary: The openPullRequest action as the driver runs it (ADR 0071): two effects of the batch in the ledger, the push of its task tree to the bottle branch and then the pull request on the code host, each found by its key before it is applied (ADR 0033), so a kill between them never pushes twice or opens two pull requests (I4). The attempt ends once both are recorded. A later round of the pull request, after a failure on it sent the batch back, pushes again under a key of its own onto the round before, and opens nothing (ADR 0219); once that push went, it renders the body again, unless someone edited it (ADR 0227).
cards.comments: The openPullRequest action as the driver runs it (ADR 0071): two effects of the batch in the ledger, the push of its task tree to the bottle branch and then the pull request on the code host, each found by its key before it is applied (ADR 0033), so a kill between them never pushes twice or opens two pull requests (I4). The attempt ends once both are recorded. A later round of the pull request, after a failure on it sent the batch back, pushes again under a key of its own onto the round before, and opens nothing (ADR 0219); once that push went, it renders the body again, unless someone edited it (ADR 0227). What Foedrum asks the code host to open. The branch in the repository itself, never a fork's. Opened as a draft (ADR 0167); ready for review when absent. Where pull requests are opened (architecture §3.1). Every call stops when `signal` aborts. The URL of the pull request in `repo` whose head is its branch `head` and that the Brewery's own identity opened, open or not, or `undefined`: keys and branch names are predictable, so a pull request anyone else opened never counts. Opens the pull request; its URL. The body of the pull request at `url`, empty when it has none (ADR 0227). Replaces the body of the pull request at `url`, and nothing else of it (ADR 0227). The pushes of a repository's clone to its remote. Every call stops when `signal` aborts. The commit `revision` names in the clone; throws when it names none. Whether the commit `commit` is the commit `of` or one of its ancestors: both full shas. The commit the remote's branch `base` points at now, fetched into the clone's objects without reading the clone's configuration (ADR 0090); throws when the remote has no such branch. The commit the remote's branch `branch` points at, or `undefined` when it has no such branch. Pushes `commit` to the remote's branch `branch`, never by force. What the commits from `base` to `commit` (both full shas) would publish that looks like a secret, or that the scan cannot read: nothing when they may go (ADR 0079). Every path the diff from `since` to `commit` (both full shas) names: added, altered, deleted, and a rename at both paths (ADR 0201). A repository a batch writes in: its base branch, and the pushes of its clone. The branch the pull request goes into, as the remote names it (`main`). The path globs whose files the pull request names when its change touches them (ADR 0201). The Brewery, `owner/name`: its pushed branches carry it (ADR 0043). The title of the order's issue, read as the effect applies. What the pull request's body is rendered from, read when the effect applies (ADR 0167). The effect that writes it, which its marker names (ADR 0227). What one of the action's effects does, as `due` worked it out. Where the batch's change starts, and the globs its files are matched against (ADR 0201). A later round's: the commit the round before pushed, where it expects the branch (ADR 0219). A later round's body, rendered again on the pull request at `url` (ADR 0227). A character no path git names holds, in place of a name's leading dot. Whether `glob` matches `file` (ADR 0201), a wildcard also matching a name that starts with a dot, which `posix.matchesGlob` alone never does: `src/auth/**` covers `src/auth/.env`. A dot the glob writes still matches only a dot, also inside braces or a class (`{.env,.npmrc}`), which the plain match reads. Where the action pushes from and opens into, or why it cannot run. The round of the pull request this push is (ADR 0219). A later round's: the commit the round before pushed, where it expects the branch. A later round's: the pull request ended while the fix ran, so nothing is pushed. The secret scan stopped the push: the batch waits on a human (ADR 0079). The findings the blocked summary names; it counts the rest. Each commit, place and kind: never the matched text, nor findSecrets' excerpt of it. The place comes last, so a file named `token` never reads as an assignment the status comment leaves out. The URL the code host answered, which the ledger keeps for good and `batch.on_tap` carries. The base is never the start here: the task tree has moved (ADR 0066). One push per round of the pull request (ADR 0219). Recorded for good: a rewind after it does not scan again (ADR 0079). The ledger keeps the push of the batch's life: a rewind after it cannot reach its branch. A later round pushes on top of the round before, to the same pull request (ADR 0219). The effect behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key. The files of the change that match a sensitive path, read once for commits that go. The commit to push, and whether the base holds all of it: a pull request with no commits, which the code host refuses, is recorded as nothing to push instead. The base as the remote has it now, not the clone's origin/<base>, which may not have been fetched since the base moved (ADR 0090); the scan reads from the same commit. Every commit of the task tree is in the base already, also when the base moved past it. Pushed by a run before that was killed before it recorded the push. Nothing leaves the machine before the scan of every commit it would carry (ADR 0079). A later round pushes only onto the round before: a branch someone else pushed to, or deleted, is left alone, and the pull request with it (ADR 0219). Updated by a run before that was killed before it recorded the update. Only a body Foedrum wrote is rendered again: a person's edit stays theirs. The title and the draft state are never sent (ADR 0227). A pull request that ended while its fix ran gets no push: the action ends with it. The change starts where a diff Taster's does (ADR 0161, ADR 0164); none before a start. A later round renders the body again once its push went, while the pull request is open.

cards.summary: What sends a batch on tap back to a fix step: the latest base check of its open pull request's head, the commit of its latest push, conflicted (ADR 0244) or failed on the merged tree (ADR 0226), else the latest record of the checks on that head finished with a check that failed (ADR 0219). Pure: the supervisor reads it to issue the command, and decide reads it again to act on it.
cards.comments: What sends a batch on tap back to a fix step: the latest base check of its open pull request's head, the commit of its latest push, conflicted (ADR 0244) or failed on the merged tree (ADR 0226), else the latest record of the checks on that head finished with a check that failed (ADR 0219). Pure: the supervisor reads it to issue the command, and decide reads it again to act on it. An open pull request whose checks failed on the head the batch pushed, with the failed ones. The open pull request of `batch` whose latest record of checks finished with a failure on the commit of the batch's latest push; `undefined` while they run or passed, for a head someone else pushed, and once the pull request ended or its branch moved. A person's skip left this head as it is. A record keeps the failed checks first, so the checks it left out never hide a failure. The first problem of the open pull request of `batch` on the head of its latest push (ADR 0226): its latest base check of that head conflicted (ADR 0244) or failed on the merged tree, else its checks failed on the head. A check either conflicts or runs the merged tree, never both. A person's skip left this head as it is, whatever was wrong with it. Only a check that names this head: one without a head may be of an older one. The cause a fix command names for `problem`. The pull requests whose failure has sent `batch` back to brew a fix, each once (ADR 0219). Whether a person's pause holds the order of `batch` or the whole Brewery (ADR 0202). `pauseOf` passes over a batch on tap, which runs nothing; this is the pause of the fix it would start. The step of `recipe` that opens the pull request, when it has an onPullRequestFail route.

cards.summary: The check of the Brewery's open pull requests of one repository against each other (ADR 0230): each intake pass, after the base check, merge-trees two open heads it has no record of, and records what it found for each of the two batches. A conflict shows on the status comment and in the merge brief's evidence, and never holds "Ready to merge".
cards.comments: The check of the Brewery's open pull requests of one repository against each other (ADR 0230): each intake pass, after the base check, merge-trees two open heads it has no record of, and records what it found for each of the two batches. A conflict shows on the status comment and in the merge brief's evidence, and never holds "Ready to merge". What it could not do: a branch it could not read, a merge-tree that failed, a refused record. An open pull request of a batch, with the head its latest push recorded. The open pull request of `batchId` as `state` has it, when it is one. Whether `batchId`'s fold has the merge-tree of `side`'s head with `other`'s. One pass: merge-trees every pair of open heads of one repository not checked yet. The open pull requests of each repository, in the log's order. A repository without a base check: nothing to check it with. Each bottle branch's remote tip once per pass, and only for a pair that is due; `undefined` when it could not be read or is gone. A branch someone else pushed to is not checked (ADR 0198); a gone one is closing. Each side on its own: a pass killed between the two records left one out. A pass given up at its deadline records nothing more. Other writers append beside the pass (ADR 0044): a head that moved meanwhile is a new pair. Another open pull request the batch's open pull request conflicts with, and in which files. The repository a batch writes in, as the log names it; `undefined` for a Brewery issue's batch, which opens a pull request only in a one-repository Brewery (`repositoryOf`), so it shares that repository with every other. What the pair checks of the open pull request of `batch` say now: the other open pull requests of its repository it conflicts with, and whether every other one was checked clean. A record counts only while both heads are the ones the batches' latest pushes recorded.

cards.summary: The openPullRequest action (ADR 0071), the pure core: the keys of its two effects, the bottle branch it pushes, the pull request the ledger recorded, and the pull request's text from the order and the brewers' out docs.
cards.comments:
The openPullRequest action (ADR 0071), the pure core: the keys of its two effects, the bottle branch it pushes, the pull request the ledger recorded, and the pull request's text from the order and the brewers' out docs. The effect that pushes the batch's task tree to its bottle branch in `round` of its pull request: `push` in the first, as before rounds were, then `push.<n>` (ADR 0219). The round of the batch's pull request: 1, and one more each time a failure on it sent the batch back (ADR 0219). What the ledger recorded for each push of `batchId`, round by round from the first, as far as they go: a round pushes only after the one before (ADR 0219). Unread here: each reader passes over a result that is no push. The latest push the ledger recorded for `batchId` (ADR 0219), when it is one the engine records. The effect that opens the batch's pull request, once per batch. The effect that writes the batch's pull request body in `round`: the open's in the first, then `body.<n>`, which renders it again (ADR 0227). The text a body marker's digest is of: its line endings made `
`, its end trimmed. The first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `text`, as a status comment's revision has (ADR 0072). The marker line that ends a body Foedrum wrote: its key, and the digest of `text` above it. The key and digest of `line` when it is a body marker of `batchId`. Whose a pull request's body is (ADR 0227): Foedrum's own, with its marker, or left alone. Whose the body of `batchId`'s pull request is (ADR 0227): Foedrum's own when its last line is a marker of the batch and the digest of the text above it matches, line endings made `
`: only the last line, so a marker a brewer wrote into how it works never passes for it. A marker of the batch on another line: the text after it changed, or it moved. What the latest round's body effect recorded (ADR 0227), for a round after the first. The local name of the batch's bottle branch in `repo`: `foedrum/<batch>/<owner>.<name>`. The pull request the ledger recorded for `batchId`, by its URL, or `undefined`. The open pull request of `batch` that its ledger opened, with the commit and the bottle branch its push recorded; `undefined` also once someone else pushed to that branch (ADR 0198). A round that found the branch moved or gone pushed nothing: the pull request is left alone. The commits the state records for `batchId`, which a 40-character hexadecimal word may name without being a key (ADR 0088): where its attempts' worktrees started, its rewinds' commits, and the commit each push recorded, the commits it refused (ADR 0079) and the commit it found the branch moved to (ADR 0219). Read from the folded state, never from git. A finding left as there before the change (ADR 0191). What a step reported in the out doc of its latest attempt that succeeded. A Taster's verdict and findings (ADR 0161). The pull request's sections a `pullRequest` brewer wrote (ADR 0167). A Finer's changes, or why there was nothing to simplify (ADR 0166). The new tests and the regression tests a Gauger named (ADR 0170). The findings its attempts marked pre-existing, for a person to file (ADR 0191). One finished attempt of a batch, as the pull request's brew table shows it (ADR 0167). The engine's word for how it ended, or a Taster's verdict. Why a failed attempt failed: the engine's text, which may quote a model's words. The finished attempts of `batch`, in the order they started (`Batch.path`). A running attempt, the action's own among them, has no result yet. A keyword after anything but an ASCII letter or digit, the word boundary GitHub reads: emphasis with `_` around it starts a word once GitHub renders it (`_fixes #3_`), and so does `é`. Every character reference GitHub would decode, named or numeric: `@` is an `@`. A line break as CommonMark reads one, kept by `split`: `
`, `` or `
`. A blank line, which ends every paragraph, and so every span and HTML tag in one. What GitHub may read before a span, taking a backtick from it: an HTML tag or an autolink (`<`), a link's destination or title (`]`), and its math (`$`). Where `text`'s code spans start and end, paired as CommonMark pairs them but within one line (ADR 0184): a run of backticks no backslash escapes, and the next run as long. Where GitHub could read a span as text, there is none: after a span that holds a `|`, which a table splits first, on a line with what GitHub may read before a span, and on the lines after a run left open, such a line or a `|` until a blank line, since a span or a tag can go on over them. A backslash escapes the character after it, a backtick too, outside a span. A run with no partner on its line may have one on the next: the line goes on pairing. `text` with `edit` applied to what lies outside its code spans. Model text without what GitHub would act on outside a fence (ADR 0167): the `@` of a mention, a closing keyword before an issue reference, and the `&` of a character reference, except inside a code span, where GitHub acts on none of them (ADR 0184). A removal can make what it removes again: `closes closes #3`, `@@ann`, `&@ann`. The spans are paired again each time, in case a removal changes how a line pairs. Whether the pull request opens as a draft (ADR 0167): unless a Taster tasted the change and every Taster approved. The reports of `batch`'s steps, in the order they were first scheduled. A check's success has no out doc; a Taster's has its verdict and findings too (ADR 0161), a pullRequest brewer's the pull request's sections (ADR 0167), a Finer's its changes (ADR 0166), and a Gauger's its tests (ADR 0170). The findings the succeeded attempts of `step` marked pre-existing (ADR 0191), in order, each place and why once: every round's, since a later round never raises one again. Where a finding is, how bad, and whether it was there before the change, on one line, after its lens when it names one. The lens it was found through, on a step of several lenses together (ADR 0220). Where a Finer's cha

cards.summary: Ranks (ADR 0208): the order in which the intake orders and claims its queue, by arrival unless a person moved an order with `foedrum rank`. Pure: the intake and `rank` both sort through it.
cards.comments: Ranks (ADR 0208): the order in which the intake orders and claims its queue, by arrival unless a person moved an order with `foedrum rank`. Pure: the intake and `rank` both sort through it. An order of the intake's queue, as it sorts. When its issue was created on GitHub: its arrival. 0 for a Brewery issue, else 1 + the place of its repository in foedrum.jsonc. A ready sub-order of `order`, started under `parentBatchId` (ADR 0211): it sorts at its order's place, ahead of a new order of the same place. Whether a sub-order of the latest breakdown of `order` has no batch yet (ADR 0211). A rank's place stands in for its issue's arrival. Where an order goes among those of its arrival: a ranked one by its tie, the lower ahead, and an unranked one behind them. `queue` in rank order: the orders marked "finish first" by when they were marked, then the rest by arrival, a rank's in place of its issue's. Of the orders that share an arrival, the ranked ones go first by their tie; then the Brewery's own issue, the order foedrum.jsonc lists the repositories in, and the issue number break a tie. A started order's next sub-order goes ahead of a new order of its place (ADR 0211). `queue` with one entry per order: an order's ready sub-orders hold one place (ADR 0211). Where `rank <order> <position>` puts the order: the arrival of the order now at `position` among those of `queue` without the mark, leaving `order` out, and a tie that puts it just ahead of that order and behind the ranked orders of the same arrival ahead of it; past the end, `now`. So the order keeps its place relative to the orders around it as they are ordered, and a later arrival goes behind it. A ranked order ahead of it with the same arrival: the new rank goes between the two. Why `order` cannot be ranked, from the folded state alone, or undefined: it is a sub-order, which its plan ranks, the Brewery issue of a claimed target issue, or it has a batch, so it left the queue, and no sub-order of its latest breakdown is left to start (ADR 0211).

cards.summary: The ready set (ADR 0211, ADR 0216): the sub-orders the intake may start now, a pure function of the folded state. A sub-order is ready when it is in its order's latest breakdown, has no batch yet, and every sub-order it is blocked by is done: its pull request merged, and for a `release` dependency, a release of its repository recorded after that merge. `releaseWaits` says which repositories' releases the intake reads for that (ADR 0223).
cards.comments: The ready set (ADR 0211, ADR 0216): the sub-orders the intake may start now, a pure function of the folded state. A sub-order is ready when it is in its order's latest breakdown, has no batch yet, and every sub-order it is blocked by is done: its pull request merged, and for a `release` dependency, a release of its repository recorded after that merge. `releaseWaits` says which repositories' releases the intake reads for that (ADR 0223). A ready sub-order, with the batch it is ordered under: its order's latest. The merged pull requests of `issue`, by URL: of one of its batches, or of a bottle it is in, which its bottled batches record as theirs (ADR 0211). Where the fold recorded the merges of `issue`'s pull requests (ADR 0216). Whether the sub-order a dependency is blocked by is done: its pull request merged, and for `release`, its repository released after that merge, in any case (ADR 0211, ADR 0216). The Brewery orders a person stopped that still have a batch Stuck for it (ADR 0205). The ready sub-orders of every order not held, by order number, each order's in its plan's order. A paused or stopped order would only hold the slot (ADR 0202, ADR 0205); a cancelled one wants nothing more. A repository a `release` blocker waits on, and the merges a release of it must hold. The repository as the first breakdown that names it spells it. Each waiting blocker's merged pull requests, by URL: a release must hold one of each. The repositories whose release a sub-order waits for (ADR 0223): of each order not cancelled, every `release` blocker of a sub-order with no batch that merged and is not done, by repository in lower case, in the order the orders and their breakdowns name them. A paused or stopped order is read: its sub-order starts once the hold lifts (ADR 0223).

cards.summary: An attempt's receipt as a person reads it (ADR 0172): one line per attempt where a batch is shown, and a batch's total. Never a cost: claude reports list prices, not what a user pays (ADR 0181).
cards.comments: An attempt's receipt as a person reads it (ADR 0172): one line per attempt where a batch is shown, and a batch's total. Never a cost: claude reports list prices, not what a user pays (ADR 0181). A finished attempt's receipt, with the tokens its step.finished recorded. The receipts of `batch`'s attempts, in the order they ran. `2m 38s`, `45s`, `1h 2m`. `812 tokens`, `4.13k tokens`, `1.34M tokens`: three significant digits past a thousand. Rounded first: 999,600 is 1M, not 1000k. The parts of one receipt's line: duration, turns, tokens and denials, each left out when there is nothing to show. `told` shows a text the stream gave: a tool's name, a refused prefix. The parts of `batch`'s total over its attempts with a receipt; none when no attempt has one.

cards.summary: The Brewery's recipe files as the engine's Recipes (ADR 0053), the core (ADR 0021): every recipe, brewer and lens file is read and checked, and either all of them load or none does. Foedrum's defaults lie under the Brewery's files: a Brewery file replaces the default of its name (ADR 0098), a lens the default of its folder and name (ADR 0143). brewery-files.ts reads the files.
cards.comments: The Brewery's recipe files as the engine's Recipes (ADR 0053), the core (ADR 0021): every recipe, brewer and lens file is read and checked, and either all of them load or none does. Foedrum's defaults lie under the Brewery's files: a Brewery file replaces the default of its name (ADR 0098), a lens the default of its folder and name (ADR 0143). brewery-files.ts reads the files. A file of the Brewery, by its path from the Brewery's root with `/`: its text, or why not. The files of one kind: recipes (`*.jsonc`), brewers and lenses (`*.md`). The Brewery's recipe files (`recipes/*.jsonc`), brewer files (`brewers/*.md`) and lens files (`lenses/diff/*.md`, `lenses/plan/*.md`, ADR 0143), and Foedrum's own defaults (ADR 0098), each by its path in `defaults/`. Foedrum's `defaults/models.jsonc`, merged under the Brewery's models.jsonc (ADR 0153). A recipe a step that chooses the recipe may offer: its name and description (ADR 0232). A lens's text, from the Brewery's `lenses/` or Foedrum's defaults (ADR 0098). Its folder and file name: `diff/<name>` or `plan/<name>` (ADR 0143). The file it was read from: `lenses/<folder>/<name>.md` or `defaults/lenses/<folder>/<name>.md`. The brewer of a recipe's step, with its instructions: the brewer file's body. The lenses its inputs name, by name. On a Taster's step: the lens it reviews through, `diff/<name>` or `plan/<name>` (ADR 0161). On a Taster's step of several lenses: each, in the step's order, reviewed together (ADR 0220). On a Taster's step: whether a `changes` verdict holds the batch up (ADR 0161). On an interactive step: the recipe's first message to the session (ADR 0222). On a step that chooses the recipe, or whose brewer names the recipes input: the Brewery's recipes but those that choose one, in order (ADR 0232, ADR 0234). Every brewer and lens in use, and what names them: what doctor reports on (ADR 0141). The brewers the recipes' steps name, the lenses those brewers' inputs and steps name, and of those the lenses a lens step reviews through (ADR 0221). The brewers of the loaded recipes' steps. The brewer of step `stepId` of recipe `recipe`, or `undefined` when there is no such step. The checks of the loaded recipes' check steps (ADR 0069). The checks of step `stepId` of recipe `recipe`, or `undefined` when it is no check step. Whether any recipe has a check step. The step whose tests step `stepId` of recipe `recipe` proves red, when it is a red proof. The first red proof of recipe `recipe` and the step it proves, when it has one (ADR 0078). A check step's checks, and for a red proof the step whose tests it proves. The paths of the default files in use: those the Brewery has no file of its name for. One line per problem, each starting with the file it is about. What doctor and a refused command say when the files are not valid. The most text one input of a brewer may hold: it reaches the prompt on stdin, and the event log through the out doc. A lens is held to it when the brewer loads (ADR 0098). The longest deadline a step may have: a year. A schema's reason in one line, as doctor prints it. The name a file must hold: its file name without the extension. What a file replaces a default by: its path in its kind's folder, without the extension, so `nip` for `recipes/nip.jsonc` and `diff/security` for `lenses/diff/security.md` (ADR 0143). , '') Whether `file` is a folder the shell could not list: its path names the folder, without a file name and its extension, so it is never matched by name like a file. The defaults of one kind that no file of `own` is named like: a Brewery file replaces them. A defaults folder that could not be read is always kept, so it fails the load. The defaults the Brewery keeps, by kind: those it has no file of the same name for (ADR 0098). The files the load reads, by kind: the Brewery's own, then the defaults it keeps (ADR 0098). Each Brewery file that replaces a default of the same name, with that default, recipes, then brewers, then lenses (ADR 0098, ADR 0141). The paths of the defaults the Brewery has no file of the same name for (ADR 0098), then Foedrum's models.jsonc, which always applies under the Brewery's and is listed, not loaded (ADR 0153). The lens a brewer input reads (`"from": "lens:<folder>/<name>"`), when it reads one. Each file's checked content, or the problems that make the load fail. A step the engine runs, as its recipe answers about it. A `Duration`. Whether it gets another attempt after `attempts`, the last of which failed retryably. Where its onFail (a check), onBlocked findings (a brewer) or onPullRequestFail (the openPullRequest action, ADR 0219) route goes, and how often. The action it is, which the engine runs itself (ADR 0071); none for a brewer or a check. A check step that expects its checks to pass: not a red proof (ADR 0164). The parallel group it is a child of (ADR 0168). A brewer step whose attempts run as a person's session (ADR 0222). A brewer step whose answer chooses the batch's recipe (ADR 0232). The deadline of the openPullRequest action (ADR 0071): its effects are retried on every pass of the driver until then, through a GitHub rate-limit pause, which lasts an hour at most (ADR 0052). How many attempts the action gets in each round of its pull request (ADR 0219): one fails only when it has nothing to push. The deadline of a check step without one of its own (ADR 0069). How often a check step is tried again after an attempt that read nothing: cancelled, lost, or one whose worktree the driver could not make. A check that read the tree is not tried again: it would read the same. Whether an attempt ended without a reading of its own: cancelled, or retryably failed. The recipe's settings after routing, which a `when` may read (ADR 0064). The parts of a `when` its schema accepted. Why the engine cannot follow `when` yet, or `undefined` when it reads a recipe setting. A step's result is not recorded for a when to read until tasting lands (#26). Whether `when`, which reads a recipe setting,

cards.summary: The recipe label of a batch whose recipe a person chose by answering a step that chooses it (ADR 0232): `recipe:<name>` on its Brewery issue, or on the Brewery issue that is a claimed batch's order (ADR 0156), set once through the ledger as the driver's effect `[batchId, "recipe-label"]`, found on the issue before it is applied (ADR 0033), as the lane labels are (ADR 0154): the issue's other recipe labels come off, so its next order has one to route by. A label added after routing routes only the issue's next batch (ADR 0068).
cards.comments: The recipe label of a batch whose recipe a person chose by answering a step that chooses it (ADR 0232): `recipe:<name>` on its Brewery issue, or on the Brewery issue that is a claimed batch's order (ADR 0156), set once through the ledger as the driver's effect `[batchId, "recipe-label"]`, found on the issue before it is applied (ADR 0033), as the lane labels are (ADR 0154): the issue's other recipe labels come off, so its next order has one to route by. A label added after routing routes only the issue's next batch (ADR 0068). The Brewery's repository, `owner/name`, where its issues are. A recipe label that is due: the issue, and the label. The recipe label of every batch whose recipe an answer chose, for the driver. The label behind each key `due` gave; the driver asks `due` before it applies a key. The issue's labels: whether it shows the due one, and its other recipe labels, to take off. GitHub's label names are case-insensitive. Once: a later choice in the batch labels nothing more.

cards.summary: How the state machine asks a recipe where a batch goes next (architecture §4.3, ADR 0025). The state machine handles every outcome and blocker kind itself; a recipe only answers these questions, so recipe files (#52) can change without touching the lifecycle.
cards.comments: How the state machine asks a recipe where a batch goes next (architecture §4.3, ADR 0025). The state machine handles every outcome and blocker kind itself; a recipe only answers these questions, so recipe files (#52) can change without touching the lifecycle. Why a route sends a batch back: a failed check, findings, or its pull request (ADR 0219). An action step the engine runs itself, never a brewer (brewers-and-recipes §1, ADR 0071). What follows a step that succeeded or was skipped. The recipe is done: the batch goes on tap with these pull requests, and with the one its step `opens` opened, when the recipe has an openPullRequest step that the batch did not skip by its `when` (ADR 0071). When a running attempt counts as stalled: no file write or commit for `turns` turns or for `minutes` minutes, whichever comes first (brewers-and-recipes §1). How many of its batches may brew at once (ADR 0217); absent when it has no limit of its own. The step a batch starts with. Its step ids in the order the recipe lists them, a parallel group's children in its place: what the status comment shows (ADR 0072, ADR 0168). Whether the recipe has a step `stepId`: a parallel group, or a child of one, too. The children of `stepId`, in the recipe's order, when it is a parallel group, whose attempts run side by side (ADR 0168); `undefined` for any other step. The parallel group `stepId` is a child of, or `undefined` when it is none's (ADR 0168). Whether `stepId` is an interactive brewer step: its attempts run as a person's session, which only a driver with a terminal opens (ADR 0222). Whether the answer to the question of `stepId` chooses the batch's recipe (`chooses: "recipe"`, ADR 0232). The action `stepId` is, which the engine runs itself; `undefined` for any other step. Whether an attempt at `stepId` merges the base into its worktree before it runs: the recipe's last check step that expects to pass, when an openPullRequest step follows it (ADR 0164). How long an attempt at `stepId` may take, in milliseconds. When an attempt at `stepId` stalls, or `undefined` when it has no stall limit. The `when` of `stepId` that is false for `batch`, so the batch skips the step when it reaches it, or `undefined` when the step runs (ADR 0064). What follows `stepId` in `batch` once it succeeded or was skipped. Whether `stepId` gets another attempt after a failed or cancelled one (`maxAttempts`). The step an `onFail` route (a failed check), an `onBlocked: findings` route or an `onPullRequestFail` route (ADR 0219) sends `batch` back to, or `undefined` when `stepId` has no such route or its rounds are used up. The step the `why` route of `stepId` goes back to, whatever its rounds; `undefined` without one. How many rounds the `why` route of `stepId` has sent `batch` back, or `undefined` when the step has no such route (ADR 0064, ADR 0192). How many rounds the `why` route of `stepId` may take, or `undefined` without one (ADR 0226). The recipe called `name`, or `undefined` when the Brewery has none.

cards.summary: The releases of the repositories a `release` blocker waits on (ADR 0216, ADR 0223): each intake pass reads the latest release of every repository with a merged, unreleased `release` blocker, and records it once it holds a merge of every blocker that waits on it, so the sub-orders they block start.
cards.comments: The releases of the repositories a `release` blocker waits on (ADR 0216, ADR 0223): each intake pass reads the latest release of every repository with a merged, unreleased `release` blocker, and records it once it holds a merge of every blocker that waits on it, so the sub-orders they block start. A repository's latest release as the code host has it: GitHub's latest release, else tag. Its tag's name: the version a record names. When it was published, or for a tag its commit's date, in ISO 8601. A tag with no release: its date is its commit's, set where it was made (ADR 0223). What the pass reads of a repository's releases; GitHub's is `githubReleaseReader`. The latest release of `repo`, or undefined when it has none. Whether `release` of `repo` holds the merge of the pull request at `pullRequest`. A release it recorded. What it could not do: a release it could not read, a refused record. One pass: reads the latest release of each repository a blocker waits on, and records it when it holds a merge of every blocker waiting on it (ADR 0223). The waits as the log has them at the start: a release recorded here ends its own. A release recorded counts for every blocker merged before it: it must hold them all. A pass given up at its deadline records nothing more.

cards.summary: A recipe file as a batch uses it (ADR 0017): settings the schema leaves unset are decided here, from the brewers the recipe uses, so an unset testFirst never reaches the engine as off.
cards.comments: A recipe file as a batch uses it (ADR 0017): settings the schema leaves unset are decided here, from the brewers the recipe uses, so an unset testFirst never reaches the engine as off. The Brewery's brewers by name, or `undefined` for a name it has none of. `testFirst` as the recipe says, else `true` when any of its brewers produces commits. Throws when the recipe names a brewer the Brewery does not have. Every brewer is looked up before any is judged, so a missing one is refused wherever it is.

cards.summary: Which session a retry or an answered attempt resumes (ADR 0117, ADR 0118): the one of the attempt before it, when claude started it and an attempt of it has a worktree to run in again. Pure: the driver recreates the worktree and records the start.
cards.comments: Which session a retry or an answered attempt resumes (ADR 0117, ADR 0118): the one of the attempt before it, when claude started it and an attempt of it has a worktree to run in again. Pure: the driver recreates the worktree and records the start. How attempt `ref` starts when its brewer resumes: in a session it continues, or fresh, and why. The id of the session it continues. The attempt that made the worktree the session ran in, and that worktree. The attempt of `step` that made the worktree session `id` runs in, and that worktree: the one of the attempts with that session id that recorded a worktree. A resumed session keeps its id, and only the attempt that started it had a worktree of its own (ADR 0029). The worktree `attempt` of `step` runs or ran in, and the attempt that made it: its own, or for a resumed attempt the one whose session it continues (ADR 0117); none before it started. Whether `ref` of `batch` is the retry of an attempt that ran out of its turns, by the mark on that attempt's outcome: then `ref` resumes its session whatever the brewer's `retryMode` (ADR 0175). Whether `ref` of `batch` resumed the session of an attempt that ran out of its turns, as the status comment says it (ADR 0175). Whether the attempt of `step` before attempt `n` ran out of its turns, by its outcome's mark. How attempt `ref` of `batch` starts when its brewer resumes; undefined when it has no session to resume: it is no retry and answers no questions, or the attempt before it ran no session. A route comes after its step succeeded, and that session's branch holds the task tree, which a failure resumed on it would move: so only a retry or an answered attempt resumes, and never one after a success (ADR 0117, ADR 0118). Only a finish through its runner's end carries claude's report: its process is gone, and claude started the session. A lost or abandoned attempt has none (ADR 0117). A retry after a success (Stuck on a divergence, then retried): its commits would move the task tree, which that session's branch holds (ADR 0066, ADR 0117).

cards.summary: The EventStore on the built-in `node:sqlite` (ADR 0002). The only module that imports it.
cards.comments: The EventStore on the built-in `node:sqlite` (ADR 0002). The only module that imports it. How long a write waits for another connection's lock before failing; default 5000 ms. Opens an existing store for reading only (ADR 0030): no journal mode change, no migration, and every write fails. A store at another schema version is refused. Opens the connection; defaults to `new DatabaseSync`. Tests inject one to inspect it. Migration n brings the database from schema version n to n + 1 (`PRAGMA user_version`). Times are stored as epoch milliseconds, so they compare as times whatever their ISO precision. `deadlines` and `effects` are indexes of the events, maintained on append (and so by `replay`). node:sqlite reports the extended result code in `errcode` (ADR 0002 verification). The deadlines row of a batch rather than a step: its routing deadline while Ordered, or its Conditioning or Stuck reminder (ADR 0032). Step ids are never empty. A body that is not JSON fails the schema like any other invalid event. Read again under the write lock: another connection may have migrated meanwhile. Opens (and creates or migrates) the store at `path`; `':memory:'` for a private in-memory one. A reader changes nothing: a store at another version is for a Foedrum that knows it. An id from the state branch; AUTOINCREMENT continues after it. The earliest due deadline of a batch is its earliest pending deadline. Keeps the deadlines index up to date with an appended event. Scheduling a step ends a routing deadline or a Conditioning or Stuck reminder, and replaces the step's earlier attempt. A retry of a batch Stuck on routing: Ordered again, with a new routing deadline (ADR 0032). A Stuck batch waits for a human: its reminder replaces its steps' deadlines (ADR 0025). indexed by the events_index_effects trigger A paused attempt's new deadline as its pause is lifted (ADR 0202). Appends `event`, with the given id when it comes from the state branch. The date first, so an invalid expiry gets the store's own message. Its later writes fail on the ended transaction; the caller already gets this error.

cards.summary: The state branch's shell (ADR 0011, ADR 0024): gathers facts from git and the store, and carries out what state-branch.ts decides. Git runs only through the injected `Git`.
cards.comments: The state branch's shell (ADR 0011, ADR 0024): gathers facts from git and the store, and carries out what state-branch.ts decides. Git runs only through the injected `Git`. The Brewery clone. The state branch's own worktree, in the work root outside the clone (ADR 0012). Default `origin`. Default `foedrum/state`. Where a stale lock file's removal is said; default nowhere. Waits between tries for the writer lock at a start; default a timer. Nothing to push. Not pushed (no network, a remote hook); the marker stays and the next boundary retries. Opens the state worktree, checks that a commit can be made (and signed, when the clone signs), and brings the store and the branch in line. Throws `StateBranchStopError` when the engine must not run. Commits and pushes every event after the pushed-through marker, with the out docs the store kept (ADR 0103); call it at every step boundary. Throws `StateBranchStopError` when the push is rejected: another engine wrote. A `failed` flush leaves events only in the local store, so the caller retries it on its own deadline (the supervisor tick), not only at the next boundary, which may never come. The branch the events are pushed to, unless the options name another. The ref of the signing check's test commit; deleted again right away. A signing prompt that nobody answers must not hold up the start for long. The output limit of the one call that lists the whole branch (ADR 0035). Files are written next to their place and renamed, so a crash never leaves half a log. A start waits for another driver's start or flush to let the writer lock go (ADR 0107), longer than that flush's push may take. --no-verify skips pre-commit and pre-push only. Every call gets core.hooksPath at an empty folder Foedrum owns, next to the worktree, so no hook of the clone runs (ADR 0024). Auto gc and maintenance are off, so no git outlives the writer lock and takes the branch's ref lock after it (ADR 0115). Every git that writes the worktree runs under the writer lock (ADR 0107), so a lock file of git's found while it is held was left by a git that no longer runs: the index's and HEAD's in the worktree's git folder, and the branch's and the signing check's refs in the clone's common one (#306, ADR 0115). The clone's are removed before the worktree is opened, whose add may need the branch's ref; so their folder is asked of the clone, since the worktree may not exist yet (#320). The log files in the worktree. No batches folder yet is no batches; any other failure must not look like none. The worktree's commit; undefined before its first commit (git answers 1, nothing else). The remote branch's commit, or undefined when it does not exist. One test commit, signed when the clone signs, so a broken signing setup refuses the start instead of failing every step boundary (ADR 0024). commit-tree does not read commit.gpgSign as git commit does, so it is asked to sign. A symbolic link or submodule from the remote could lead reads and writes outside the worktree; refuse the branch before anything of it is checked out (ADR 0024). One entry of about 100 bytes per file, and the branch grows with every event: the runner's 4 MiB default would stop every sync at about 40,000 files (ADR 0035). A rebuild (the database is missing or was moved aside after a stop): nothing in the worktree is needed any more. Its local branch moves to the remote; the remote is never touched, and a diverged local commit stays in the reflog. Untracked out docs may stay; anything else would be lost or mixed into the logs. `checkAll` also checks log files no pending event goes to (ADR 0024: a recovery flush). Read after the events: the out doc of a pending step.finished was kept before it (ADR 0103). Out docs alone are pushed too: one kept after its events were pushed waits for no event. The branch holds the same bytes on every machine, whatever core.autocrlf says. A user's pack-refs whose ref lock was removed as stale can set the branch back to its packed value after the commit (ADR 0115): then the events are not on it. The commit itself, not the branch, which that pack-refs can still set back before the push. The branch has them now; a crash before this writes them again, with the same text. One start or flush at a time in this process: a second flush waits and then pushes what is left. The writer lock keeps out the other processes of the work root (ADR 0107). Another driver's flush may push this one's events too; the caller retries on its deadline.

cards.summary: The state branch's pure core (ADR 0011, ADR 0024): which file an event belongs to, how log files are read, merged and extended, what a step boundary is, and whether the engine may start. No I/O: the shell (state-branch-git.ts) gathers the facts and carries out the decisions.
cards.comments: The state branch's pure core (ADR 0011, ADR 0024): which file an event belongs to, how log files are read, merged and extended, what a step boundary is, and whether the engine may start. No I/O: the shell (state-branch-git.ts) gathers the facts and carries out the decisions. The engine must stop: the state branch and this engine's store disagree (ADR 0024). A file on the state branch, by its path with forward slashes, and its text. The batch an event belongs to; `undefined` for events without one. The usage window holds every batch's brewers (ADR 0206). The schema already refuses such ids; this is the one check where a path is built (ADR 0024). The log file an event belongs to: its batch's `events.jsonl`, or the top-level one. Where the out doc of an attempt goes: next to its batch's `events.jsonl`. The most bytes of an out doc's text the state branch keeps (ADR 0103); past it, a fixed line takes the text's place. Whether `path` is a log file: `events.jsonl` or `batches/<batchId>/events.jsonl`. 1-based, for messages. Reads one log file; throws `StateBranchStopError` naming the file and line of a bad line. Merges every log file by id. Throws `StateBranchStopError` for a bad line, a repeated id, or an event in a file it does not belong to. A kept out doc as a file on the branch: model output, stored as it is and never read back as a log or an order (ADR 0103). Past `MAX_BRANCH_OUT_DOC_BYTES` a fixed line takes its place. Whether a logged `event` is `ours` as the store reads it: the schema drops an old receipt's cost (ADR 0181). The new text of every log file the pending events go to, then every out doc in `outDocs` at its `outDocPath`, so each goes into the commit of the step.finished that records it (ADR 0103). `current` holds the files to check, as they are in the worktree (missing when absent): at least those the pending events go to. Lines after `pushedThrough` that a crashed flush left behind are replaced; one that differs from the pending event with its id, also as the store reads it, means another engine wrote it, and throws `StateBranchStopError`. Without pending events only the out docs are planned: those kept after their step.finished was pushed, such as an attempt's that Stuck abandoned. Each pending line by id, with the file it goes to. The commit message of a flush. The branch's events after the local ones, once every local event is checked to be on the branch with the same id and content; throws `StateBranchStopError` when one is not. Whether appending `event` (which took the state from `before` to `after`) ends a step: it is `step.finished`, or it changes a batch's lane kind (ADR 0024). What the engine knows at start-up. The remote branch, for messages, such as `origin/foedrum/state`. The state worktree's commit; undefined before its first commit. The remote branch's commit; undefined when the branch does not exist. Whether the marker's commit is the remote head or one of its ancestors. Push what is not on the branch yet. Append the branch's events after the local ones (the database is missing or behind). The start-up table of ADR 0024. A push whose marker was not written; the flush checks that the files hold our events. The paths in `git ls-tree -r -z` output that are not plain files: symbolic links and submodules, which could lead reads and writes outside the state worktree (ADR 0024). The commit of exactly `ref` in `git ls-remote` output, or undefined when it is not there. ls-remote matches patterns against the end of a ref, so `refs/heads/x/refs/heads/<branch>` also matches; only the exact ref counts. Throws when its object name is not a full sha. Reads `git push --porcelain`: rejected means the remote moved (non-fast-forward).

cards.summary: The status comment of a batch of a Brewery issue (architecture §8, ADR 0072): its text rendered from the folded state alone, and its edits as revisions in the ledger, `[batchId, "status.<n>"]`, each found by its marker on the Brewery's own comment before it is applied (ADR 0033).
cards.comments: The status comment of a batch of a Brewery issue (architecture §8, ADR 0072): its text rendered from the folded state alone, and its edits as revisions in the ledger, `[batchId, "status.<n>"]`, each found by its marker on the Brewery's own comment before it is applied (ADR 0033). What the status comment says of a pull request's merge brief: the current one, or the open pull request that has none (ADR 0229). The status comments on the code host, as the Brewery's own identity sees and makes them. The Brewery's own comment on the issue whose body ends with `marker`: its id and body. The body of the comment `comment`, or undefined when it is gone or not the Brewery's own. Comments on the issue; the new comment's id. Replaces the body of `comment`; `gone` when it was deleted. How long a text a brewer or an issue wrote may be in the comment. How much of such a text is read for secrets (ADR 0088): what can be shown, and room past it for a match that starts there, so a token cut at `longest` is still found whole. How many assumptions of one step the comment shows. How many questions of a batch Stuck for input the comment shows, and options of each. HTML's characters and `@`, as the entities GitHub shows as themselves. One character as GitHub shows it as itself: Markdown's escaped, the rest of `entities`. `text`, which a brewer or an issue wrote, as one line of at most `longest` characters that GitHub renders as it is: no Markdown, no HTML (so no marker), and no mention. It is cut after escaping, between characters, so no escape is cut in half and the line never grows past `longest`. What the status comment and `foedrum stuck` recommend when a findings route ran out of rounds, until the analyse recipe can plan the order again itself (ADR 0192, #388). `rounds` rounds of a findings route, in words. A text a brewer wrote at `stepId` as one plain line, or a fixed line when it looks like a secret. A URL as an autolink of its normalized form: the schema keeps the text it was given, and `new URL` encodes the spaces and angle brackets that would let the rest of it render as Markdown. The command that opens the session a batch waits for (ADR 0222): `foedrum brew` of its issue in a terminal, taking the batch from the driver that parked it. A target issue's order is named by its repository's alias, which only foedrum.jsonc knows. A check's name and link are whoever runs CI's words (ADR 0213), shown as plain text and a link. The check's name and command are the Brewery's configuration (ADR 0209). The files are the repository's names (ADR 0244). Who stopped it and why are a person's words, shown as plain text (ADR 0205). What a findings route that ran out of rounds left open, as the Findings section shows findings, and the recommendation to step back (ADR 0192). A commit as the comments show it: its first eight digits.
