cards.summary: The supervisor's thin shell (ADR 0021, ADR 0027): one tick, which the commands that run the driver call on their own interval. It reads the store, asks the core (supervisor.ts) for commands, has the command log decide and append them, releases expired leases and retries the state branch's flush. The clock and store are injected.
cards.comments: The supervisor's thin shell (ADR 0021, ADR 0027): one tick, which the commands that run the driver call on their own interval. It reads the store, asks the core (supervisor.ts) for commands, has the command log decide and append them, releases expired leases and retries the state branch's flush. The clock and store are injected. What the supervisor reports instead of failing: it keeps running. decide refused a command of the tick: another writer changed the batch after the tick read the store, or the core and decide disagree, which is a bug. Deciding or appending a command threw; the tick goes on with the other commands. A driver also reports a finish it recorded this way when the read of the state after it throws (#289). The flush of the state branch failed; the next tick retries it. The flushes have failed since `since`, for longer than the flush deadline (ADR 0024 as amended by ADR 0027). A tick threw; the next tick runs anyway. Time between Conditioning and Stuck reminders; default 2 days (architecture §4.3). How long an Ordered batch may wait to be routed; default 1 hour (ADR 0032). How long flushes may fail before the supervisor reports it; default 10 minutes. Whether the supervisor acts on a batch now: a driver's own batches and the free ones, never one another driver holds (ADR 0019). Default every batch. The events the tick appended. Runs one tick. Rejects with `StateBranchStopError` when the engine must stop. A report that throws must not stop the supervisor: deadlines and reminders still need it. Every command is decided against the events committed when it is appended, also those another writer appended after the tick read the store. Decides `command` and appends its events in a transaction of its own. One broken command must not keep the other batches from their deadlines (I5). One tick at a time, whoever starts it: a tick waits for the one in flight. Another driver's batches are its own supervisor's: their deadlines and leases stay as they are. Before the batches' commands, which were planned while the window was closed (ADR 0206). Unpushed events never wait for a tick that works (ADR 0024).

cards.summary: The supervisor's pure core (architecture §4.4, ADR 0025, ADR 0027): from the folded state, the due deadlines and the expired leases, the engine commands one tick issues. It never builds events: decide does, so the supervisor cannot do what the state machine refuses.
cards.comments: The supervisor's pure core (architecture §4.4, ADR 0025, ADR 0027): from the folded state, the due deadlines and the expired leases, the engine commands one tick issues. It never builds events: decide does, so the supervisor cannot do what the state machine refuses. What the runner (#11) knows about a running attempt: when it last wrote a file or committed. Turns since then. For display (ADR 0174): the main thread's turns so far; a brewer's attempt only. For display: the latest main-thread tool call, reduced to its name and one safe word. For display: whether a denial came after the latest main-thread tool call. For display: whether the repository's setup runs, before claude starts. The runner's progress signals; `undefined` for an attempt it does not run. The batches whose pending deadline is due (`EventStore.batchesPastDeadline(now)`). The leases that expired (`EventStore.expiredLeases(now)`). An engine command about one batch. At most one per batch, to decide in this order. Every expired lease but those of lost attempts it leaves to the next tick (ADR 0168). A closed usage window's reopen is due, before the batches' commands (ADR 0206, ADR 0215). The commands one tick issues: deadlines first (invariant I5), then lost, then stalled attempts. One command per batch: the first one decided makes the others moot. The expired leases of lost attempts this tick leaves to the next: a batch's other children of a parallel group, which would otherwise wait out their deadline with no lease (ADR 0168). A step the recipe file no longer has (renamed under the batch) has no stall limit: its deadline still holds, and asking the recipe about it would throw on every tick. A batch on tap whose pull request failed on the head it pushed goes back (ADR 0219). A window is every batch's: whichever supervisor ticks first reopens it (ADR 0206), and each reopens at its own reset (ADR 0215). What a due deadline asks of `batch`: expire, remind (ADR 0025) or `unrouted` (ADR 0032). A paused batch's attempt that has not started waits for continue, not its step (ADR 0202), and any while a usage window is closed for its reopen, whatever its family (ADR 0206, ADR 0215). An interactive step's open session is a person's wait, with no deadline: its lease ends it when its driver dies (ADR 0222). The command that sends `batch` back from its open pull request (ADR 0219): on tap, its latest base check of the head of its latest push failed on the merged tree (ADR 0226) or its latest record of the checks on that head failed, its recipe has an onPullRequestFail route, and no pause holds it (ADR 0202). Derived from the folded state alone, so the next tick after a kill issues it again, and decide refuses it once the batch has left on tap. The attempts of a brewing batch that run: each the latest of its step, neither finished nor abandoned. Since when flushes of the state branch fail, and whether that was already reported. Follows the state branch's flushes: `overdueSince` is set once, on the first flush that still fails `deadlineMs` after the first failure, so the engine raises attention once (ADR 0024 as amended by ADR 0027).

Whether `windows` hold a brewer attempt on `family`: the window of every brewer, its family's, or any window when its family cannot be told (ADR 0215). When a closed usage window reopens, and whether claude's reset could be read. The documented forms only (ADR 0091): `3:45pm`, or a weekday before it, `Mon 12:00am`. The instant `resets` names at `now` in `zone`: the next moment that matches, if it can tell. ICU reports Etc/Unknown when it cannot tell the machine's zone, and rejects it as a zone. Today or the coming weekday; once that moment passed over an hour ago, a day or a week on. Across midnight the hour before is yesterday's, or last week's weekday: always past. When the window whose reset claude wrote as `resets` reopens, read at `now` in `zone`: the next moment that matches (`3:45pm`, `Mon 12:00am`) plus the margin, or an hour on when unread. cards.comments: The attempt worktree cleanup, wired into the engine (ADR 0029, ADR 0037): over every batch at a driver's start (crash repair), and over one batch once it has ended. cards.summary: What a batch's commits would publish that looks like a secret (ADR 0079), the pure core: the messages, the headers and the added lines that `git log` shows for them, read with findSecrets. A finding names the commit, the file (or the message, or the header) and the kind, never the text it matched.
cards.comments: What a batch's commits would publish that looks like a secret (ADR 0079), the pure core: the messages, the headers and the added lines that `git log` shows for them, read with findSecrets. A finding names the commit, the file (or the message, or the header) and the kind, never the text it matched. The place of a finding in a commit's message. The place of a finding in a file whose path would itself say too much. A commit's headers in `git log --format=raw`: the tree and parents are hashes the push needs, the author and committer are named by their header, and any other header by `header <name>`. The commit a `commit <sha>` line starts, a full sha (ADR 0254); undefined for any other line. A package lock's integrity hashes (Subresource Integrity) look random and are not secret. In any other file such a prefix could disguise a key, so only a lock's are left out. The findings, one per commit, place and kind, in the order they were found. The findings in the output of `git log --format=%x00%H%n%B`: one commit after each NUL. The findings in the headers of each commit in the output of `git log --format=raw`: the author, the committer, and every other header the push carries and `%B` does not show (a signature, an encoding, a merged tag). The message, indented below them, is `scanMessages`' to read. A name is published too: a finding never names one that looks like a secret. A signature's armour is base64 by nature; a token in it is still found by its own kind. git ends the headers only at an empty line, so a line that is only a CR is still a header. The message, indented, is scanMessages' to read. The commits of the output of `git log --format=%x00%H%n%B`, in order. The commits of the output of `git log --format=raw`, in order. The path of `diff --git a/<path> b/<path>`, quoted as git quotes it: renames are off, so both halves name the same file and the line splits in the middle, spaces in the path or not. The findings in the output of `git log --format=%x00%H --patch --unified=0` with the prefixes `a/` and `b/`: the added lines of each file, and every binary file, which the scan cannot read. The lines of each hunk are counted from its header, old and new apart, as a context line counts on both sides: an added line is never read as a header, nor a header as part of a hunk. A path is published too: it is read like a line, and a finding never names one that matches. `\ No newline at end of file` belongs to the line before it. A binary file the commit deletes publishes nothing: the base has it. The header says so, never the path, which could end in ` and /dev/null`. A word of text that has a full commit id's length, in either case. Every 40-character hexadecimal word of `text`: what may be a commit rather than a key.

Input may come from untrusted repositories (ADR 0020); the limit also bounds locateError's recursion. Longest accepted input in characters (1 MiB, ADR 0020), not counting a BOM. Comments and trailing commas become spaces (line breaks kept), so positions in the result match the input. index in `out` of a comma that may turn out to be trailing last character outside comments and whitespace ', i)) { ', i)) { const end = text.indexOf(' A comma right after '[', '{' or another comma is not trailing; JSON.parse rejects it. Throws a ParseError at the first syntax error in `json` (comments and trailing commas already blanked out). Runs only after JSON.parse rejected the input, whose messages do not always carry a position. Elements of an array or members of an object, after the opening bracket. A ParseError at `offset` in `text`; lines are counted by LF, so CRLF counts once. Index just past the string starting at `start`, or the end of the line if it is unterminated. JSON whitespace only: JSON.parse rejects anything else, such as a no-break space.

Foedrum never holds a token. It returns what GitHub answered, parsed but unchecked: every caller checks it, since it comes from outside. On GitHub's rate limit it pauses, and fails every request until the pause ends (ADR 0052).
cards.comments: A small GitHub client over `gh api` (ADR 0073): REST and GraphQL calls with gh's own login, each given up after its timeout or when the caller's signal aborts. On GitHub's rate limit it pauses, and fails every request until the pause ends (ADR 0052). The process runner gh runs through; default the real one. Unit tests pass a fake (ADR 0021). gh's `--hostname`: `github.com` (the default), a GitHub Enterprise host or `github.localhost`. The environment gh runs in, without the GitHub token variables; default this process's. Default this process's platform; it decides how environment names compare. Where gh runs; default this process's working directory. How long one request may take; default 30 s. How long an answer may be; default 4 MiB, the process runner's output limit (ADR 0035). The time in milliseconds, for the rate limit's pause; default `Date.now`. What GitHub answered: its status, its body parsed but unchecked, and its headers. How long the answer was, in bytes: what the reads count against their cache (ADR 0068). What GitHub answered as text: its status, its body as gh printed it, and its headers. GitHub's rate limit holds requests until `until` (ADR 0052): the request that met it, and every request of this client before then, fails with it without reaching GitHub. Where the API's paths start, without a trailing `/`. `path` from the API's root, `/repos/...`; `body` as JSON, or `null` when there is none; `headers` added to the request, such as `if-none-match`. `GET path` with its answer kept as text, never parsed, escape sequences and all, up to `maxBytes`, which also bounds gh's output: a job's log (ADR 0228). A GraphQL request; an answer that is not 200 fails. Parses an answer's body, which may be empty or not JSON at all. The longest pause a secondary limit without headers doubles up to. The longest pause of all, whatever a header says: GitHub's primary limit resets every hour. A header that holds a whole number, such as a reset in epoch seconds; undefined for anything else. The API root gh asks on `hostname`, without a trailing `/`: where a next page's link must point (ADR 0052). `github.localhost` is gh's development host, served over http. api.github.com'; api.github.localhost'; ${hostname}/api/v3`; Room for the status line and the headers, above an answer's own limit. gh's name for the host's GraphQL endpoint, which is not under the REST API's root everywhere. What `gh api --include` printed: a status line, header lines up to an empty one, then the body. `undefined` when it printed no status line, so gh failed before GitHub answered. A header no request could carry says nothing the client reads. gh's environment: no token variable, which gh would prefer to its own login (ADR 0073), and no debug output; it never prompts or looks for updates, and prints no colours. Requests wait for GitHub's rate limit until `pausedUntil`; `secondaries` counts the secondary limits without headers in a row, whose pause doubles. Pauses for GitHub's rate limit when `answer` calls for it, as GitHub's documentation says: a retry-after first, then the reset of a used-up limit, else a minute that doubles while the limit repeats. True when the answer is a refusal for the limit. The last request the limit allowed: the next one would be refused. One request through `gh api --include`, with an argument array and no shell; a body goes on stdin. gh exits 1 on a status of 300 or more after printing the answer, so a 304 or a 404 is an answer like a 200; without a status line, gh failed before GitHub answered (ADR 0073). `limit` bounds the answer; `escapes` lets gh print one with terminal escape sequences, which it refuses since 2.97.0 (ADR 0228). cards.comments: Conditional reads of GitHub (ADR 0008, ADR 0052): every GET carries the ETag of the answer it got before, and a 304 answers that same body again without counting against the rate limit. How many bytes the pages of one list may have; more fails the read. Default 32 MiB. How many items a list asks for per page. Anyone who can open an issue or comment on a public repository can write a body of 65,536 characters, up to 6 bytes each in JSON, so a page of 10 stays under the client's 4 MiB answer limit, and long bodies cannot stop a read (ADR 0052). A GET of `path`, conditional on the answer before; a 304 answers that one as 200. Every item of the list at `path`, page after page; `what` names it in an error. With `field`, each page is an object that holds its items under that name, as GitHub's check runs. The URL of the `next` relation in a `Link` header, or undefined when there is none. The last answer with an ETag of each path, least recently used first, and their bytes. An answer longer than the whole cache is never kept. gh's login goes with every request: never to a page off the API.

cards.comments: A bounded, link-safe read of one file inside a root: an out doc, a check's report. Only a regular file, reached through no link, of at most a given size (ADR 0047, #134). A swap that came before the identity was taken and is still in place moved the real path (review of #136); one made and undone within these few calls is not seen. A hard link keeps its name in the worktree, but its content may be any file of the volume. Never more than the limit, even when the file grew since.

Native Windows has none (ADR 0010). A process runner that wraps another, so the deadline, the stop and the output limit stay the process runner's (ADR 0035).

cards.summary: Finding the file a command name runs (architecture §13, executables): through PATH, and on Windows also PATHEXT, so `claude` can be found as `claude.cmd` and `foedrum doctor` can show what runs. Whether a regular file is at the path. npm's CLI script as installed with the node at `execPath`, so npm runs without npm's shims or a shell: `<node dir>/node_modules/npm` on Windows. Elsewhere node is `<prefix>/bin/node`, and npm is in `<prefix>/lib/node_modules/npm` (the nodejs.org builds, nvm, setup-node), `<prefix>/libexec/lib/node_modules/npm` (Homebrew's keg, which macOS resolves node's link to) or `<prefix>/share/nodejs/npm` (Debian's and Ubuntu's npm package), looked at in that order.

cards.summary: An exclusive lock between processes on one machine (ADR 0037): a SQLite database in exclusive locking mode keeps the lock of its first write until it is closed, and the file lock under it (fcntl, LockFileEx) dies with the process: no stale lock to detect, and no pid that a new process may reuse. On macOS and Linux the lock is an fcntl lock, which belongs to the process, not to the file handle: closing any handle to the file drops every lock the process holds on it. So nothing may open a lock file except takeFileLock; another open and close in the same process, even a read, would free the lock while it is held.

Keep this object for as long as the lock is held: the lock lives in the SQLite database it holds, and garbage collection of that database would close it and free the lock. Releases the lock; call it once. SQLite's result code when another connection holds a lock it needs. Takes the exclusive lock of `path`, waiting up to `waitMs` (blocking) for a holder to let go; `undefined` when another connection, in this process or another, still holds it. The write that takes the exclusive lock for good.

cards.summary: Stale `index.lock` cleanup (architecture §13, file locks). git creates `index.lock` in the git folder while it writes the index and deletes it when done; a git that is killed (at its deadline, or with its tree) leaves it behind, and every later git command that writes the index then fails with "Unable to create '…/index.lock': File exists". Run this only for a worktree no git command of this Foedrum is running in; the age guards against another one. A caller that knows by a lock of its own that no git writes the index (the state worktree under its writer lock, ADR 0107) passes `maxAgeMs: -Infinity` instead of relying on the age, and removes the other lock files a killed git leaves there with removeStaleLock (#306).

A lock at least this old is stale; default 60 s. Removes `<gitDir>/index.lock` when it is older than maxAgeMs, through removeTree. Removes the lock file at `lock` (git's `<file>.lock` beside the file it writes) when it is older than maxAgeMs, through removeTree.

cards.summary: Holding a process and everything it starts in a kill-on-close Job Object on Windows (#92, ADR 0039), through a PowerShell helper started by its full path: job-object.ps1. Node has no way to create a job itself, and its own job lets grandchildren break away.
cards.comments: Holding a process and everything it starts in a kill-on-close Job Object on Windows (#92, ADR 0039), through a PowerShell helper started by its full path: job-object.ps1. Node has no way to create a job itself, and its own job lets grandchildren break away. The exit code of the helper when it could not start the program inside a job. The line the helper writes, alone on stdout, when it could not start the program in a job. One argument quoted as Windows programs read their command line (CommandLineToArgvW). node's own quoting (libuv's quote_cmd_arg): backslashes double only before a quote and at the end, where the closing quote follows them. An environment as the block CreateProcessW takes with CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT: name=value entries sorted by name without regard to case, each ended by NUL, and one more NUL. As node's spawn on Windows: of names that differ only in case, the first in sorted order. What the helper passes to CreateProcess: the file it starts, and its whole command line. cards.summary: Robust removal of files and folders (architecture §13, file locks). On Windows a folder can carry the ReadOnly attribute and a file can be held open briefly by another process (an editor, an antivirus scan, a process whose working directory is inside the folder), so a plain delete fails with EPERM, EBUSY or ENOTEMPTY. removeTree clears the read-only bits and retries those errors with a short exponential backoff before giving up.
cards.comments: Robust removal of files and folders (architecture §13, file locks). On Windows a folder can carry the ReadOnly attribute and a file can be held open briefly by another process (an editor, an antivirus scan, a process whose working directory is inside the folder), so a plain delete fails with EPERM, EBUSY or ENOTEMPTY. removeTree clears the read-only bits and retries those errors with a short exponential backoff before giving up. Adds the owner's write bit (and, for folders, read and search) to the path and everything below it. On Windows, Node maps the write bit to the ReadOnly attribute. Symbolic links are left alone, so nothing outside the tree changes.

cards.summary: Replacing a file by renaming another over it (architecture §13, file locks). On Windows the rename fails with EPERM, EBUSY or EACCES while another process (an antivirus scan, the search indexer, an editor) has the target open; replaceFile retries those with a short backoff.

Letters and digits in any script, and punctuation that is literal inside double quotes. Not " % ! ^ (special there too), line breaks, or anything a path or a flag does not need. Throws when a part has a character outside letters, digits, space and `_ - . , : = / \ @ + ~ ' ( )`.

The Claude Code session of a brewer's attempt, so any action can resume the right session (ADR 0019): the id the driver chose before claude started, and the worktree it runs in (ADR 0116). `resumes`: the session it continues; `fallback`: why it started a new session where its brewer would have resumed one (ADR 0117). What claude reported in its init event: its version and the model it ran, for diagnosis (ADR 0116). A run that ended before the init has none. The worktree an attempt was given (ADR 0029): in which repository, where, on which branch and at which commit, so it survives restarts and a resumed attempt can get it back (ADR 0019). The path and branch say where it was and nothing acts on them: `recreate` builds both from the attempt again and takes only the commit (ADR 0037). The issue of an order or sub-order: an issue in the Brewery, or a claimed issue of the target repository `repo`, whose order is a Brewery issue (ADR 0043, ADR 0144). The route back that scheduled an attempt (ADR 0064): from the step whose check failed (`onFail`) or whose brewer was blocked by findings (`onBlocked`), or from the openPullRequest step whose pull request failed its checks on `head` (`onPullRequestFail`, ADR 0219), or on its merged tree with the base at `tip` (`cause: 'merged_check'`, ADR 0226), or conflicts with the base at `tip` (`cause: 'conflict'`, ADR 0244). A sub-order writes in exactly one repository (architecture §3.2). `subOrder` waits for `blockedBy`'s branch (`code`) or for its release (`release`). The most command prefixes a receipt keeps of one denied tool family (ADR 0172). A denied command's first one or two words: never its arguments, which are model output. claude's list price, which an event from before ADR 0181 holds: read, and dropped. What an attempt took, from its stream (ADR 0172), never its cost (ADR 0181); its tokens are on `usage`. Whether claude's `result` event was read. The run resumed its session: its API duration and tokens per model are then the session's so far, not the run's alone (ADR 0042). File tool calls that came back without an error. Tool results that came back as an error, denied calls apart. Per tool family, in the order each was first denied. A named check, or none for a Brewery's literal command or the repository's setup, which says so (ADR 0140); the command line as it ran; and where no sandbox held it, that it ran unsandboxed: a check or a setup on native Windows (ADR 0076, ADR 0158). What one check of a check step did (ADR 0069). The repository has no such check (null in foedrum.jsonc): skipped, never guessed (ADR 0023). The process runner killed its tree: the step's deadline, a stop, or too much output. A signal the runner did not send ended it: a crash, an abort, the OOM killer. It could not start; the tail says why. The longest reason a base check records for checks that did not run (ADR 0203). The most open findings a Stuck reason keeps of a findings route that ran out (ADR 0192). The most of a kept finding's file or `why`: what the status comment reads of it (ADR 0088). An open finding of the last round, its texts cut to `MAX_OPEN_FINDING_TEXT` (ADR 0192). A findings route that used its rounds (ADR 0192): how many it used, the first open findings of its last round, and how many more there were. The most findings `step.finished` keeps of an attempt blocked by findings: one per disposition. The findings of an attempt blocked by findings, a blocking Taster's `changes` (ADR 0221): the first of them, cut as a Stuck reason's open findings are, and how many more there were. Only when a findings route ran out of rounds; an older Foedrum cannot read it (ADR 0192). No file write or commit since `lastProgressAt`, for `turnsWithoutProgress` turns (ADR 0027). An Ordered batch that nothing routed by its routing deadline (ADR 0032). The openPullRequest step `stepId`'s pull request failed its checks on `head` with its onPullRequestFail rounds used: the first failed checks

cards.summary: What Foedrum reads of GitHub's answers: only the fields it uses, checked, since they come from outside the process (ADR 0033). Unknown fields are ignored; GitHub adds them freely.
cards.comments: What Foedrum reads of GitHub's answers: only the fields it uses, checked, since they come from outside the process (ADR 0033). Unknown fields are ignored; GitHub adds them freely. `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits` and `GET .../git/commits/{sha}`. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/{ref}`: one ref, never the list a partial name gives. One page of a REST list: its items are checked by whoever reads them. One page of a REST list GitHub wraps in an object, such as `{ check_runs: [...] }`. A REST error's body. GitHub's 422 answer, with a code for each thing it refused (`already_exists`, `invalid`). The GraphQL answer to `repository(owner, name) { id }`. One item of `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`, or `GET .../issues/{n}`. null for an account that was deleted since. Present when the item is a pull request: GitHub lists them among the issues. The order's title, which a pull request takes (ADR 0071). The order's text; null when the issue has none. One item of the intake's listing: with its creation time, its arrival in the queue (ADR 0208). `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}`. The commit its merge made, which a release must hold (ADR 0223). Its description, null when it has none (ADR 0227). `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest`: its tag and when it was published (ADR 0223). A commit's date, as GraphQL gives a tag's target (ADR 0223). The newest tag by its commit's date, as `GraphQL refs(refPrefix: "refs/tags/")` gives it. A lightweight tag's target is its commit, an annotated tag's is a tag of one; a tag of a tree or a blob has neither. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits/{sha}`: when it was committed (ADR 0223). `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}`: how head stands to base (ADR 0223). The head of `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}` (ADR 0213). One item of `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` (ADR 0213). For a check run of GitHub Actions, the id of its job, whose log can be read (ADR 0228). One item of the `statuses` of `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/status` (ADR 0213). One item of `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`, or the answer to `POST` there (ADR 0071). null for an account that was deleted since. `repo` is null when the head's repository was deleted. GitHub's 422 answer with the errors it found in a request, each with its message. One item of `GET .../issues/{n}/comments`, or the answer to `POST` there. null for an account that was deleted since. The comment's GraphQL id, which `minimizeComment` takes (ADR 0229). GraphQL's answer to whether a comment is hidden (ADR 0229). GraphQL's answer to `minimizeComment` (ADR 0229). `GET /user`: the account gh is logged in as (ADR 0073). A repository, as far as `foedrum init` reads it (ADR 0199). A file's contents, base64 up to GitHub's 1 MB; a larger file comes with `encoding: none`.

cards.summary: House-yeast rule frontmatter: one learned rule per file (ADR 0018).
cards.comments: House-yeast rule frontmatter: one learned rule per file (ADR 0018). The repository is not part of the scope: it follows from where the rule is stored. A lens by its name, in either folder, or by its folder and name (ADR 0143, ADR 0169). A lesson seen once in a review of Foedrum's own pull requests, one line of the main checkout's .foedrum/house-yeast-candidates.jsonl until the state branch carries candidates (ADR 0122). The house-yeast rules an attempt was given, by id, those the budget cut, and the rule files left out as invalid, by path: recorded on its step.finished (ADR 0169).

cards.summary: Ids that become path segments on the state branch: batch and step ids (ADR 0024).
cards.comments: Ids that become path segments on the state branch: batch and step ids (ADR 0024). Lower case, so two ids never share a folder on a case-insensitive file system; a letter or digit at both ends, so no `.`, `..`, hidden or trailing-dot names (Windows drops a trailing dot); and no name Windows reserves for a device, with or without an extension. One regex, so the generated JSON Schema checks exactly what zod checks. A batch or step id: one path segment on every operating system, at most 64 characters. A lens by its folder and file name (ADR 0143): `diff/<name>` reviews a diff, `plan/<name>` a plan, as `lenses/diff/<name>.md` and `lenses/plan/<name>.md` hold them. The short name of a target repository in the Brewery's config, the start of the batch ids of its claimed issues (`<alias>-<issue>`, ADR 0050): a lower-case letter, then letters and digits, at most 20 in all. It starts with a letter, so it never begins a Brewery issue's `<issue>-<n>`, and has no hyphen, so the issue that follows it is never ambiguous.

cards.summary: JSON Schema files generated from the zod schemas, for editors and other tools (ADR 0007).
cards.comments: JSON Schema files generated from the zod schemas, for editors and other tools (ADR 0007). Writes one file per schema into `dir`; the same schemas always give the same bytes. The input form: what a person or model writes, so fields with a default are optional.

cards.summary: What a lane label revision records in the ledger (ADR 0154): the label it left on the issue, or null when it took the lane labels off.
cards.comments: What a lane label revision records in the ledger (ADR 0154): the label it left on the issue, or null when it took the lane labels off. The labels of the lanes, in the order a batch moves through them.

cards.summary: .foedrum/local.jsonc: what one machine says about a Brewery, git-ignored next to its event store (ADR 0063).
cards.comments: .foedrum/local.jsonc: what one machine says about a Brewery, git-ignored next to its event store (ADR 0063). A path on this machine, absolute, so it does not depend on the folder serve runs in: on Windows with a drive or a UNC share, since `\\work` lies on the drive serve runs on.

cards.summary: models.jsonc: model aliases and per-brewer overrides (brewers-and-recipes §5).
cards.comments: models.jsonc: model aliases and per-brewer overrides (brewers-and-recipes §5). A name brewers use for a model, so evaluations can swap the model behind it. Passed to `claude --model`, which on Windows runs through a shell: no spaces, quotes or operators, and no leading dash that could read as an option. The fields of a models.jsonc, without the check that its `brewers` name an alias of its own `models`: a Brewery's file may name an alias of Foedrum's defaults, so serve checks it on the merged models (ADR 0153).

cards.summary: Out-doc frontmatter: how a brewer reports its outcome (brewers-and-recipes §2, ADR 0005).
cards.comments: Out-doc frontmatter: how a brewer reports its outcome (brewers-and-recipes §2, ADR 0005). The most dispositions an out doc lists, and the longest file and `why` of one (ADR 0191). What the brewer a findings route brought back did with one finding of its route input (ADR 0191), at the finding's place as the Taster wrote it, or the change as a whole without a file: fixed, or with a `why`, dismissed as not a defect or left as there before the change (ADR 0094), a `why` that names the evidence a later round checks (ADR 0204). Optional, so an out doc without them reads as before; an older Foedrum cannot read one with them (ADR 0191). `questions` only with needs_input and `blockerKind` only with blocked: strict objects reject them elsewhere. The out-doc frontmatter with a brewer's own fields (for example a review verdict) added to every status. Reads an out doc; a syntax error or a frontmatter that breaks `schema` makes it invalid, with the reason. The name of a Taster's out doc schema (`output.schema`): what makes a brewer a Taster (ADR 0161). A Taster's verdict: `changes` holds a blocking step up (ADR 0161). One finding of a Taster (ADR 0161): where, how bad, and why; `introduced` is false for a defect that was there before the change (ADR 0094). A finding about the change as a whole has no file. Optional, so a one-lens out doc reads as before; an older Foedrum cannot read a finding with it (ADR 0220, as ADR 0191 records for dispositions). The most items a Taster's `riskLeft` lists, and the longest one (ADR 0214). One line of at most `max` characters. A Taster's out doc: the contract's, with its findings, a verdict when it is done, and the risk its review leaves (ADR 0214), optional, so an out doc without it reads as before. The verdict follows from the findings, so the engine, not the model, decides what holds a blocking step up (ADR 0161). The out doc of a Taster's step that reviews through `lenses` (ADR 0220): on a step of several together, each finding names the lens it was found through, one of the step's; on a one-lens step, a finding that names one names the step's, so no Taster labels its findings with lenses it was not given. The lens a finding was found through: its own, or else its step's (ADR 0220). A finding's lens before the rest of its line, when it names one (ADR 0220). What a Taster reported in the out doc of an attempt that succeeded. The risk left after its review and what it could not verify (ADR 0214); none when empty. The verdict and findings of an attempt's `output` when a Taster wrote it (ADR 0161), with its risk left when it wrote any (ADR 0214); undefined for any other brewer's out doc, and for a check's success, which has none. Where a finding or a disposition is: its file and line, or the change as a whole (ADR 0191). Any out doc's dispositions, read leniently: none when it lists none, or none it can read. The dispositions of any out doc's output that lists them (ADR 0191); none for one without. The assumptions of an out doc that succeeded, beside whatever else it holds (a brewer's own fields): what the status comment shows (ADR 0072). The name of the out doc schema of a brewer that writes the pull request's sections (`output.schema`, ADR 0167): the default Cellarman's. The longest How it works and See it, the most before/after rows, and their longest value. One row of the pull request's before/after table (ADR 0167). The pull request's sections a brewer wrote (ADR 0167): model text, untrusted. The out doc of a brewer whose schema is `pullRequest`: the contract's, with the sections. They are optional, since a retry for a missing one would redo the whole run; the limits keep the body within GitHub's without cutting its Markdown. The sections of an attempt's `output` when a `pullRequest` brewer wrote any and was done; undefined for any other out doc. The name of the out doc schema of a brewer that simplifies a batch's change (`output.schema`, ADR 0166): the default Finer's. The most changes a Finer lists, the longest file of one, and the longest line of why it changed nothing. One change a Finer made (ADR 0166): where, and why; `line` when it is about one. What a Finer reported: its changes, or why there was nothing to simplify (ADR 0166). The out doc of a brewer whose schema is `fining`: the contract's, with its changes. A `done` lists them, or says why there was nothing to simplify, never both: the engine reads which, to take a done without a commit (ADR 0166). The changes of an attempt's `output` when a Finer wrote it and was done; else undefined. The name of the Gauger's out doc schema (`output.schema`, ADR 0170): the default Gauger's. The most names a Gauger gives in each list, and the longest name: the red proof's (ADR 0170). The out doc of a brewer whose schema is `gauge`: the contract's, with its new tests and its regression tests, by the names the runner reports (ADR 0170). The tests a Gauger named (ADR 0170), by the names the runner reports: model text, untrusted. Any out doc's lists of tests, read leniently: a Brewery's own brewer may name them too. The tests of an attempt's `output` when it names any; undefined for an out doc without them, and for a check's success, which has none.

cards.summary: The plan out doc (ADR 0233): an order broken into sub-orders, one repository each, with what each touches, how they depend on each other, and the recipe each should run with.
cards.comments: The plan out doc (ADR 0233): an order broken into sub-orders, one repository each, with what each touches, how they depend on each other, and the recipe each should run with. The name of a plan's out doc schema (`output.schema`, ADR 0233). The most paths one sub-order touches, and the most other cuts a plan lists. The longest sub-order title, the longest of every other line of a plan, and the longest path. One line, so the plan comment stays within GitHub's length. A sub-order's name in its plan: dependencies and the graph name it, since no issue exists yet. A path a sub-order expects to change, `new` when it does not exist yet. A sub-order of the plan waits for another's code or for its release, as `Dependency` does. One sub-order of a plan (ADR 0233). An estimate, with no cap: the sizing lens and the gate judge it (#587, #588). Off only with a reason (#219); left out, the recipe's own holds. Other cuts considered, each with why not, and why this one. A plan's out doc: the contract's, with its sub-orders and alternatives on every status, so a `needs_input` plan reads without them; a `done` needs its sub-orders (ADR 0233). A NUL is in no id, so no two pairs share a key. What a plan's out doc holds once it is done. The plan of an attempt's `output` when a `plan` brewer wrote it and was done; else undefined.

cards.summary: Building blocks shared by the recipe, brewer and configuration schemas.
cards.comments: Building blocks shared by the recipe, brewer and configuration schemas. A wall-clock limit: a positive whole number of seconds, minutes, hours or days ("30m"). A `Duration` ("30m") in milliseconds. `con` → `[cC][oO][nN]`: the generated JSON Schema keeps a pattern but not its flags. A file name every OS can create as written: none of the characters Windows reserves (`\` and `:` also rule out drive letters and alternate data streams), no line breaks, no trailing dot or space (Windows drops them, which also rules out `.` and `..`), and no device name. Control characters (NUL included) are invalid in Windows file names, and NUL everywhere. A path inside the worktree: relative, with forward slashes, never leaving it. The abstract checks recipes name; each repository maps them to commands (ADR 0023). A command with optional per-OS overrides, run through the platform shell (architecture §13). A Claude Code permission rule: a tool name, optionally with a specifier (`Bash(git diff*)`). Claude Code checks file permissions against Read(path) and Edit(path) rules only: Edit rules cover every tool that edits files, and Read rules, best-effort, Grep and Glob. It never consults a path rule for Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit or Glob (ADR 0093). Why Claude Code would never consult a path rule, naming the rule to write instead. A deny rule of a brewer or an attempt: never a path rule Claude Code would not consult. An allowlist entry: never AskUserQuestion, which is always denied (ADR 0006). A rule a brewer's attempt may allow: never one that reaches git with no fixed subcommand. claude matches a deny rule against the command as written, so `git -C . push` gets past `Bash(git push *)`; a push is denied only when no allow rule matches it (ADR 0062). A rule of the permission ceiling or of a repository's tools: never one that names gh. These are not allowlists, so a broad rule such as `Bash(*)` stays; what reaches an attempt is checked by `BrewerAllowedTool` (ADR 0082). git subcommands that update a remote, and `submodule` (`submodule foreach` runs a command). Not complete: a subcommand that runs a command from its own line (`rebase -x`, `fetch --upload-pack`) is out of this check's reach, as is any such program (ADR 0062). Common programs that run the rest of their command line as a command (Windows extensions dropped); a known list, not a complete one (ADR 0062). The package managers read by their subcommand, each with whether a subcommand is a runner: it runs the rest of the line as a command, as `npx` does (ADR 0165). npm resolves any start of `exec` or `explore`. The others read any other subcommand as the program word of the rest. A program word without quotes, call operators, assignments or variables: a name or a path. The extensions Windows runs a program by (PATHEXT): `git.cmd` is git too. PowerShell runs `.ps1`. git or gh after a wrapper, also through a PowerShell shim, which a wrapper may start. A package manager's subcommand: no option, quote, star or escape. What follows a program can be read as written only in plain characters: anything else may be a quote, an escape or an expansion of the shell a wrapper starts (`env g""h`, `env /usr/bin/g?`, `cmd /c g^h`, `bash -c g\h` run gh), so it fails closed (review of #225). What a rule lets a shell run, read from its program word: not a shell rule (`none`); any program (`any`: a whole shell, a star in or right after the program word, a program word with a quote, `&`, `$` or an assignment, or in Bash a backslash, which quotes there); or a program by its name, without its path and Windows extension, with what follows it up to the first star, and whether that can be read as written. `any` keeps the name of a plain program word with a star right after it (`gh*`). Lower case, since PowerShell matches without case; `:*` is the older spelling of ` *`. A program word with what follows it up to the first star. A package manager is read by its subcommand (ADR 0165): a runner is read as `npx`; for pnpm, yarn, bun and corepack, any other subcommand is the program word of the rest; an option, a star or an unreadable word in its place is any program. Whether a shell rule may match git with no fixed subcommand, failing closed on the program word: any program (`shellProgramOf`); a wrapper with a star, with what follows it unreadable, or with git after it; git's own `git-<name>` programs with a star, or one that pushes; or git, by name or path, with an option, a quote or a star where the subcommand would be, or with a subcommand that pushes or that a star could make into one. Whether a shell rule names gh: gh by name or path, or a wrapper with gh after it (ADR 0082). Whether a shell rule may start gh, failing closed as `reachesAnyGitCommand` does: any program, a rule that names gh with any arguments, a wrapper with a star or with what follows it unreadable, or git asking its credential helper for the login (ADR 0082). Whether a git rule may ask git's credential helper, which on a Brewery is `gh auth git-credential` (ADR 0073), for the login: `git credential`, `git credential-<helper>`, `git-credential-<helper>`, or a star that could make the subcommand into one (`git c*`). Tools whose specifier is a command (Claude Code splits it on shell operators) or a path (gitignore-style, where `*` stays within one folder and `**` crosses folders). Operators, substitutions, redirections, and the grouping PowerShell evaluates as a command (`(…)`, `{…}`); a star fails closed on all of them. Claude Code reads `//path` as absolute, `/path` from the settings file, `~/path` from home. Whether a specifier may reach outside what a glob of the ceiling seems to cover. Whether an allowlist entry stays within the ceiling, failing closed: a ceiling rule covers the same tool when it has no specifier, when its specifier is the entry's, or when its specifier, read as a glob, matches the entry's specifier as written. A star never stands for a shell operator in a command rule, a single star never st

cards.summary: Reading JSONC files and Markdown files with frontmatter against a schema (ADR 0020).
cards.comments: Reading JSONC files and Markdown files with frontmatter against a schema (ADR 0020). Reads a JSONC file such as foedrum.jsonc; a syntax error or a broken schema gives the reason. Reads a Markdown file with frontmatter, such as a brewer or a house-yeast rule. ParseError, or JSON.parse's own SyntaxError when the reader cannot locate the error.

cards.summary: The recipe choice out doc (ADR 0232): the question of a step that chooses the batch's recipe, whose options are among the Brewery's recipes it may offer. Built per step from those names, as a Taster's is from its lenses (ADR 0220).
cards.comments: The recipe choice out doc (ADR 0232): the question of a step that chooses the batch's recipe, whose options are among the Brewery's recipes it may offer. Built per step from those names, as a Taster's is from its lenses (ADR 0220). The name of a recipe choice's out doc schema (`output.schema`, ADR 0232). The out doc of a step that chooses among `choices` (ADR 0232): `needs_input` with one question whose options are among them, or `blocked` or `failed` as for any brewer; never `done`, since only a person's answer chooses.

cards.summary: Recipes: brewers, checks and actions in order, with loops (brewers-and-recipes §3).
cards.comments: Recipes: brewers, checks and actions in order, with loops (brewers-and-recipes §3). A step id: a file name on the state branch (ADR 0024); `recipe` names the recipe's settings. `<step>.<field>`, optionally compared with a quoted value: `tasting.verdict != 'approve'`. An expression's parts: what it reads, and the value it compares that with, if any. The step it reads, or `recipe` for the recipe's settings. The parts of an expression the schema accepted, or `undefined` for any other text. Back to an earlier step, at most `maxRounds` times; after that the batch becomes Stuck. The longest prompt of an interactive step, in UTF-16 units: about 4 KiB (ADR 0222). Only findings are routed: an environment or divergence blocker always makes the batch Stuck. A named check, or in a Brewery's own recipe a literal command (ADR 0023). A red proof reads the structured test report, so it only runs the `test` check (ADR 0017). Whether `input` is a step of ADR 0019's `session` kind, which ADR 0222 removed. The kind of a step: the one field that says what it does. The step's id; a brewer step defaults to its brewer, an action to its name in kebab case. The brewer a step runs: a brewer step's own; none for other steps. Every step with its path in the recipe, nested loop and parallel steps included. How a step refers to another: reads its result, goes back to it, or proves its tests red. The step ids a step refers to, with the path of each reference within the step. Where a step is: its position in walk order and the path of the list that holds it. Why a reference from `from` to `to` is not allowed, or undefined when it is. Gone (ADR 0194, ADR 0253): refused by name, so a recipe that still has one says why. No default here: ADR 0017 defaults it to true for recipes that write code, which depends on the brewers the recipe uses, so the loader decides when it is absent. A recipe: step ids are unique, every goto, red proof and expression names a step, only the openPullRequest action has an onPullRequestFail route, a route goes back to an earlier step at the same level or in an enclosing loop, and a red proof reads an earlier step's tests. A brewer named recipe, without an id of its own (StepId already rejects an explicit one). The pull request the route is for is the one the openPullRequest action opens (ADR 0219). A recipe Foedrum ships: language-independent, so its checks are names only (ADR 0023).

cards.summary: What a revision of a status comment records in the ledger (ADR 0072): the comment it made or edited, and the digest of the text it showed. Never the text: the ledger is kept for good. And what a merge brief records (ADR 0225): its comment and the record of the checks it was posted for.
cards.comments: What a revision of a status comment records in the ledger (ADR 0072): the comment it made or edited, and the digest of the text it showed. Never the text: the ledger is kept for good. And what a merge brief records (ADR 0225): its comment and the record of the checks it was posted for. The first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256. The first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the text. A merge brief posted on a pull request (ADR 0225): its comment, and the record it was posted for, the pull request, its head and the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the record's checks. A merge brief hidden as outdated (ADR 0229): its comment, hidden as GitHub's `OUTDATED`, or gone when it was not there to hide.

cards.summary: Step outcome, the single contract every step ends with (architecture §4.2, ADR 0005).
cards.comments: Step outcome, the single contract every step ends with (architecture §4.2, ADR 0005). A question a brewer cannot answer itself (ADR 0006): options, a recommendation, why it blocks. JSON, because outcomes are stored in the event log. The run went past its turn budget, and its retry resumes its session (ADR 0175). The run's commits hold what the push's secret scan would refuse: its retry is told why (ADR 0187).

cards.summary: The event store's own records: effect keys (invariant I4), leases (ADR 0002), the state branch's pushed-through marker (ADR 0024), and the commit sha they and the events share.
cards.comments: The event store's own records: effect keys (invariant I4), leases (ADR 0002), the state branch's pushed-through marker (ADR 0024), and the commit sha they and the events share. The key of an effect of an attempt. The key of an effect of a batch rather than one of its attempts (ADR 0043). The key of an external side effect: applied at most once (invariant I4). The parts of an effect key in the order of its text: an attempt's four, or a batch's two. The parts of an attempt key, the `attemptKey` of a lease, in the order of its text (ADR 0027). The shape of a canonical text, so the generated JSON Schema rejects most other texts too; the refinement is the exact check. Every canonical text matches its shape. Text written exactly as `JSON.stringify` writes valid `parts`, so each key has one text only. One key, one text: otherwise two spellings of a key would both pass the UNIQUE index. The canonical text of an effect key: the JSON array `[batchId, stepId, attempt, effect]`, or `[batchId, effect]` for an effect of a batch (ADR 0043), so no part can collide with a separator, written exactly as `JSON.stringify` writes it. The canonical text of an attempt key, the `attemptKey` of a lease: the JSON array `[batchId, stepId, attempt]`, the only text the supervisor can match to an attempt (ADR 0027). A full commit id: 40 lowercase hex characters, a SHA-1 id. Foedrum supports SHA-1 repositories (ADR 0254); a 64-character SHA-256 id is refused where it enters. A full commit id as a pattern, which the scans for ids in other text build on too. Whether `text` is a full commit id, the one check `CommitSha` and every git reader use. Why `text` is no full commit id: a SHA-256 one is named as not supported (ADR 0254), any other gets `otherwise`. A full commit id (ADR 0254). The most findings the ledger keeps of one refused push (ADR 0079). What the secret scan found in a batch's commits (ADR 0079): the commit, the place (the file's path as git shows it, `message`, or why neither can be named) and the kind, never the text. The most sensitive files the ledger names of one push (ADR 0201). The files of a batch's change that match its repository's sensitive paths (ADR 0201): how many, and the first `MAX_SENSITIVE` of them as git named them. The result the ledger keeps for the push of the openPullRequest action (ADR 0071): the branch, the commit pushed, the revision it was resolved from, and whether the base already holds every commit of it, so nothing was pushed; or what the secret scan found, so nothing was pushed either (ADR 0079): each commit, place and kind, never the text. A push that went keeps the sensitive files its change touches, when there are any (ADR 0201). A later round's push that found the branch at another commit than the round before pushed (`moved`), or gone (`gone`), pushed nothing (ADR 0219). The result the ledger keeps for a later round's body of the openPullRequest action (ADR 0227): the digest of the body it wrote, the first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256, or why it left the body as it was: a person or a bot edited it, or it carries no marker of the batch. The most files the ledger names of one merge of the base that conflicts (ADR 0164). A file a merge left unmerged, as `git status` names it (ADR 0244): its status, and whether it holds no conflict marker, as a binary file or one a side deleted does not. The result the ledger keeps for the merge of the base into a batch's last check attempt before its pull request (ADR 0164): the base's commit as fetched, and the merge commit made, or the files the merge conflicts in, so it was aborted; neither when the base had nothing new. A merge at the start of a routed fix keeps its conflicts in progress for the brewer (`kept`, ADR 0244): the files still unmerged, at most `MAX_CONFLICTS`, and how many more. How far the state branch has the log (ADR 0024): every event up to `eventId` is on the remote branch, in `commit`. Kept in the store, never in the log, so it has no JSON Schema file. Which driver drives a batch until when (ADR 0019): alive while `expiresAt` is in the future. The owner is the driver's lock owner (ADR 0037). Kept in the store's batch leases table, never in the log, so it has no JSON Schema file. Who holds an attempt (and its session) until when; alive while `expiresAt` is in the future. Kept in the store's leases table, never in the log, so it has no JSON Schema file. The text of an attempt's out doc, kept in the store from the attempt's end until a flush puts it on the state branch at `outDocPath` (ADR 0103). Model output: stored, never followed. Kept in the store's out docs table, never in the log, so it has no JSON Schema file.

Why `since` or `branch` must not reach git, or nothing when both may. Scans the commits on `branch` in `clone` after `since` as the push does (ADR 0079, ADR 0187); never throws, git's failure is `unscanned`. The push's own scan, in the clone, with git reading the objects as committed (ADR 0079).

cards.summary: The attempt worktree manager's shell (ADR 0012, ADR 0029): gathers facts from git and the attempts root, and carries out what attempt-worktrees.ts decides. Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021).
cards.comments: The attempt worktree manager's shell (ADR 0012, ADR 0029): gathers facts from git and the attempts root, and carries out what attempt-worktrees.ts decides. Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021). Foedrum's work root, outside the Brewery checkout (default `~/.foedrum/<brewery>/`). `owner/name` of the repository the attempts write in. The repository the worktrees are added to: the user's clone (`source: local`) or the managed clone (`source: managed`, from `ensureManagedClone`). The clone's remote the fetch reaches; default `origin`. The remote as Foedrum names it: its `root` is where the base fetch makes its git directories, which the cleanup clears of what a stopped call left (ADR 0130, ADR 0137). The clock for the age of a stale index.lock. An attempt's worktree: where it is, its branch, and the commit it was at when made. One line per item: what a cleanup removed, kept (with the reason) and could not remove. The folder the repository's attempt worktrees live in. Fetches, then gives a new attempt its worktree on its own branch at `base` (a commit or a ref such as `origin/main`). Call it only for an attempt whose lease the caller holds and that has not started. Throws when something of the attempt is in the way. Gives a resumed attempt its worktree back (ADR 0019): the one that is there, or a new one on its branch, or at `commit` when the branch is gone. Throws when that cannot be done. Fetches the clone's remote, one fetch at a time with `create`'s: a plan's check reads a base the clone has no ref of yet (ADR 0233). Throws when the fetch fails. Removes the worktrees, folders and local branches that nothing claims, stale index.lock files of kept worktrees no attempt runs in, and the git directories of its own that a stopped call left over an hour ago (ADR 0130). At engine start without `batchId` (crash repair); with it, when that batch has ended. A fetch of a large repository takes a while, and so does a checkout from a partial clone, which downloads every file then; a stalled one must still end. The first clone of a large repository takes longer still. The output of a git call that must succeed. `worktree list` or `worktree add`, not just `worktree`. The folders below the attempts root: `<stepId>/<attempt>` per batch, and whatever is not a step folder as it is. Removes a folder and the empty folders below it; false, removing nothing more, when anything else is in it. Retried like any removal while Windows still holds the folder; gone already is fine. The file system calls the cleanup of the git directories makes; injected by tests. Removes the git directories of its own that a stopped call left in `root` (ADR 0130). Only a candidate is read: nothing else in the root is touched, not even by an lstat. Gone since the listing, as a running call removes its own, or still going on Windows, whose delete-pending entry fails with EPERM: nothing left to judge. No hook or fsmonitor of the clone's runs in the engine's git (ADR 0137). git lists worktrees by their real path, so the attempts root is compared through links (a work root on a linked folder, macOS /var for /private/var). Whether the folder's .git file names its record. A brewer can rewrite that file, and git run there would read the repository it names, core.fsmonitor and all. The state of a worktree folder, with git run against its record only, never by discovery from inside the folder. With `outDoc`, that untracked file alone still counts as clean, and is named (ADR 0081). One fetch at a time: concurrent fetches in one clone fail on git's ref locks. With `--prune`, a branch the remote deleted and made again as a folder never stops it (review of #266). No maintenance that would outlive the call, and no submodule's remote (review of #370). Carries out one action; the line it reports, if any. Only while it still points where the facts saw it; its config section goes too. A recorded commit comes from the state branch: never let it pass as an option. The out doc of the attempt's step, which every attempt that ran here wrote (ADR 0081). A worktree's branch is deleted only once the worktree is gone. Where to clone from. A local clone to borrow objects from (`--reference`). The rename that moves the finished clone into place; default the file system's. A URL as it may be shown: without a user name or password, which may be a token. The clone a repository's attempt worktrees are added to: the user's, or the managed one. serveSetup refuses it before anything opens; never git in the working directory instead (#202). The repository's managed clone (`source: managed`, ADR 0012): a bare partial clone in the work root, made once. Returns its path. Cloned next to its place and renamed when done, so a crash never leaves half a clone there. Credentials in the URL would be in the process list and in the clone's config; a credential helper provides them instead. A bare clone fetches into nothing by default; into origin/* like any clone, so a fetch never moves Foedrum's own branches. Retried while Windows still holds a file the clone just wrote.

cards.summary: Decides where an attempt's worktree lives, whether it can be created or recreated, and what a cleanup removes (ADR 0012, ADR 0029). Pure: attempt-worktrees-git.ts gathers the facts from git and carries the decisions out (ADR 0021).
cards.comments: Decides where an attempt's worktree lives, whether it can be created or recreated, and what a cleanup removes (ADR 0012, ADR 0029). Pure: attempt-worktrees-git.ts gathers the facts from git and carries the decisions out (ADR 0021). One attempt of a step of a batch; the same shape as the engine's `AttemptRef`. The folder of a repository under the work root: `<owner>.<name>`, lower case. The owner has no dot, so the first one separates the two. Where the managed clone of `repo` is in the work root (ADR 0012). Where each base fetch of `repo` makes a git directory of its own, which writes into its clone's objects and reads none of the clone's configuration (ADR 0090, ADR 0137). How old a git directory of Foedrum's own must be before a cleanup removes it: far longer than the longest call can keep one, its 300 s transfer and the minute each of its local calls may take (ADR 0130). An entry of the git directories' root. Whether it is a directory, not a file or a link. When it last changed, in ms since the epoch: never before it was made. The name `withOwnGitDir` gives a git directory: a `randomUUID`, which is lower case, and `.git`; with `.tree`, the worktree a merged-check run makes beside it (ADR 0203). Whether an entry of the root could be a git directory of Foedrum's own: the only ones read. The git directories a stopped call left that a cleanup removes (ADR 0130): `<uuid>.git` directories older than the floor. Anything else in the root stays. A path segment that is also a component of a branch name: git refuses `..` anywhere and a `.lock` ending (git check-ref-format). foedrum/state is the state branch, so no branch can be below it. The attempt of three name parts, when they are its canonical spelling. The local branch of an attempt: `foedrum/<batchId>/<stepId>/<attempt>`. The name the local branch `foedrum/<rest>` is pushed under in a target repository: `foedrum/<brewery>/<rest>`, with the Brewery as `<owner>.<name>` in lower case, so two Breweries never push the same branch (ADR 0043). The attempt whose branch this is, or undefined for any other branch. The batch of a branch in a batch's namespace, `foedrum/<batchId>/…`, attempt or not. The folder of an attempt below the attempts root, with `/` separators. The attempt whose folder this is (below the attempts root, `/` separators), or undefined. A worktree git lists for the clone. The path below the attempts root with `/` separators, or undefined outside it. `unchecked` outside the attempts root. A clean worktree's untracked out doc, its only change: deleted before it (ADR 0081). A local branch under `refs/heads/foedrum/`. A batch folder under the attempts root and the attempt folders found below it. `<stepId>/<attempt>` of every folder two levels below the batch folder. The entries of `attempts` that hold a `.git` file or folder. What the engine's state says about the worktrees: whether each batch it knows is still live (it may brew again: ordered, brewing, conditioning or Stuck) or has ended (on tap or cancelled), and which attempts hold a live lease: the leased attempt and every attempt whose session it continues, whose worktree it runs in (ADR 0029). The out doc of each step of an ended batch whose brewer is known, by `<batchId>/<stepId>`: the one untracked file a worktree of that step may have and still go (ADR 0081). The branch of each ended batch's task tree that no push recorded (for a rewind, the attempt branches that may hold its commit, ADR 0101), by name, with the commit the batch started from: the only ref to its commits, kept while it holds any (ADR 0084). The branch of the task tree of each batch on tap whose pull request is open: a fix round starts from it (ADR 0219). Whether a worktree is clean, from its `git status --porcelain`: nothing, or nothing but its untracked out doc, which is then named (ADR 0081). The out doc is one path segment (`PathSafeId`), so git names it as it is, unquoted. `branch` is deleted once the worktree is gone. A folder under the attempts root that git does not know as a worktree. A batch folder whose attempts all went; removed only when it is empty by then. Deleted only while it still points at `tip`. A kept worktree no attempt runs in: its stale index.lock goes. What a cleanup removes, from the facts of one clone and the claims. With `batchId`, only that batch's worktrees, folders and branches are looked at (the batch has ended). A worktree with a live lease is never removed (#37: the driver renews the lease, so it expires when the driver dies, even while an orphaned brewer process still runs). A batch the state does not know has no claim on the attempts root, which is Foedrum's. The task tree of an ended batch that no push recorded: its branch is the only ref to its commits while it holds any past the batch's start (ADR 0084). The task tree of a batch on tap whose pull request is open: a fix round starts there (ADR 0219). What goes: attempt folders (below the root) and branches that go with their worktree. A worktree git lists below the folder: removing the folder would take it along. Its branch goes with it, or stays with it. A record whose folder is gone holds nothing, wherever it was in the attempts root. undefined: kept without a word, as every worktree of a live batch is. The branch goes too only when its batch has ended. A batch the state does not know may have committed work nobody pushed (a store rebuilt without its last events, two Breweries on one work root): its branch stays for the branch pass to report, as does an unpushed task tree's. Folders git does not know as worktrees: a crash before git recorded one, or after it dropped the record. git lists it under another spelling of its path, or it belongs to another clone: either way removing it would skip the checks a worktree gets. Branches that no worktree in the attempts root has: the ones of ended batches go, unless a worktree elsewhere has one checked out. A batch the state does not know may be another Brewery's that shares the clo

The commit a merge in progress merges: MERGE_HEAD is there while one is. The files a merge in progress left unmerged, as `git status` names them (ADR 0244); of the first `MAX_CONFLICTS`, the ones without a conflict marker, which git could not mark. A rename's or copy's entry is followed by its original path. u <XY> <sub> <m1> <m2> <m3> <mW> <h1> <h2> <h3> <path> A file holds a marker when a line of it starts one; never a binary file (-I). A commit of its own, also when the start is behind the base, and no editor. Left in progress, with its markers, for the brewer to conclude (ADR 0244).

cards.summary: The pushes of the openPullRequest action (ADR 0071), the shell: git in the repository's clone, never in an attempt's worktree (ADR 0066), with no hook or fsmonitor (ADR 0137); the base is fetched from a git directory of its own (ADR 0090). Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021).
cards.comments: The pushes of the openPullRequest action (ADR 0071), the shell: git in the repository's clone, never in an attempt's worktree (ADR 0066), with no hook or fsmonitor (ADR 0137); the base is fetched from a git directory of its own (ADR 0090). Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021). The clone the attempt worktrees are added to: the user's, or the managed one. The clone's remote, which the push and its lookup reach, and whose `<remote>/<base>` the base fetch starts from; default `origin`. The remote as Foedrum names it, which the base fetch reaches (ADR 0090); without it, it refuses. How the secret scan runs git (ADR 0079): on the objects as committed, so that no replace ref, graft or shallow file in the clone, which every attempt worktree shares, hides a commit or changes its parents, and with no attribute file of the user's. Its flags turn off what the clone's configuration could otherwise change: diff drivers, textconv, prefixes, renames, notes, signatures and colour. A partial clone would fetch a missing object, so a word asked of cat-file would leave. A graft file at /dev/null makes git print its deprecation hint ahead of every error. No transport at all, whatever the git version: a lazy fetch fails here instead. Every header as stored, which %B leaves out: the author, the committer, a signature, an encoding. Uncoloured, unabbreviated and not re-encoded, whatever the clone's color.ui, log.abbrevCommit or i18n.logOutputEncoding say. When the headers read shows other commits than the messages read, something bent its output. How a patch prints, whatever the clone's configuration says. Every commit but a merge, by its own change. The merges, each with its parents: the engine's merge of the base (ADR 0164). Past the runner's output limit (ADR 0035), the scan reads no further and refuses. The sha after each NUL of the patches: the commit each patch is of. A push or fetch of a large repository takes a while; the effect's deadline aborts it sooner. A base branch as git reads it in a refspec: never an option, a second refspec or a range. A branch Foedrum pushes, so that nothing from outside reaches git as an option or a refspec. The patches of the commits in `range`, each commit after a NUL and its sha: every commit but a merge by its own change, and each merge against its last parent, the base it brought in (ADR 0164), so what the base added is never read as the batch's, and what the merge itself adds is. The first parents' lines are read in their own commits. `undefined` past the output limit. A git directory of the call's own, reaching the remote by the URL Foedrum names (ADR 0090). 0: an ancestor, 1: not one; anything else is git failing. The fetch runs in a git directory of its own (ADR 0090): no fetch at the same time, and nothing a fetch killed at its deadline left (a ref's lock, a ref of a commit the clone has pruned since), takes part. The clone's own origin/<base>: where the fetch starts. The ref starts at the clone's base: the fetch then brings only what the clone lacks, and git's check of what it brought stops there instead of walking a blobless clone's history to blobs it never had. Never by force, and by the commit's sha: no ref of the clone names what is pushed. No hook of the clone's runs: `--no-verify` alone would skip only pre-push. Only this one ref goes, whatever push.followTags or push.recurseSubmodules say: nothing past the ledger. A 40-character hexadecimal word is a key unless the clone has it as a commit; the commits' own hashes, after each NUL, and the headers read's commit, tree and parent lines are not read. A message's own `commit <sha>` line is asked as any other word. Each path once, a rename's two as a deletion and an addition, never quoted after -z. As committed, as the scan reads them: no replace ref or graft of a brewer's names the files.

cards.summary: Git in a clone that attempt worktrees share: the engine's calls there run with no hook or fsmonitor (ADR 0137), and the push's base fetch runs in a git directory of Foedrum's own, with the clone's objects and the URL Foedrum names (ADR 0090).
cards.comments: Git in a clone that attempt worktrees share: the engine's calls there run with no hook or fsmonitor (ADR 0137), and the push's base fetch runs in a git directory of Foedrum's own, with the clone's objects and the URL Foedrum names (ADR 0090). The repository's remote as Foedrum names it, which the base fetch reaches from git directories of Foedrum's own, never through the clone's configuration (ADR 0090, ADR 0137). `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>.git`: the repository the pull request goes into. The folder each call makes its git directory in, and removes it from after. The name of each git directory; default a random UUID. What every engine call in the clone runs with (ADR 0137): no hook of the clone's, such as reference-transaction on a ref update, which could fail the engine's own call; no fsmonitor, whose daemon would outlive it. git in the clone (ADR 0137). No hook, gc or maintenance in Foedrum's own git directory: a gc would prune the clone's objects. The URL Foedrum names as the promisor remote of its own git directory, for a partial clone: a delta of a file the clone has no copy of then resolves from that URL, never through the clone's configuration (review of #266). The signal as git's options take it. `sha` when it is a full commit sha (ADR 0254); otherwise it throws the line that says why not. The output of a git call that must succeed; git's first line of why, when it fails. The git command, after git's own options such as `--git-dir`. A git directory of Foedrum's own whose objects are the clone's. The URL Foedrum names. The directory itself. The clone's object store, which git there writes into. git in the directory; its output, or throws with git's reason. Fetches `refspec` from the URL Foedrum names, with nothing else: no tags, no FETCH_HEAD, no submodules, no maintenance. Into a partial clone it fetches blobless, with that URL as the directory's promisor remote. git in the directory, its result whatever its exit code: in a partial clone, an object the clone lacks comes from the URL Foedrum names, as the fetch's do (ADR 0198). Runs `use` with a git directory of its own, made for it in the remote's root and removed after, also when it fails (ADR 0090): git there reads that directory's configuration and hooks, never the clone's, and writes into the clone's object store (`<git-common-dir>/objects`, so the clone's alternates still count). Nothing a call killed at its deadline left is read again. git's options in the directory: the clone's objects, and its own configuration over the call's. Whether the clone is partial, asked once per directory, which is then set up as one. A partial clone as the clone's configuration says: a promisor remote, or the extension older gits write. One that says so falsely fetches no files, and one that hides it fails to fetch. The promisor remote of a partial clone's directory, for the call only. A gc there would prune every object of the clone that its own refs do not reach. git init makes the directory, but not the folder it is in.

cards.summary: Runs git for Foedrum: non-interactive, with a timeout, through an argument array (architecture §13). Code that drives git takes a `Git` so unit tests can pass a fake one (ADR 0021).
cards.comments: Runs git for Foedrum: non-interactive, with a timeout, through an argument array (architecture §13). Code that drives git takes a `Git` so unit tests can pass a fake one (ADR 0021). The exit code; `null` when git was killed, for example by the timeout or the output limit. Why the runner killed git, when it did. Kills git after this long; default 60 s. Configuration for this call only, given through the environment (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`). Kills git and every process it started when it aborts. Kills git when its output passes this many bytes; default the runner's 4 MiB (ADR 0035). Environment for this call only, after git's own: it never turns a prompt back on. Written to git's stdin, which is then closed. The environment git runs in: it never prompts, in the terminal or through Git Credential Manager's window; a missing credential makes the command fail instead. The user's ssh choice (GIT_SSH, core.sshCommand) stays: without a terminal, ssh cannot prompt either. The GitHub token variables go, so gh as git's credential helper answers with its own login (ADR 0073). core.longpaths, then the call's own configuration, after any configuration the environment already gives git: out docs on the state branch can be deeper than Windows' 260 characters (ADR 0024). Why the runner killed git, for its stderr; nothing for a stop, which the caller asked for. git through the given process runner; unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021). The call's own after git's, but never in place of what keeps git from prompting. The real git, through the platform's process runner. The timeout is a hard deadline: it kills git and every process git started (a credential helper, ssh, gpg) and answers at once, without waiting for their output to close. A git that cannot start (not installed) has no exit code either.

Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021). The checks on the merged tree get a worktree of it from such a directory (ADR 0203).
