A merge of a large tree takes a while; the intake pass's deadline aborts it sooner. The checkout of the merged tree, which in a blobless clone fetches its blobs (ADR 0203). Who makes the merged tree's commit: Foedrum, so the user's configuration need not name one. A ref of the clone's that the merged tree's directory gets: a tag or a remote-tracking ref. Whether a line of `for-each-ref` names a full commit sha (ADR 0254) and such a ref. What git's merge-tree answered: the merged tree, and the files of a conflict. 0: clean, 1: conflicts; anything else is git failing. The merged tree, then each conflicting file, each after a NUL. How `head` and `tip`, both full shas the clone has, merge. A worktree of the merged tree of `head` and `tip` for `use`, removed after (ADR 0203). Runs `use` with a worktree of the merged tree of `head` and `tip` (ADR 0203): a commit of it on both, checked out from a git directory of Foedrum's own that borrows the clone's objects and holds a copy of its tags and remote-tracking refs. Both go when `use` ends, also when it fails. The clone's tags and remote-tracking refs, so `git describe` or a log of the base reads what it reads in a check step's worktree. git in the worktree runs without the call's object directory: it borrows the clone's.

cards.summary: The paths of a plan read at a commit (ADR 0233), the shell: `git ls-tree` in the clone, which reads trees only, so a blob-less clone fetches nothing. Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021).
cards.comments: The paths of a plan read at a commit (ADR 0233), the shell: `git ls-tree` in the clone, which reads trees only, so a blob-less clone fetches nothing. Git runs only through the injected `Git`, so unit tests pass a fake one (ADR 0021). The most characters of paths one call gives git: Windows' command line holds 32,767. `paths` in runs of at most `MOST_PATH_CHARS` characters, each with at least one path. A full sha, so that nothing reaches git as an option or a revision expression. No hook or fsmonitor of the clone's runs in the engine's git (ADR 0137). The paths as written: no `*`, `?` or `[` read as a pattern. -t lists each folder on the way to a path, and the path itself when it is a folder.

cards.summary: Parses `git worktree list --porcelain -z`: NUL-terminated fields, records ended by an empty one.
cards.comments: Parses `git worktree list --porcelain -z`: NUL-terminated fields, records ended by an empty one.

cards.summary: Reads the records under .git/worktrees/ for the cores (ADR 0021): the folder each record's gitdir file names, whether that folder is still there, and its lock.
cards.comments: Reads the records under .git/worktrees/ for the cores (ADR 0021): the folder each record's gitdir file names, whether that folder is still there, and its lock. A record under .git/worktrees/. `folder` is the worktree folder its gitdir file names, or undefined when that file is missing or empty; git no longer lists such a record. A relative gitdir (worktree.useRelativePaths) is relative to the record.

cards.summary: Carries out what worktree-removal.ts decides, and gathers the folder state it decides from. Shared by the worktree cleanup and the attempt worktree manager (ADR 0021).
cards.comments: Carries out what worktree-removal.ts decides, and gathers the folder state it decides from. Shared by the worktree cleanup and the attempt worktree manager (ADR 0021). git with success as a flag, and a reason on every failure. Foedrum's git with success as a flag. A failure is printed with its reason, and git does not always give one. For a git that reads a worktree's index: no fsmonitor command and no hook runs (#263). git status of the worktree at `path`, run in `main` against `record`, its record under the clone: never by discovery from the folder, whose .git file a brewer can point at a git folder of its own, with a core.fsmonitor command in its configuration (#263, ADR 0095). Submodules are not looked into; git worktree remove refuses a worktree that has one. A gitlink would make git look into the submodule with a git found by its own .git file. The state of a worktree folder that git lists; `unchecked` when the repository at `main` has no record of it, which keeps it. A worktree's untracked out doc, its only change when git listed it (ADR 0081). A folder that took its place since stays, and git worktree remove refuses it as any other change. Removes a worktree of the repository at `main`; throws, with git's reason, when it cannot. git worktree remove runs git status in the folder, which inherits this configuration. git deletes the .git file and the record even when it fails on a busy file, and no later run would see the folder again; with the .git file still there, it refused.

cards.summary: How a worktree is removed, from the state of its folder and its record (ADR 0021): the rule the worktree cleanup and the attempt worktree manager share. worktree-removal-git.ts carries it out.
cards.comments: How a worktree is removed, from the state of its folder and its record (ADR 0021): the rule the worktree cleanup and the attempt worktree manager share. worktree-removal-git.ts carries it out. clean or dirty: the folder is a worktree; no-git: the folder is there without its .git file; gone: only the record under .git/worktrees/ is left; foreign: its .git file names another git folder than its record, so git is not run there; unchecked: never looked at. git worktree remove, then whatever a busy file left behind; `outDoc`, the worktree's only change, is deleted first (ADR 0081). A removal that stopped after deleting the .git file: the folder and the record go. Only the record is left. Why a worktree with changes stays; undefined for any other folder. How to remove a worktree that nothing else keeps, or why it cannot be removed.
